  [@Yi-111-a](https://github.com/Yi-111-a) for the additional cases from
  [#137](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/137), included through
  [#144](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/144).
- **Terminal and status details:** parse tmux window fields with printable
  separators ([#101](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/101)); distinguish
  health that was not requested from a failed read
  ([#102](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/102)); use native realpath for
  Codex hook trust ([#103](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/103)); pass
  known Claude/Codex runtime hints to Herdr
  ([#106](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/106)); report missing fresh
  startup context or adapters as needing attention
  ([#107](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/107)); accept numeric Claude
  rate-limit reset timestamps ([#108](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/108)).
  Thanks to [@dajiaohuang](https://github.com/dajiaohuang).
- **Pi input and portable checks:** retain line editing with `TERM=dumb`, and
  correct macOS path and timezone assumptions in tests. Thanks to
  [@shravansumanthanan](https://github.com/shravansumanthanan) for
  [#123](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/123).
- **Configured restore paths:** restore-check uses the configured shared-docs
  root. This does not repair every issue in
  [#130](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/130). Thanks to
  [@jbaehova](https://github.com/jbaehova) for
  [#139](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/139).
- **Anthropic gateways:** permit `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in configured provider-auth
  environment forwarding. Thanks to [@FenjuFu](https://github.com/FenjuFu) for
  [#143](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/143).
- **Terminal authentication maintenance:** reuse the shared token-comparison
  helper. Thanks to [@Sunil56224972](https://github.com/Sunil56224972) for
  [#145](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/145).

## Also in this release

- **Mixed Claude/Codex projects:** shared skills are now also placed where Codex
  looks for them, even when a matching Claude copy exists. Edited Codex skills are
  kept unless you force an overwrite. Thanks to [@a4w-h4y](https://github.com/a4w-h4y)
  for diagnosing [#159](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/159), fixed by
  [#162](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/162).
- **Slow polling no longer piles up:** identity and transcript polling no longer start
  overlapping work on every tick when a sweep runs slowly. This prevents accumulated
  overlap; it is not a measured overall CPU reduction, and polling cadence is
  unchanged. Thanks to [@korallis](https://github.com/korallis) for reporting
  [#161](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/161), addressed in part by
  [#169](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/169).
- **Codex behind managed shell wrappers:** messages and queue nudges reach a ready
  Codex seat launched through a managed shell wrapper, instead of being refused as a
  bare shell. The existing process-identity and input-readiness checks are retained
  ([#171](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/171)).

## Upgrade and verification limits

Node.js 22 and 24 remain supported; Node 20 is unsupported. This maintenance
change adds no dependency, engine or database-migration change. Follow the
[existing upgrade procedure](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/f8f3aff68bf425735173df9e2c5ac5ef19716f5b/skills/_canonical/core/openrig-upgrade/SKILL.md).

**Verified on an installed 0.6.2 test machine:** a two-agent Codex team (owner and
checker) completed a native handoff, an independent review and the owner's closure.
After a graceful reboot, and again after a hard power-off, the same Codex pair resumed
useful, reviewed work. Recovery used a manual daemon start and resuming the existing
rig; it was not automatic. Checked task files, queue records and saved history prefixes
were preserved, but a checkpoint written just before the hard power-off was lost, so
this is not a general crash-durability guarantee.

**Not yet verified:** Claude-only and mixed-runtime starters; the scope, loading and
revocation of the OpenRig command-permission rules; and any overall CPU improvement.

Slack app manifest/setup assistance and Rig Stream classification remain
experimental, with no new real-app or provider-run validation here. The existing
Slack connector is not experimental. See the
[retained limitations](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/f8f3aff68bf425735173df9e2c5ac5ef19716f5b/docs/releases/v0.6.0.md#known-limitations).

Release commit: `f8f3aff68bf425735173df9e2c5ac5ef19716f5b`.

body.name: OpenRig v0.6.1 — first-use repairs and one help path
body.body:
**Published:** `@openrig/cli@0.6.1` is available on npm as `latest`.

```sh
npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.6.1
```

# OpenRig 0.6.1 — First-use repairs and one help path

OpenRig 0.6.1 improves first-use guidance, Codex readiness and linked-worktree
launches, with a single help path and regression checks on pull requests.

## Find help from the installed version

Ask your agent to read:

```sh
rig context get help
```

The [help guide](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/d83bbebe97430c3f2777226fecc089d31e276aa8/docs/reference/help.md) brings together environment checks,
setup and restart symptoms, permissions, instance layout and escalation. Its
linked reference guides are included with the package too. If OpenRig cannot
install or `rig` cannot run, use the guide online at
[openrig.dev/help/agents](https://www.openrig.dev/help/agents), or read
`daemon/docs/reference/help.md` inside the installed `@openrig/cli` package.
For help, email **hello@openrig.dev**; a GitHub account is not required.

This is the canonical guide added in
[#113](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/113), with entry points from the
README and agent startup guidance.

## Read a catalogued project's execution view

```sh
rig view show execution --project <catalog-id> --mission <mission> --json
```

The CLI now forwards the selected project and mission to the existing daemon
resolver, which uses that project's configured missions root. Previously the
CLI could only use the default workspace for this view. Omitting `--project`
keeps the existing behavior. This does not add project inference from the
current directory. Thanks to [@dajiaohuang](https://github.com/dajiaohuang) for
[#105](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/105).

## Codex readiness and bundled guidance

- Startup/resume checks recognize Codex's `»` conversation prompt, including a
  fresh prompt after a dismissed hook-review panel. Numbered selection menus
  still require attention. Thanks to
  [@dajiaohuang](https://github.com/dajiaohuang) for
  [#111](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/111).
- The bundled Vault skill has valid frontmatter, with a regression check for
  shipped skill headers ([#115](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/115)).
- Historical development evidence has been removed from the public source tree
  ([#118](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/118)). The retired
  `spike/tui-drivability` prototype was also removed
  ([#119](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/119)); the shipped TUI remains.

## Identity readings and Codex launches

- **Boot-time comparisons on non-UTC hosts:** parse SQLite's zone-less boot
  timestamp as UTC. Identity and context-usage readers then compare observations
  with the actual generation start, avoiding time-zone shifts that could reject
  current observations or accept older ones. Thanks to
  [@Coder8124](https://github.com/Coder8124) for
  [#124](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/124).
- **Custom Codex status lines:** recognize an interactive conversation when its
  header has scrolled away and the status line puts a mixed-case model name
  after other fields. Unresolved trust, hook, update and model-selection gates
  remain in place. This is recognition only; the separate stale restore-warning
  behavior from [#116](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/116) is not
  repaired here. Thanks to [@Hexgunner69](https://github.com/Hexgunner69) for the
  report and [@Aummadour](https://github.com/Aummadour) for screen-derived
  regression cases included in [#125](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/125).
- **Linked Git worktrees:** Codex fresh launches resolve the worktree's Git
  directory and common Git directory instead of treating its `.git` file as a
  directory. Resume/fork arguments and permission modes are unchanged. Thanks to
  [@mgall-ibizdigital](https://github.com/mgall-ibizdigital) for the report,
  reproduction and suggested approach in
  [#121](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/121), addressed by
  [#126](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/126).

## Regression checks on pull requests

[#117](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/117) adds eight test jobs: build
and package-file inspection, type checking, repository checks, four separate
daemon/CLI/TUI/UI suites, and an installed queue-durability scenario. The latter
checks a normal run, an intentionally introduced lost-baton failure and a
healthy return. A checker that misses that seeded failure cannot pass.

The workflow uses Node 22, Linux runners for the build/repository/installed
scenario jobs, and macOS runners for the four package suites. It does not run
all eleven historical scenario seeds or certify every platform, provider or
authenticated native-agent workflow.

## Upgrade and compatibility

Node.js 22 and 24 remain the supported versions; Node 20 is unsupported. No
dependency, engine, permission-mode or database-migration change is introduced
by this maintenance release. Follow the existing
[upgrade procedure](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/d83bbebe97430c3f2777226fecc089d31e276aa8/skills/_canonical/core/openrig-upgrade/SKILL.md)
when updating an existing instance.

Package identities and the checks performed on each published artifact belong
with its [GitHub release](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases). These
source notes do not certify every platform or authenticated native workflow.
Native permission enforcement across fresh launch, resume and fork retains
the verification limits recorded for 0.6.0.

Slack app manifest/setup assistance and Rig Stream classification remain
**experimental**. This release makes no new real-app, provider-run, accuracy or
reliability claim for them. The existing Slack connector is not experimental.
See the [0.6.0 limitations](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/d83bbebe97430c3f2777226fecc089d31e276aa8/docs/releases/v0.6.0.md#known-limitations) for retained boundaries.

## Checks on this artifact

The exact package was installed in a disposable macOS 15.7.3 ARM64 guest with
Node 24.21.0/npm 11.19.0. Consumer postinstall ran, SQLite 13.0.3 loaded its
bundled prebuild, and database integrity and all 89 migration identities were
checked. Two real Codex project agents completed a CSV-import repair and
independently reviewed it; the final task check passed three regression tests.

This was an assisted custom-prefix installation: native login shells did not
inherit that prefix. The initial agents located the absolute command, the
operator corrected the TUI shell PATH, and a later fresh-agent orientation
stopped at `rig not found`. Agent shells used Node 22; the daemon and final
operator check used Node 24. This does not establish a completely unassisted
installation on every platform.

Fresh launch and resume produced bounded observations. A native fork child was
observed, but managed fork completion was not verified after a command timeout;
do not interpret this as universal native permission-enforcement coverage.
Pi was not tested and Herdr was unavailable in this run.

OpenRig remains intended for trusted local/private environments. This release
does not claim hardened public-network deployment or add a manual UI-token
setup requirement.

## Artifact identity

- Source: `d83bbebe97430c3f2777226fecc089d31e276aa8`
- Tree: `ed73fe548f6421374cae96aba7963d5683b45405`
- Package SHA256: `bf9aa3a78c2bf6ac887920485da7793545dd6a283d21120dd766b20da7454e87`

body.name: OpenRig v0.6.0 — works for strangers
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.6.0 — works for strangers

`@openrig/cli@0.6.0` is published on npm and is the `latest` release.

This release requires **Node.js 22 or 24** and upgrades to better-sqlite3 13.
Node 20 is no longer supported. On Apple silicon, use Node.js 22.

Highlights:

- Per-seat permission choices for future launches, with audited selection and truthful launch status.
- An opt-in typing guard that holds automatic input for seats where you type by hand.
- A single TUI action to open a whole rig in Herdr.
- Pi activity-generation checks, clearer kernel runtime selection, Codex launch isolation and the mission-readiness fix.
- **Experimental:** offline Slack app manifest/setup assistance and optional Jev/Rig Stream classification, off by default. Experimental labels are not authoritative routing or delivery decisions.

An ordinary candidate-tarball install passed on a fresh macOS ARM64 VM with
Node.js 22.22.1, real npm postinstall, SQLite, all 89 migrations and daemon
startup/shutdown. The final merged-commit package differs only in two build
stamps and also passed the Build installation/upgrade checks. Prior Node 24
SQLite/migration/GC evidence is retained; fresh Node 24, Linux, Windows and
authenticated native-permission journeys were not established by these checks.
The Slack manifest and stream classifier may be incomplete or not work in your
setup; please report issues or contribute fixes.

See the [full release notes, migration guidance, limitations and contributor credits](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/57380a250e797c182a336e97afe2e0edb841ba9c/docs/releases/v0.6.0.md).

Thanks to [@jimallen](https://github.com/jimallen) for reporting the Node 26 installation
failure and proposing the better-sqlite3 13 upgrade in
[#16](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/16), and to all contributors and reporters credited in the full notes.

Release commit: `57380a250e797c182a336e97afe2e0edb841ba9c`.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.17 — install with Bun
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.17 — install with Bun

Changes for version **0.5.17**. Publication status and date are recorded on the
[GitHub release](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.17) and npm.

OpenRig 0.5.17 can be installed with Bun as well as npm.

## Install with Bun

```sh
bun add -g @openrig/cli
```

Earlier versions listed the unpublished `@openrig/daemon` package as a dependency.
npm used the copy bundled in the package, but Bun looked it up in the registry
and failed with a 404. The package now imports the daemon copy it already ships
and no longer depends on `@openrig/daemon`, which also makes it smaller. npm
installation is unchanged.

OpenRig still runs on Node.js, so install Node.js 22 as well. Bun may block this
package's postinstall script. In that case the Node.js version and SQLite check
does not run at install time. See [what OpenRig changes on your machine](../../README.md#what-openrig-changes-on-your-machine).

The installation fix was verified with Bun 1.4.0 and npm on macOS arm64 with
Node.js 22. Other combinations are not verified.

## Contributors and included pull requests

Thanks to [@drewpayment](https://github.com/drewpayment) for reporting the Bun
installation failure in [#66](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/66),
fixed in [#68](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/68).

The Node support range and SQLite version are unchanged. The macOS arm64 with
Node 24 SQLite installation limitation noted for 0.5.15 still applies; use
Node 22 on macOS arm64.

## npm publication status

`@openrig/cli@0.5.17` is published as npm `latest`. The registry tarball was verified byte-identical to the reviewed package.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.16 — choose the Claude instruction file
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.16 — choose the Claude instruction file

Changes for version **0.5.16**. Publication status and date are recorded on the
[GitHub release](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.16) and npm.

OpenRig 0.5.16 lets a rig keep its managed Claude Code instructions out of a
tracked `CLAUDE.md`, and adds an advisory portability report for pull requests.

## Keep a tracked CLAUDE.md unchanged

OpenRig writes its instructions for Claude Code members into managed blocks in
each member's working directory. By default that file is `CLAUDE.md`. If your
repository tracks `CLAUDE.md`, select `CLAUDE.local.md` in the rig spec:

```yaml
managed_blocks:
  claude-code: CLAUDE.local.md
```

Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.local.md` from the working directory as well; keep it
out of git, for example with a `.gitignore` entry. The selection applies when
members launch, restore, relaunch or are added, and it is kept by `rig export`
and rig bundles. `rig down` removes OpenRig's blocks only from the selected file.
OpenRig never edits, moves or deletes blocks in the other file.

Only the `claude-code` key is accepted, with `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md`;
any other key or value is rejected before a member launches. Without the field,
behavior is unchanged. Codex members always use `AGENTS.md`.

**Switching an existing rig:** blocks OpenRig already wrote into `CLAUDE.md`
stay there. Until you remove them, the file stays modified and Claude Code loads
both copies. Delete each `<!-- BEGIN OpenRig MANAGED BLOCK: … -->` …
`<!-- END OpenRig MANAGED BLOCK: … -->` section by hand and keep the rest of the
file. If `CLAUDE.md` has no other uncommitted edits you need to keep, you can
instead run `git restore CLAUDE.md`; that command discards every unstaged change
to the file, not only OpenRig's blocks. See
[the RigSpec reference](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/blob/5c5470303518a2142a7cb673b08414c0f73d3d3e/docs/reference/rig-spec.md#choosing-the-claude-instruction-file).

## Portability report for pull requests

A new pull-request workflow lists added lines that contain values tied to one
machine, network or account: credentials, home and temporary paths, network
addresses and email addresses. Suspected credentials are withheld from the
report. Findings never fail the check; the author decides what to change. It is
pattern-based and does not guarantee that nothing private remains. Run it
locally with:

```sh
node scripts/portability-report.mjs
```

## Contributors and included pull requests

Thanks to [@hvpaiva](https://github.com/hvpaiva) for reporting and proposing the
Claude instruction-file option in [#25](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/issues/25),
and to [@mvschwarz](https://github.com/mvschwarz) for the README badges and demo
([#54](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/54)) and the portability report
([#56](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/56)).

The Node support range and SQLite version are unchanged. The macOS arm64 with
Node 24 SQLite installation limitation noted for 0.5.15 still applies; use
Node 22 on macOS arm64.

npm publication: verified available as @openrig/cli@0.5.16.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.15 — first-use recovery, software factory guidance and Pi fixes
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.15 — first-use recovery, software factory guidance and Pi fixes

Changes for version **0.5.15**. Publication status and date are recorded on the
[GitHub release](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.15) and npm.

OpenRig 0.5.15 improves startup and recovery, adds public guidance for a continuing
software team and user-chosen command permissions, and fixes Pi reply visibility,
shell context and terminal input handling.

## Start and return with clearer guidance

Before launching, read
[what OpenRig changes on your machine](../../README.md#what-openrig-changes-on-your-machine).
Provider integration can configure executable hooks and workspace trust; changing
only `OPENRIG_HOME` does not isolate provider configuration. The
[getting-started guide](../reference/getting-started.md) walks through your first
task and explains these setup effects.

Check the commands available in your installation:

```sh
rig --version
rig --help
rig up --help
```

Startup and recovery recognize native Codex through shell and Node launchers,
and report uncertainty when process identity cannot be established. Recognized
update notices are skipped without installing provider updates. Authentication
and trust choices remain yours.

Startup errors now describe the problem and a recovery action. If a name matches
both a starter and a stopped rig, `rig up <name> --existing` selects the existing
rig. Inspect its reported state before assigning more work.

## Continue useful reviewed work

Give your agent a real repository, an outcome and the decisions you want to keep.
The bundled OpenRig Software Factory recipe supports direct team work,
queue-supported orchestration or an optional explicit Workflow.

```sh
rig context show skills/core/openrig-software-factory --json
rig context get skills/core/openrig-software-factory/SKILL.md
rig context get skills/core/openrig-software-factory/references/worked-example.md
```

Start with the two-seat team. Add one or two seats with `rig grow` when the work
benefits from separate responsibilities. The example covers roles, context,
work ownership, independent review, concurrency and cost, and distinguishes
changes to the running team from saving an updated RigSpec. Use guidance matching
your installed version.

## Choose command permissions

Ask your agent to inspect the target harness, explain the available scopes and
apply your choice while preserving existing rules:

```sh
rig context get skills/applying-a-permission-policy/SKILL.md
```

Allowing the whole `rig` command family includes lifecycle and configuration
changes as well as reads. Choose narrower commands or retain approval prompts
when appropriate. Project-only setup requires supported, active and trusted
project configuration; if it is unavailable, the agent should explain the limit
instead of substituting user-wide permission. Back up touched files and verify
the selected rules in the actual conversation. Shipped sandbox, approval and
permission defaults are unchanged.

## Known compatibility limitation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24, installing the SQLite dependency can fail when a
suitable prebuilt binary is unavailable and compilation is not available.
Compiler-built SQLite has also failed during database cleanup at runtime.
**Use Node 22 on macOS arm64 for now.** This recommendation does not change the
declared Node support range, and this version does not update SQLite.

## Pi replies, input and recovery

Pi replies and tool progress are visible for the supported RPC event shapes.
Shell tools retain the managed OpenRig context needed for identity and routing.
Provider errors are shown with bounded text, and exhausted retries do not print
the same error repeatedly.

Pasted messages wait for explicit submission. The terminal runner accepts input
beyond the terminal's canonical buffer limit, preserves editing and cancellation,
and recovers after rejecting an oversized framed message. This is not a general
latency guarantee or an unrestricted input-size promise.

An added seat whose first startup failed during resource projection, before its
startup context was saved, can use the guarded retry after the setup problem is corrected.
Retain the complete original member fragment and its source root; a snapshot alone
does not reconstruct missing startup configuration. Use one retry at a time.
Ordinary conversation resume remains separate.

**Pi support is qualified and supervised.** Controlled coding, follow-up,
reporting and conversation continuity were verified with Pi 0.87.1 and OpenRouter
`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`; ordinary-seat identity, tools and a reply also worked.
Completion of an ordinary useful task and unattended team operation remain
unverified. Context-profile selection and hook-generation coverage are limited;
do not assume parity with every Codex or Claude integration. The Software Factory
guide likewise does not establish fully unattended operation.

## Contributors and included pull requests

Thanks to [@danielkuykendall23-boop](https://github.com/danielkuykendall23-boop)
for the Pi reply fix in [#37](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/37), and to
[@mvschwarz](https://github.com/mvschwarz) for Codex startup and restore guidance
([#38](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/38)), Software Factory and permission
guidance ([#39](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/39)), contribution and
support guidance ([#45](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/45)), and the
first-use README ([#46](https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/pull/46)).

This release also includes the startup-identity refinements, guarded first-start
retry, Pi shell/error handling and terminal-input fixes described above. Project
work-policy features and the Node 22/SQLite 13 upgrade are outside this release.

---

npm publication status: verified. @openrig/cli@0.5.15 is available from npm; the registry tarball matches the verified release artifact.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.14 — clearer navigation, mission progress and human notifications
body.body:
OpenRig 0.5.14 makes reading more predictable when opened or refreshed, keeps
human requests distinct from informational updates, and groups instance settings
and health where they are easier to find.

## Enter and keep reading

Bare interactive `rig` enters the ordinary TUI after confirming a running rig.
An instance without running rigs keeps the startup chooser. Help, Skip and Local
remain responsive during slow or unverified detection; a late observation does
not take navigation away after the user has chosen another route.

Pages distinguish initial loading, successful empty results, refresh and failure.
The navigator remains usable through page and rig changes. A previously read page
can stay visible with its original scope label while the selected page loads;
that prior content has no action targets. Same-scope refresh retains useful content,
with the previous read time and Retry. A failed Feed source retains its own data
while healthy sibling sources update. Confirmed denial, empty results and removals
clear affected content, and late replies cannot replace the current selection.
First visits retain navigation and local feedback. Topology first offers rig
selection, then reads that rig before unrelated fleet details. Terminal names are
available before detailed readiness and preview.

Projects keeps malformed mission and slice sources visible as local errors while
healthy neighbors remain readable. Correcting the affected source and refreshing
restores its content without showing its parser fragment above unrelated work.

Optional blocker descriptions load independently, so an unavailable description
does not hide primary queue facts or change the recorded human recipient.
Fleet reads share one elapsed request budget across stages and retain local
results when a remote source fails. Repeated proof-policy and delivery-receipt
reads avoid duplicate work while later reads still observe current inputs.
These changes reduce measured work; they do not establish a latency guarantee.

Selective restore and startup event indexes reduce inventory read work while
preserving event history and projection results. Private query replay does not
establish a general live response-time guarantee.

Terminal catalogs reuse one inventory read instead of repeating the same global
scan. The measured result was equivalent with less query work; this is not a
general latency guarantee. Existing saved-view discovery, passive preview and
deliberate Herdr Open remain available.

## Complete requests and quiet updates

Human notifications distinguish explicit decision requests from informational
updates. A request carries a complete brief and requested action; related
supplemental detail can continue in its thread. Content that exceeds supported
limits is refused with an author correction instead of silently losing essential
text. The shipped authoring guidance calls for concise, complete human briefs.

Informational FYIs require no action or reply and do not create approval
obligations. Delivery completion is separate from a human decision. Partial or
ambiguous delivery remains distinguishable, and retry/reply tracking keeps each
request and its thread separate. Existing callers without an explicit intent
retain decision behavior.

## Find requests and instance health

The six top-level entries are **Topology, Specs, Projects, Terminals, Feed and
System**. Feed explicitly covers the instance and all humans. **Human requests**
shows recipients and relevant scope; **Updates** includes confirmed delivered
FYIs alongside existing outcome and health updates. Delivered FYIs remain in a
bounded history after their delivery obligation closes. Reading is not approval.
Feed's Explorer contains these categories, with entries in the content pane.
Specs kind groups and Derived terminal views start collapsed and expand explicitly;
Saved views stay prominent. Saved membership still requires deliberate setup, and
opening a terminal view remains an explicit action.

System opens to instance **Health**, followed by **Configuration** and
**Connections**. Contextual Health, global Help and compatible direct commands
remain available, including `attention`, `needs`, `feed`, `config` and
`connections`.

## Understand mission progress

Projects puts completed outcomes, current work and owner, blockers, next dependency
and slice boxes before process prose at both terminal widths. Accepted required
proof judgments determine slice outcomes; all slice outcomes must be complete
before the mission reports outcomes complete. Evidence attachments, quiet activity
and handoff alone do not accept proof. Reopened or assigned unfinished work stays
open, including when there is no unassigned next slice.

Actual custody and planned ownership remain separate. Authored lifecycle and
publication are separate from outcome completion; unknown ownership or eligibility
stays unknown. Narrow screens retain a full first box and scroll for the remainder.

## Operator notes and verification limits

Root, CLI, daemon and web UI versions are 0.5.14; the terminal TUI remains 0.1.0.
Node requirements are unchanged. Migration 081 adds explicit intent and
supplemental detail to queue records. The migration head is now
`084_inventory_event_indexes`, adding three selective inventory read indexes;
083 adds the two review read indexes. Migration 082 adds nullable identity
provenance to archived queue transitions. Archival preserves recorded values and
refuses an archive schema that cannot carry them; legacy unknown values remain null.
Shared history, RECENT and OWNER/receipt readers now include archived records,
so their results can broaden even where the command or TUI code is unchanged.
Migration alone does not reconstruct previously lost metadata. Use the supported
upgrade and continuity process when adoption is authorized.

The private combined review exercised installed journeys at 140×42 and 80×24,
including entry, refresh, source failure, scope identity, detail/Back, saved
terminal Open and notification correlation. An initial Feed source-failure defect
was retained in the evidence and repaired, then independently rechecked. Owner
candidate-native evidence and the reviewer's child TUI against an unchanged
parent daemon remain separate observations.

Later operator inspection exposed disruptive navigation and a misleading mission
overview. The corrected private combined review covers the new navigation,
organizers and native mission states. Its false NEXT-completion finding was
preserved, repaired and independently rechecked at both widths. These private
results remain limited to the journeys and environments exercised.

VM inspection was accepted on September 14: generally zero-to-two-second
loading with occasional timeouts, along with formatting, icon colors and default
views. This observed result is not a general latency or availability guarantee.
Later recovery of the same candidate preserved sessions but did not establish a
durable responsiveness fix.

- Intermittent read timeouts remain. An inherited CLI health-check deadline can
  report the daemon unresponsive before sending a queue request even when the
  direct request succeeds. That defect is not fixed here; occasional server
  delay also remains unattributed.
- Earlier notification checks used controlled HTTP responses and synthetic replies.
  A later real single-consumer Slack exercise confirmed complete decision/detail/FYI
  posting and reply correlation; the operator confirmed phone readership and
  readability. That observation does not establish OS push behavior or all clients.
- Terminal provider evidence covers disposable Herdr members. Other provider,
  remote and parent-host behavior is not established by this review.
- Saved Build watch discovery was exercised in the VM and its native judgment
  recorded. That observation does not establish general navigation responsiveness.
- Simultaneous default TUI clients retain the existing programmatic control-socket
  limitation. Unique test sockets do not prove general multi-client isolation.
- Version and package checks do not repeat the development journeys or establish
  a new whole-source, all-platform or unfamiliar-human usability result.
- Observed shutdown-drain timeouts, recorded config-preservation uncertainties
  and a prior `recorder_write_failed` observation are not claimed resolved.
  Recovery evidence remains distinct from ordinary-entry verification and does
  not establish whole-system health.
- Historical source-scan findings retain their recorded dispositions; a clean
  changed-path scan is not a clean whole-source scan.
- Bundled Workflow Specs, including `basic-loop`, can disappear from discovery
  after an upgrade changes the install directory despite their YAML remaining
  intact. The discovery fix is explicitly deferred beyond 0.5.14; this release
  contains no repair for it.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.13
body.body:
**Status:** published.

The source, the annotated `v0.5.13` tag, this GitHub Release, and
`@openrig/cli@0.5.13` on npm are all published. npm publication completed on
2026-09-10 and the registry lists `0.5.13` as `latest`; the published tarball was
verified byte-identical to the accepted release archive. Exact-cut substance
review and release verification are complete for this cut. Adoption so far is
**VM-only**; no parent or general adoption is established or authorized.

> Note: the in-repo `docs/releases/v0.5.13.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` carry
> "release candidate, unpublished" wording. That text is frozen inside the
> published commit and is historical, not the current public status.

OpenRig 0.5.13 connects the human TUI journey: enter the instance, choose a
project, read its current instructions, understand what needs your decision,
and deliberately open the terminals you need. Scoped oversight and explicit
Git context updates help agents work from the right instructions while keeping
authority, evidence and local authorship visible.

## Start with something useful

Bare interactive `rig` exposes Help, Skip and local reading while startup
checks are running, when the daemon is down, or when its state is unverified.
Selected project, mission and slice intent can be read from disk without
pretending it is live queue, execution or topology data. Read failures and
source provenance stay visible. Starting a daemon or returning seats to work
remains a deliberate action; reading and skipping do not imply consent.

## Read the current source and find your way back

PROJECTS keeps a selected project's identity and root through missions,
slices and source views, including projects with the same display name.
An unavailable source is reported for that project instead of substituting
another project's work. Refresh reads the current file.

The shared reader shows source paths, modification/hash information and
bounded content, with scrolling, local links, heading links and Back.
HTTP(S) links show a selectable destination for copying; no browser is opened.
Missing, unreadable, binary or out-of-root files remain named errors. Large files show the
1 MiB returned-content limit; a heading absent from a truncated prefix is
not claimed absent from the whole file. Back restores the prior reading
and navigation position.

## Know what needs your decision

ATTENTION separates **Action required** from **Updates**. Human requests
and explicit blockers show the request, urgency, scope and work it would
unblock. Outcome and health updates retain their own source and history.
Open the detail or linked evidence to understand it; viewing a request is
not approval or delivery, and closing a queue item is not proof of a
completed product outcome. Missing or incomplete reads stay visible.

## Preview terminals before opening them

TERMINALS lists saved and derived views with their members and resolved
layout. A preview is passive. Deliberate Open uses the inspected plan and
reports opened, absent or degraded members, including partial failures.
Help and side trips return to the same preview and page. The observed native
provider journey uses Herdr; broader provider limits are listed below.

CONFIG keeps full values, defaults and source/override provenance readable.
Help supplies command descriptions, grammar and examples, including during
startup failures. Narrow views retain scrolling and return controls. Health
keeps INFO severity separate from Unknown assessment, exposes stale and
unavailable reads, and explains that an empty findings list is **not a healthy
verdict**. The complete empty-health explanation is readable at 80 columns.

## Choose oversight for the work in front of you

Human-led work is quiet by default for process-only diagnosis. Explicit
delegation can enable that oversight during planning as well as execution,
subject to the existing diagnosis policy and delivery prerequisites. Ordinary
work reminders and operational health retain their behavior. Scope, phase
and posture come from explicit sources; unresolved identity stays unknown.

Use `rig mode effective` with an explicit scope to inspect the result.
The [scoped operating posture reference](../reference/scoped-operating-posture.md)
describes selection and precedence. A posture preference grants no execution
authority. Correction records can retain selected current guidance and
distinguish an assessment, an action actually taken and a later observed
effect. These are supported mechanics, not evidence of improved judgment:
natural behavioral effect remains **UNOBSERVED**, and human time cost remains
**UNMEASURED**. No cure or reduced recurrence is claimed.

## Update context without discarding local authorship

`rig context add <repository-path-or-URL> --git` retains the relationship
between a Git source, its checkout and a selected context pack. Use `--pack`
when selecting a pack within a repository. Existing Git credentials apply.

Use `rig context source inspect <ref>` to inspect local changes, conflicts,
revision and selection without fetching. `rig context source update <ref>`
explicitly fetches and merges upstream before selecting clean content.
Committed local work survives an ordinary merge. Dirty work, conflicting
changes, unavailable upstreams or edits to the served selection cause a
named refusal rather than a reset or overwrite. Resolve and commit, or abort
the merge, in the retained checkout before retrying; the prior served
selection remains available during a conflict. Updates do not push.

Checkout history, selected served bytes and actual agent consumption remain
different facts. Read the selected bytes with `rig context get <ref>` and
check the intended consumer. This does not automatically synchronize every
context library or adopt guidance into running agents.

## Operator notes and validation limits

Root, CLI, daemon and web-UI package versions are 0.5.13. The terminal TUI
retains its independent 0.1.0 version. Node requirements are unchanged.
The ordered migration head advances from 079 to
`080_scoped_operating_posture`, extending the existing mode-binding store
with scoped human-led/delegated choices while preserving legacy rows.
Use the supported upgrade and continuity procedure when adoption is
authorized; preparing this candidate performs no live migration or restart.

Accepted development evidence connects the journey at 140×42 and 80×24,
including unavailable/Unknown controls, two-project isolation, current-source
reading, deliberate native terminal opening and Git conflict preservation.
Those observations retain their original development cuts and attribution.
Version, release-note and package checks are separate from those journeys;
they are not a new whole-release usability study.

- Simultaneous default TUI clients can replace one another's programmatic
  control-socket address. This remains a known, unfixed limitation, judged
  nonblocking for the demonstrated single-client human journey. Unique test
  sockets do not prove product-level multi-client isolation; historical lost
  requests remain unverified.
- Native terminal proof covers Herdr. SSH login, cmux end-to-end behavior
  and effects on a parent host remain unverified. Existing native continuity
  evidence is reused only for unchanged paths, not new provider coverage.
- A private shutdown timed out while closing connections; clean completion
  and pending effects remain unverified. Earlier sandbox public-start failures
  remain recorded failures despite a later successful managed private start.
- Synthetic findings and requests exercise mechanics, not natural behavioral
  improvement or real human approval/delivery. No unfamiliar-human study,
  real-host reboot or all-platform run is established.
- Exact-cut verification and publication authorization are complete for this
  cut, and the substance receipt binding was re-measured at the publishing seat.
  npm availability was subsequently confirmed and the registry artifact verified
  byte-identical to the accepted archive. Nothing here authorizes adoption beyond
  the VM-only adoption already recorded.


## Install

```sh
npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.5.13
```

## Release identity

- Commit: `bda26cb90def54b844260f12a63ce9cabc50509c`
- Tree: `ee5b73d91f1c21c6a8edb0457e9875ff196ba9da`
- Previous public main: `b6c8d8f0444bc721d0ba4062a7384d25601c1c6f` (fast-forward, 31 commits)

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.12
body.body:
**Status:** published.

The source, the annotated `v0.5.12` tag, this GitHub Release, and
`@openrig/cli@0.5.12` on npm are all available. npm publication completed on
2026-09-09 and the registry lists `0.5.12` as `latest`; the published tarball
was verified byte-identical to the accepted release archive. The exact-cut
substance gate and release verification completed before publication.

> Note: the in-repo `docs/releases/v0.5.12.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` carry
> "release candidate" wording. That text is frozen inside the published commit
> and was written before this publication step; it is not evidence that these
> Git surfaces are unpublished.

OpenRig 0.5.12 connects everyday workflow actions to useful progress views,
recoverable ownership and a readable TUI. The goal is to let an operator or
agent start, understand, adapt and return to work without maintaining status
copies or knowing a private recovery recipe.

## Record a judgment once

An authorized, evidence-backed proof judgment derives the affected proof,
slice, mission and project readiness. Correcting that judgment updates its
dependent views while retaining unrelated work and the original evidence.
Code, attributed patch-equivalent work and non-code artifacts can carry
truthful provenance. A checkbox, uploaded file or closed queue item does not
become semantic acceptance, and readiness does not mean publication.

## Know which graph is running

Ordinary workflow inspection distinguishes authored scope from the bound
running graph, advisory ordering from executable dependencies, and planning
waves from runtime steps. `rig workflow revise` previews supported changes
before applying them, preserving completed work and current custody.
Incompatible edits name the decision that needs reconsideration. Operation
identity and `rig workflow operation` recover an ambiguous creation/revision
result without duplicating its effect. Selected development-method guidance
returns with workflow continuation, including the original story and useful
next action; the daemon does not judge the meaning of agent-authored prose.

## Give failures an owner and a recovery path

Exception readiness explains the selected owner before failure and keeps
missing configuration, a genuine no-match and unavailable routing evidence
distinct. Routing uses authored agent identities or registered human fallback.
An unhandled dependency-branch failure records its occurrence, owning task
and wake together, even when another branch remains live. A failed nudge does
not erase the task. After correcting the cause, use `rig workflow resume`
with `--occurrence <failed-qitem-id>` to select that failure: its obsolete
exception closes in the redrive transaction, while other unresolved failures
and completed work remain visible.

## Wait quietly without losing work

Healthy unchanged waits avoid repeated full-context packets. Overlapping
notifications for the same actionable episode share presentation and retain
provenance. Changed blockers, missed delivery and stranded work retain bounded
recovery or escalation. Ordinary reads expose the current owner, blocker and
next useful decision first, with explicit expansion for complete evidence.
Unknown activity remains unknown; a reminder is not progress.

## Start and return through the same TUI

Bare interactive `rig` is the normal front door, including first setup,
daemon-down startup and return after a restart. The TUI shows the intended
instance and observed prerequisites, offers daemon startup, and supports
selecting the rigs and seats to return to work. Kernel is recommended first;
unselected rigs keep their histories. Resume preserves the selected seat's
recorded conversation when available. An unavailable resume offers a named
repair or an explicitly confirmed fresh, re-primed conversation; it is never
silently replaced. Launcher and native startup fixes retain useful errors
when a runtime or dependency is unavailable.

## Browse general instance settings in CONFIG

CONFIG organizes instance, workspace/context, display/timezone, waiting,
snapshot and recovery settings into readable categories with source and
override provenance. Advanced settings and full values remain discoverable.
Slack and human connections are one child of CONFIG. Opening or refreshing
the browser is passive and secret-safe; configured values remain distinct
from observed application, connectivity and delivery. Users can return to
ordinary scope and work views without opening configuration files.

## Operator notes

Root, CLI, daemon and web-UI package versions are 0.5.12. The terminal TUI
retains its independent 0.1.0 version. Node requirements and the ordered
migration head `079_workflow_lifecycle_parallel` are unchanged from 0.5.11;
this release adds no database migration.

Use the supported upgrade and continuity procedure when adoption is authorized.
Preparing this candidate does not restart a daemon or renew existing seats.
Configuration inspection is not an editor, credential migration, automatic
repair or a promise that every setting hot-reloads. Editing an authored graph
alone does not adopt it into a progressed workflow. The exception repair does
not retroactively create tasks for failures already committed by older code;
inspect retained occurrences and use the supported recovery route deliberately.

## Validation scope and known limitations

The accepted development outcome includes one less-primed, returning/assisted
agent journey through two dependent slices: recording and correcting proof,
revising the graph, waiting and returning, recovering a real failed handout
check, and navigating CONFIG back to work. Focused mechanism reviews and
installed controls support that journey. Native startup, resume and wake
observations retain their original source cuts and times; they are reused
with attribution, not presented as new runs on the version-only candidate.
Candidate package and generated-version checks are recorded separately from
those development judgments.

- This was not an unfamiliar-human study, an unassisted greenfield usability
  trial or all-platform verification. Setup and one-time native approvals
  remain part of the recorded journey.
- The final exception task was consumed through public read/claim/action
  after its placeholder destination could not receive a nudge. It does not
  establish native exception delivery or external human receipt.
- Quiet-wait measurements establish the tested workload's attention and
  recovery behavior, not a global latency guarantee or provider billing-token
  savings. A retained startup catalog-unavailable control also failed on its
  unchanged parent; the evidence is not an all-green test-suite claim.
- Whole-package substance review and exact-release verification have bound this
  candidate; the substance gate was consumed at the publishing seat against this
  exact source and archive. npm availability was subsequently confirmed and the
  registry artifact verified byte-identical to the accepted archive. Nothing here
  authorizes runtime adoption.


## Install

```sh
npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.5.12
```

## Release identity

- Commit: `b6c8d8f0444bc721d0ba4062a7384d25601c1c6f`
- Tree: `a24ee20dc1ff7bc9b2fbb8dca59702d3b324f31c`
- Previous public main: `ffd5ac1dd71367561ed8357bc42d5131821ee5f2` (fast-forward, 36 commits)

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.11
body.body:
**Status:** published. The source, the annotated `v0.5.11` tag, this GitHub
Release, and `@openrig/cli@0.5.11` on npm are all available.

npm publication completed on 2026-09-08; the registry lists `0.5.11` as
`latest`. The published tarball was verified byte-identical to the accepted
release archive. The exact-cut substance gate and release verification
completed before publication.

> Note: the in-repo `docs/releases/v0.5.11.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` carry
> "release candidate" wording. That text is frozen inside the published commit
> and was written before this publication step; it is not evidence that this
> release is unpublished.

OpenRig 0.5.11 makes it easier to start useful work in an ordinary repository,
understand the team and its workflow in the TUI, and diagnose configuration or
lifecycle failures without mistaking uncertain state for success.

## First useful work and a shared view

- The `first-project` starter provides a focused Codex owner/checker pair for
  one repository. The README follows that path from launch through a useful
  change, independent checking, and returning to the work.
- A new kernel includes a shared TUI terminal. `rig tui --shared` attaches to
  that existing view; plain `rig tui` opens a standalone view. Joining the
  shared view does not silently launch a missing terminal or agent.
- Herdr users can follow the same repository and terminal journey. This is
  preparation for useful operation without a plugin; no Herdr plugin or
  community-adoption result is part of this release.

## Understand work in the ordinary TUI

- Mission views expose workflows, their current step and owner, waits, and
  the work packet behind a transition. Source navigation connects the view
  to the authored work and specs.
- Specs presents the declared purpose, including a rig's `summary`, and
  distinguishes missing content from a failed read.
- Connections shows the running daemon and CLI identities, effective instance
  settings, configured and applied gateway state, and registered human routes.
  It is a passive inspection surface; a configured connector is not proof
  that a person received a message.
- Command completion, readable Recent activity, and a persistent configurable
  timezone make daily navigation easier. The default display timezone is
  America/Los_Angeles.
- A timed-out daemon probe stays unverified throughout the TUI chrome instead
  of being labeled as a confirmed outage.

## More reliable coordination and lifecycle

- Project-owned release profiles provide reusable ceremony and post-release
  boundary steps. Current-release closure does not depend on inventing a
  successor mission. Agents still judge the evidence behind each obligation.
- Workflow exception recovery preserves the correct owner and clears resolved
  exception state. Stuck-work findings retain the source evidence needed to
  route them honestly.
- Terminal delivery preserves long authored context; paced-walk verification
  checks the intended piece and the applicable runtime/generation record.
  Delivery and native-turn completion remain distinct from comprehension.
- Context profile and work-install commands accept consistent Claude runtime
  spellings (`claude-code` and `claude`) alongside `codex`, with invalid
  explicit values rejected before projection.
- Startup uses the selected authored proof. It does not add an unrequested
  exercise, and terminal-only members do not receive agent proof challenges.
- Daemon shutdown has a bounded budget and an attributed outcome receipt.
  Failed or missing receipts remain visible on the supported stop paths.
- Daemon startup binds success and state publication to its actual child,
  handles competing starts, and retains uncertainty when child liveness
  cannot be established. Cross-host request attribution identifies the origin
  independently of the selected destination.

## Operator notes

Root, CLI, daemon, and web-UI package versions are 0.5.11. The terminal TUI
retains its independent 0.1.0 package version. Node requirements are unchanged.
The ordered database migration head remains `079_workflow_lifecycle_parallel`;
this release adds no migration beyond the 0.5.10 source baseline.

Diagnosis `show` and `list` now return summary-depth `--json`, retaining current
state and decisions while identifying omitted evidence. Consumers needing the
complete record must use `--full --json`, or execute the printed expansion
command. Queue `show` retains its 512-codepoint body preview and adds explicit
size, completeness, and expansion metadata. HTTP responses and mutation JSON
remain complete. These defaults are not a global output-size cap.

Use the supported upgrade procedure with a database backup and continuity
checks. A daemon restart and a rig shutdown have different effects; the latter
stops seats. Existing kernels are not automatically rebuilt to acquire the new
shared terminal.

## Validation scope and limitations

The candidate retains earlier isolated, installed-package evidence for the
connected first-project/workflow/TUI journey and focused verification of the
purpose and unverified-state corrections. Those earlier runs are attributed
prior evidence, not new end-to-end or provider enrollment tests for this cut.
Package identity and bounded installed rendering checks accompany candidate
preparation; exact-cut substance and final release verification remain required
before publication.

- First-use evidence includes fresh re-entry; it does not establish
  same-conversation resume or complete mixed-runtime enrollment.
- Controlled Connections evidence and passive inspection do not establish
  external human delivery. Transient probe latency and delayed view population
  remain observed qualifications, with no universal responsiveness claim.
- Authored completion, legacy provenance, and proof pairing are separate
  readers. Updating a declaration does not create missing provenance or an
  execution-wave history.
- A bounded health-analysis proof of concept produced an attributed diagnosis
  and exited. It is research evidence, not a shipped cold-agent/run API,
  provider abstraction, or proof of a cost or latency advantage over residency.

## Install

```sh
npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.5.11
```

## Release identity

- Commit: `ffd5ac1dd71367561ed8357bc42d5131821ee5f2`
- Tree: `7e60cda501ab05738dea6e010bc369faf7be5d26`
- Migration head: `079_workflow_lifecycle_parallel` (unchanged from 0.5.10)

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.10
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.10 — explainable System Health

OpenRig 0.5.10 makes fleet health inspectable without turning observation into
another source of work. Agents and operators can query the same bounded,
evidence-bearing findings in the CLI and TUI, hand uncertain patterns to an
agent for diagnosis, and route a verified human request when project policy
requires it. The release also carries authored mission context through workflow
waits, so lifecycle progress no longer depends on an orchestrator remembering
the ceremony.

## System Health

- **Inspect health at the scope you actually own.** `rig health` supports the
  current seat, a stable seat ID, a rig, or the local instance. Each finding
  retains its category, severity, status, confidence, source window, freshness,
  rule, evidence, policy version, and smallest useful next inspection. Empty
  output explicitly does not claim health.
- **See the same truth in the terminal UI.** Instance, rig, and seat views expose
  compact health summaries, a HEALTH list, and finding drill-in from the same
  canonical records used by the CLI. There is no second score or TUI-only health
  authority.
- **Detect high-confidence operational failures without transcript sentiment.**
  Deterministic detectors cover process, governance, and context signals such as
  queue amplification, authority-boundary traffic, and context pressure. Stable
  episode identity, source bounds, freshness, and explicit indeterminate states
  prevent missing or stale evidence from reading as healthy.
- **Ask an agent to diagnose the cases code cannot settle.** Opt-in health policy
  can present one bounded investigation packet for ceremony amplification. The
  assigned agent may inspect beyond the packet, record an attributed disposition,
  and request human notification only under configured policy and connector
  readiness. Diagnosis traffic is excluded from its own detector input.

## Durable lifecycle and human delivery

- **Carry authored mission context through workflow waits.** A mission can select
  an explicit boundary workflow in `mission.yaml`; compilation includes the
  project and mission manifests plus declared context references. Waiting steps
  can re-present the same packet with bounded exponential backoff, preserving one
  obligation rather than manufacturing replacement rows.
- **Select SDLC care from authored components and waves.** Shipped role and pod
  guidance follows the project and mission selection instead of inferring a
  builder-to-QA-to-review chain from seat names. Role capacity does not create a
  gate.
- **Address humans through registered delivery channels.** Registered
  `<entityId>@external` addresses expose readiness and a next inspection. A
  verified queue create persists the request before checking its receipt, while
  posted, pending, failed, and indeterminate outcomes remain distinct. Direct
  replies return through the correlated queue thread instead of being rewritten
  as terminal input.

## Upgrade and setup notes

- Root, CLI, daemon, and web UI package versions advance to `0.5.10`. The
  terminal TUI keeps its independent `0.1.0` version.
- This release adds no database migration beyond the `0.5.9` migration head.
  Normal daemon restart is sufficient for schema state; runtime adoption remains
  a separate operator decision.
- Health list and explain are read-only. Automated diagnosis is disabled until a
  policy explicitly enables it, and no detector automatically retries, reroutes,
  relaunches, edits scope, or changes lifecycle state.
- Human delivery requires a registered address and a configured, enabled, ready
  connector. Connector setup or verification does not itself send a message.

## Known limitations

- Deterministic shipped detector domains are process, governance, and context.
  Behavioral and epistemic conclusions remain attributed agent judgment rather
  than opaque scoring.
- System Health observes bounded retained records. Unsupported, clipped, stale,
  contradictory, or unavailable inputs stay indeterminate; absence of a finding
  is not proof that the system is healthy.
- Mission-boundary workflows carry context and scheduling, but agents retain the
  judgment about evidence, publication, and activation. The daemon does not
  interpret Markdown receipts or invent the next mission.
- Slack is one human-delivery connector, not the addressing contract, and a
  posted receipt proves connector acceptance rather than human readership.

## Release verification

- The accepted product frontier is exact commit
  `b26419182d98f65ddc8f5cf1997d0b3a9bfe6f0f`, tree
  `7b311e5dca2086266a682b7ebb43f68a70344d3b`.
- Mission evidence includes positive, negative, stale, and indeterminate health
  fixtures; CLI/TUI parity; an author-excluded diagnosis, human-request, reply,
  and workflow-wake journey with zero real external sends; and live negative
  dogfood of the 5/10/20/40/60-minute workflow backoff.
- Release preparation rebuilds and tests the exact clean versioned descendant.
  Publication, tagging, pushing, and runtime adoption are separate lifecycle
  actions and are not implied by this private cut.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.9
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.9 — developer-beautiful mission control

OpenRig 0.5.9 turns the terminal UI into a real mission-control surface and
gives the instance beneath it a cleaner, more durable operating model. The TUI
is easier to scan, navigate, and drive at ordinary terminal sizes; System
World, project context, and managed skills now compose explicitly; and restore,
fresh launch, scheduled wakes, and project workflows report the state they
actually acted on.

## Developer-beautiful terminal UI

- **Read the whole instance at a glance.** The topology view now presents one
  continuous agent table across rigs, keeps pod separators visible, and shows
  bounded `RECENT` work from material queue transitions without duplicating
  archived rigs or inventing missing summaries.
- **Move from overview to action without losing context.** Instance, rig,
  mission, slice, agent, and Explorer pages share one responsive visual grammar,
  preserve rig identity while scrolling, and keep lifecycle evidence and
  actions reachable at 160, 120, and 84 columns.
- **Use the terminal as a first-class interface.** Semantic state colors,
  compact glyphs, restrained motion, resize redraw, filtering, pointer-local
  scrolling, terminal-native selection/copy, attach actions, and socket-driven
  commands work through the same production surface.

## A coherent instance, context, and skill model

- **Start from one additive instance layout.** CLI and daemon startup reconcile
  the same canonical `$OPENRIG_HOME` structure, preserve existing content, and
  refuse wrong-type managed paths before writing.
- **Compose a System World with the current project.** `context.root` is the
  addressable context library, `context.system_world` selects the instance-wide
  baseline, and `rig context work-install` reports System World, topology, and
  project inputs together.
- **Manage skills as their own resource.** `skills.root` names one versionable
  catalog. `rig skill loadout` composes system, topology, and project selectors;
  its apply mode owns only its manifest-listed projection and refuses to erase
  local or modified content.
- **Prime each runtime at the right width.** Provider-shaped onboarding gives
  Codex a compact bootstrap plus addressable coverage map while retaining the
  fuller guided route for runtimes that benefit from it.

## Lifecycle and recovery honesty

- **Create a deliberately blank occupant for one seat.** `rig seat launch
  <seat> --fresh --reason <why>` is the explicit no-continuity path; it preserves
  sibling seats and durable work and refuses unmanaged ambiguity.
- **Compile authored work into an executable lifecycle.** `rig workflow
  compile` reads `project.yaml`, `mission.yaml`, and `slice.yaml` as one graph;
  `instantiate-lifecycle` starts an eligible graph with an opaque replay key,
  and typed acceptance evidence prevents a workflow advance from standing in
  for release acceptance.
- **Know what a restore attempted.** Snapshot selection can be explicit,
  snapshots can retain the intended seat roster, and `rig restore status`
  derives the current intended-set result while keeping historical nodes and
  unverified resume lineage out of a false success.
- **Keep automation attributable.** Watchdog reminders deliver the authored
  message under an explicit scheduler identity, and effective-model detection
  follows the identity-verified current occupant rather than a retained
  predecessor session.
- **Choose judgment only where it earns the loop.** The shipped
  `agent-operated-workflows` skill distinguishes AI-enabled software,
  agent-operated workflows, and agent-operated software. The 0.5.9 instance
  migration is its first reference implementation.

## Upgrade and setup notes

- Root, CLI, daemon, and web UI package versions advance to `0.5.9`. The
  terminal TUI keeps its independent `0.1.0` version.
- Database migration head advances from `078_idle_gate_fired_condition` to
  `079_workflow_lifecycle_parallel`; normal daemon startup applies it.
- Existing instances have a deliberate layout boundary: context telemetry moves
  to `state/context-usage`, provider telemetry lives at
  `state/provider-usage`, the addressable library moves to `context/`, and the
  default System World lives at `context/system/system-world.yaml`.
- Do not perform that change as a directory rename while an old collector is
  writing. Load the shipped `openrig-upgrade` skill and follow its 0.5.9
  Agent-Operated Migration: inspect, prepare with a retained preimage, activate
  the exact target runtime separately, verify paired canonical samples, then
  invoke the non-destructive library finalizer with that exact receipt. The
  complete command sequence and rollback contract are in the top-level README.

## Known limitations

- The migration helper deliberately does not stop or start the daemon, mutate
  the database, relaunch seats, or delete legacy telemetry/library state. Those
  lifecycle and eventual-retirement decisions remain explicit operator work.
- A restore attempt receipt derives what the durable event and current process
  evidence can prove; missing or ambiguous native identity remains unresolved
  instead of being guessed.
- The TUI remains a terminal surface. Font choice and terminal color rendering
  stay under the user's terminal emulator rather than OpenRig.

## Release verification

- The accepted product candidate is exact commit
  `102dabce4ea56d870243ecd3f6ef38185ec76537`, tree
  `4b7898b6829bd3e28113bfd996f67bb1cc2761e9`, with independent whole-outcome
  evidence for the composed source heads and focused QA on the final TUI repair.
- The build VM ran the accepted candidate as a healthy, clean daemon. SQLite
  integrity passed, and the 0.5.9 migration verifier reported a complete fresh
  canonical Claude telemetry pair with no legacy tails.
- Release preparation additionally rebuilds the exact versioned cut, scans the
  complete npm inventory for private substance, installs the frozen tarball in
  isolation, and binds its runtime identity and public capability reads to the
  cut. Those receipts travel with the private publication packet.

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.8
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.8 — recoverable operations and visible work

OpenRig 0.5.8 makes long-running rigs easier to recover, understand, and
operate. It adds exact selected-rig recovery after an abrupt outage, makes the
current mission and its execution story visible to agents and operators, and
tightens the diagnostics and guardrails that keep live state honest.

## Recovery and topology lifecycle

- **Recover the selected rig after an outage.** Restore now rejects stale
  native identity, uses real provider-session evidence, and avoids substituting
  a fresh or wrong occupant or starting unrelated sibling rigs.
- **Use one topology-creation path.** Public creation and growth converge on the
  same daemon effect while preserving member working-directory overrides.
- **Keep topology declarations useful.** Rigs expose honest self-description,
  workspace declarations survive export, and a validated workspace declaration
  can be applied to an existing rig without changing its topology.

## Mission and context visibility

- **Open mission execution from SCOPES.** A selected mission now shows a
  readable `DONE` / `NOW` / `NEXT` / `ATTENTION` story, truthful working-lane
  and evidence-gap counts, bounded overflow, and stable mission switching.
- **Install the work that is actually current.** Work-install resolves complete
  files and dot-form slice IDs, and refocus derives the seat's typed current
  mission and slice instead of asking the agent to reconstruct them from
  memory.
- **Discover shipped capability.** The public capability world and its
  addressable context are available through the installed context routes.

## Operational honesty and safer setup

- **Wake once for the state that needs attention.** Park timers retire on every
  exit path, new park episodes supersede old timers, and idle-gate watchdogs use
  the same arbitrated activity oracle as the rest of the system.
- **Diagnose the mechanism that is actually live.** Producer-link health derives
  from effective endpoints, topology freshness is bounded, and synthetic model
  records no longer create false model-divergence findings.
- **Preserve user-owned Codex configuration.** Managed TOML projection refuses
  malformed or root-scoped fragments before write and preserves user tables
  across valid collisions.
- **Keep upgrades agent-led.** The shipped upgrade skill supplies bounded
  inspection, verified database backup, and contained managed-plugin refresh
  helpers while leaving cutover judgment with the operating agent.
- **Trust clean-checkout results.** The documented daemon test gate and the
  same-SHA long-lived gate now agree on deterministic source truth.

## Operator / setup notes

- Root, CLI, daemon, and web UI package versions advance to `0.5.8`. The
  terminal TUI keeps its independent `0.1.0` version.
- Database migration head advances from `077_node_session_source` to
  `078_idle_gate_fired_condition`; normal daemon startup applies it
  automatically. No manual migration step is required.
- Existing rigs do not need a topology rewrite. The new workspace-only apply
  path deliberately leaves members, pods, edges, and running sessions alone.

## Known limitations

- Selected-rig recovery does not cover total database plus filesystem loss or
  fleet-wide automatic restart.
- The existing-rig workspace story does not validate `target_repo`; that
  separate concern remains outside this release contract.
- A pre-existing backend `attention_required` state is not part of the bounded
  TUI topology-freshness work.

## Release verification

- Independent QA and review exercised the final SCOPES execution journey at
  110 and 160 columns, including mission selection, readable evidence gaps,
  bounded overflow, slice drill-in, and Escape navigation.
- Recovery testing used real Claude and Codex occupants across current, stale,
  absent, and insufficient-evidence states. It also covers native-session
  identity changing within the same OpenRig occupant record.
- The accepted product tree was replayed as a linear public lineage rooted on
  0.5.7. Every author and committer uses the project noreply identity, and the
  replayed product tree is byte-identical to the accepted local-main tree.
- Release acceptance includes package assembly, a hash-bound per-file
  substance review, and installed-runtime QA and review against the exact
  private cut.

body.name: v0.5.7 — elastic topology and coherent work delivery
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.7 — elastic topology and coherent work delivery

OpenRig 0.5.7 makes a running topology easier to create and reshape without
hand-authoring YAML, and gives agents a coherent, addressable install of the
work they are joining.

## Elastic topology lifecycle

- **Create without YAML.** Start a rig from public CLI inputs without first
  authoring a RigSpec.
- **Grow the topology in place.** Add one or several members to an existing
  pod, or create and populate a new pod, with mixed outcomes reported
  honestly.
- **Keep the declaration faithful.** Spec show/export preserves the topology,
  including a member's declared agent-image source, so save and recreate do
  not silently change how that member launches.
- **Shrink safely.** Removal refuses while a target owns active work. An
  explicit drain fallback preserves queue-item identity and state, verifies
  that the fallback session is live, and removes only the intended seat or
  pod. Ordinary no-work cleanup remains direct.

## Coherent work delivery

- **Composable product-journey SDLC.** The shipped work model composes world,
  project, mission, and slice context instead of requiring one monolithic
  briefing.
- **Useful work-install defaults.** Fresh project, mission, and slice
  scaffolds provide conventional Markdown and manifest files without
  overwriting authored content.
- **Optional YAML enrichment.** A project manifest can add an authored intent
  and ordered context addresses. Invalid optional values warn explicitly and
  retain the safe default install.
- **Addressable Markdown loading.** Installed skills can resolve precise
  Markdown sections by relative address, including through normal symlinked
  plugin projections.
- **Explicit project identity.** Agents can select and switch between projects
  without carrying context across roots; ambiguous, duplicate, and unknown
  identities refuse instead of guessing.
- **Complete public plugin-only skill catalog.** Every cataloged public skill
  supplied only by a plugin is projected with the helper files its
  instructions reference.

## Verification performed

- Targeted Node 22 daemon and CLI lifecycle/work-install suites and affected
  package builds passed throughout the surviving release range, with
  independent QA and scope/maintainability review at the completed user-story
  boundaries.
- The product cut at `14e785197` was packaged and installed in an isolated VM.
  Daemon health reported that exact clean commit, SQLite `quick_check` passed,
  and the existing ready topology was preserved across cutover.
- Disposable public CLI journeys covered create, grow, faithful export,
  guarded shrink, explicit drain fallback, and project/mission/slice work
  installation. A fresh agent session reconstructed the current five-piece
  work frontier through the installed command without cross-project leakage.
- A bounded TUI smoke opened the live topology, exercised help and basic
  navigation, and exited cleanly.
- The final release-note-only cut carries no product-source change from the
  validated product cut. Its package assembly, hash-bound surface review, and
  substance-gate receipt are release-manager gates that must pass before tag or
  publication.

## Operator notes

- Database migration head is `077_node_session_source`; normal daemon startup
  applies the ordered migration list automatically. No manual migration step
  is required.
- Run the exact-cut substance gate and retain its durable receipt before any
  tag, GitHub Release, or npm publication. Candidate QA does not imply those
  publication acts occurred.

## Known limitations

- Restore-honesty and disaster-path work are deferred to 0.5.8.

body.name: v0.5.6 — world-building as context engineering
body.body:
# v0.5.6 — world-building as context engineering

OpenRig 0.5.6 ships the context system's next layer, makes long-running
agents durable, and makes messages to humans trustworthy. Three themes: the
context a seat runs on is structured, tagged, and verifiable; an agent seat
can now outlive its own context window without a human managing the
transition; and anything routed to a human carries proof of delivery.

## The context system: structured, tagged, verifiable

- **The mission install.** A documented five-layer convention
  (`docs/reference/mission-install.md`) for installing project context into a
  seat: the pieces, their arrangement, the seat's own position, the current
  contract, and a derive-your-own-delta step that proves the install was
  consumed rather than skimmed.
- **Lore routing.** What a seat learns locally routes into addressable,
  rig-local lore packs (`docs/reference/lore-routing.md`) — carried with a
  maturity stage from birth, and structurally excluded from anything that
  ships.
- **Taxonomy everywhere.** Every pack entering `rig context` carries its
  class — WORLD / LORE / SKILLS / MISSION — surfaced in listings, with a loud
  refusal for untagged packs.
- **A public world pack with checkable claims.** The public onboarding pack
  is authored as atoms whose claims each carry a check that can fail, with
  the verifier shipped inside the pack — public content that cannot rot
  silently.
- **A complete, self-retrievable skill index.** The skill router's index now
  covers the full shipped set, is retrievable through the routes it teaches,
  and carries a recurrence test so coverage gaps stay found.
- **A substance gate for what ships.** A whole-surface review pass over every
  packaged file (bundle and npm surfaces included) runs as a named release
  step; this release shipped with all 5,316 packaged files passing.

## Continuity: seats that outlive their context windows

- **Continuity policies in the agent spec.** `compaction_strategy` is now live
  configuration with four modes: `default-compaction`, `managed-compaction`,
  `handover`, and `apprentice-handover`. Modes apply to Claude seats
  (positive runtime matching — Codex seats keep their native behavior) and
  resolve through the same spec-default < profile < member precedence as the
  rest of the agent spec.
- **The apprentice handover, automated.** A seat declaring
  `apprentice-handover` gets two armed triggers: near its context threshold,
  the system creates a fresh successor seat and runs its onboarding install;
  nearer the wall, it mints an owned handover work item for the seat that
  executes the swap. The executing seat is declared configuration (`mechanic:` on the
  policy) — never inferred from topology, and arming refuses loudly if it is
  missing.
- **Managed compaction with honest restores.** Seats in `managed-compaction`
  mode get a pre-compaction prep nudge (deposit your state before the window
  closes) and, after a configured restore, a durable receipt recording how
  much usable context the restore actually recovered — so a restore that
  silently refills the window instead of recovering width is visible.
- **Context-usage triggers as a primitive.** `rig watchdog` gains a
  usage-threshold condition: fire any command when a seat's context usage
  crosses a calibrated per-seat threshold. The continuity modes are built on
  it; your own automation can be too.

## The human layer: delivery you can prove

- **No more silent fall-through.** One destination resolver classifies every
  dispatch: terminal-bound seats use the terminal; registered humans and
  virtual seats route through the gateway; nothing falls through to a
  terminal lookup that cannot succeed. Unregistered external addresses get a
