  structured, teaching refusal.
- **Delivery receipts on the work item.** Every gateway post writes its
  receipt atomically on the queue row: `posted` (with the message timestamp
  and channel), `transport-failed` (with the error), or — derivably —
  `never-posted`. `rig queue undelivered` now consults that ledger first and
  returns only genuine failures. "Did this reach them?" is one read.
- **Notification levels, one vocabulary.** Queue transitions classify as
  `RECORD` < `NOTICE` < `ALERT` at write time — a human-required decision is
  `ALERT`; system ceremony events are `NOTICE`; the rest is durable record.
  Two independent dials configure the minimum level that posts and the
  minimum level that interrupts.
- **A delivery-rules engine.** Stored per-human preferences and availability
  decide how each message class is delivered. An `off` preference suppresses
  interruption — never the durable record, the post, or the receipt. Away
  windows defer routine traffic into digests (4-hour and daily), with
  exactly-once delivery by construction: durable episode identities, retry
  until a real receipt, and structurally non-overlapping digests.
- **Files dropped in Slack become work.** A file or image upload lands as a
  work item with the file transferred to local storage and referenced by
  path — authenticated download, size-bounded, per-file failures named, and
  no URL or token ever written to a row. A park blocked on a registered human
  automatically enters the alert path and posts exactly once per episode.

## Operational honesty

- A rate-limited seat gets exactly one timed wake at its stated reset.
- A seat holding claimed live work while sitting idle gets woken by the
  system, consuming the arbitrated activity oracle — with exactly one wake
  per park episode.
- Refocus state keys to the current occupant of a seat; a fresh occupant
  never inherits a predecessor's baselines.
- `rig ps` counts claimed in-progress work as assigned work.
- Sends refuse empty bodies; unknown daemon API routes return JSON 404s.
- Stuck-sweep findings stop re-minting after closure; cross-host custody
  verification completes durably instead of refreshing forever.
- Blocker actuation is unified: one helper, cross-host closure honest,
  delivery after the transaction commits.
- Rig expansion and serialization preserve what they were given:
  `session_source` versions, `services`, and member overrides survive
  round-trips; fork forwards model, role, restore policy, and label.
- `rig view show execution` derives who is building what, what is next, and
  each item's completion rung (locked / built / reviewed / folded / adopted)
  at read time — unknowns render as INDETERMINATE, never as idle or done.

## Process and reference

- The SDLC conventions document is now a component menu: choose per mission
  from the simple flow, the wave model, or the rigorous overlay, with
  planning rigor as a dial. Four full references ship at `docs/reference/`:
  `planning-dial.md`, `wave-sdlc.md`, `release-boundary.md`, and
  `product-management-pass.md`, joined by `mission-install.md` and
  `lore-routing.md`.

## Upgrade notes

- Three database migrations apply automatically on daemon start:
  `074_context_usage_watchdog`, `075_context_usage_watchdog_generation`, and
  `076_owner_notification_levels`. No manual steps.
- Context packs: 41 ship (up from 39).
- Delivery defaults are deliberately wide open (post at `NOTICE` and above,
  interrupt at `ALERT` and above). Tune down from measured volume with the
  two dials rather than pre-filtering.
- Continuity modes are opt-in per seat; unconfigured seats keep today's
  behavior exactly.

body.name: v0.5.5 — the ambient-attention release
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.5

## Summary — "The ambient-attention release"

**v0.5.5 makes the fleet notice, retry, escalate, diagnose, and onboard on its own.** Stop hand-babysitting the work in flight: `rig parked` diagnoses silent-stuck with confidence and teaching; the standing stuck-sweep runs without you; baton wakes retry, aggregate, and escalate on their own; parks carry their own wake and read HEALTHY; `rig ps` grows a typed `ACTIVITY` column from one oracle; the Slack human layer is live end-to-end; fresh installs onboard themselves.

**v0.5.5 contains v0.5.4 in full.** One reconciled lineage.

**Migrations**: TWO new. Head advances `071` → `073`:
- `072_thread_seat_map.ts`
- `073_queue_transition_wakes.ts`

**New verbs**: `rig parked [seat]`, `rig seat handover --source fork:|rebuild` (execute path), `queue block --on <blocker>` (park-with-wake), `rig gateway human` fragment-lifecycle verbs, `rig view show escalations`. `rig ps` gains a typed `ACTIVITY` column.

## What Shipped

### `rig parked [seat]` — derived silent-stuck diagnosis

Activity × open obligations, with per-input confidence and remedy taught inline. Reach for it when a seat looks idle and you suspect dropped work — before any `claimedAt` arithmetic or pane capture. The row face used to hide the difference between park and strand; this verb ends that.

### Self-retrying wake ladder + escalations view

Failed baton wakes retry, aggregate, and escalate on their own. Transitions ARE the ladder state (restart-safe); per-destination aggregation; rungs deliver-and-advance; unconfirmed-with-no-pickup escalates without re-send. Watch `rig view show escalations` for the aggregates. Hand off the row and stop chasing nudges.

### Standing stuck-sweep runs without you

Overdue + undelivered become routed findings with derived evidence inline. Stop hand-running `queue overdue` / `undelivered` on a timer — consume the sweep's findings instead.

**Caveat (5.6 backlog):** cross-host successor visibility is a proven false-positive class — 39 active findings at census (20 proven FP, 19 unverified). Contained fleet-wide one-per-condition; treat cross-host-lineage findings as unverified until the 5.6 detector fix. The delta itself teaches the caveat.

### `queue block --on <blocker>` — park-with-wake

A park can carry its wake and read HEALTHY. `queue block --on <blocker-qitem>` records the wake; held-with-live-wake is not flagged; auto-unparked owners get an honest wake. For imminent-but-blocked work only; not-imminent work belongs in the mission workspace — the queue is a conveyor.

### `rig ps` gains a true `ACTIVITY` column from one oracle

Typed taxonomy: working / idle-at-prompt / needs-input-as-count+reason / unknown. Evidence ladder with self-report on top and visible rung degradation. Seat-keyed across swaps. The TUI reads the same truth. For any "is it thinking or stuck" question — the oracle beats capture.

### `rig seat handover --source fork:|rebuild` — EXECUTE

`fork:` carries live context; `rebuild` primes from the durable chain and names its priming artifacts. Mid-swap failures record honestly. When replacing an occupant — no more dry-run-only planning surface.

### Slack human layer live end-to-end

Gateway running, thread-per-seat, exactly-once inbound reconciliation, escalation loudness (mention) distinct from routine. Humans are addressable members; `rig gateway human` has full fragment-lifecycle verbs. Any agent can escalate directly; escalation-class sends arrive loud on the destination's phone.

### Fresh installs onboard themselves

Fresh installs get focused onboarding packs by default (config off; existing rigs untouched). When standing up a new rig or seat — stop hand-walking the eight pieces.

### Refocus fires only when it should

At a context threshold or on demand — NEVER at session start. Post-compaction both runtimes; usage threshold Claude-only. A fresh seat getting a refocus is now a bug to file, not noise to ignore.

### One-file scope convention

`scope mission create` → `NOTES.md` + intent-bearing `SPEC`; `slice create` → `SPEC`-only (no `IMPLEMENTATION-PRD`) + acceptance `PROGRESS`; release missions get a capability-delta scaffold. `repair` is ADDITIVE — stamps append, never rewrite author frontmatter. Stamp verification is a mechanical strip again.

### Daemon bind intent has provenance

An inherited `OPENRIG_HOST` never selects single-bind; adoption gates test ALL required listeners. Daemon maintenance from any managed environment — no more `env -u` ceremony.

## STOP doing (each was correct under 0.5.4 and is wrong now)

1. **STOP the per-lock author-reconstruction protocol.** Stamps APPEND now; strip-reconstruction is mechanical.
2. **STOP diagnosing parks by `claimedAt` arithmetic + capture.** `rig parked` derives the diagnosis with confidence and teaching; capture is a fallback glance.
3. **STOP storing deferred work as queue rows.** The queue is a conveyor for imminent sequential work; deferred work lives in the mission workspace.
4. **STOP authoring `IMPLEMENTATION-PRD.md` and `MISSION_NOTES.md` on new work.** `SPEC.md` is the one spec file; `NOTES.md` is the chain name.
5. **STOP routing contact through an orchestrator by default.** Any agent escalates directly.

## Landed, not yet drivable

| Landed surface | Missing live door | Honest current action |
|---|---|---|
| A–D delivery preferences + availability (stored, validated) | rules engine (0.5.6 slice 01) | set availability via `rig gateway human` verbs; expect no routing effect yet |
| S01 operator rung | human-layer connector delivery leg (0.5.6 wave S11 territory) | escalation view + daemon health carry the floor |
| `@external` addresses on the direct send path | routing falls through to tmux (0.5.6 wave-2 fix) | reach humans via the gateway path (queue/escalation), not raw `rig send` |
| Multi-human topology | single-human ships (honesty marker); multi-human is 0.5.7 | one registered human; design assumptions accordingly |

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — two new: `072_thread_seat_map.ts`, `073_queue_transition_wakes.ts`. Head advances `071` → `073`.
- **API compatibility** — existing commands remain available; new verbs are additive.
- **Lineage** — the 0.5.5 product delta is reconciled onto the published 0.5.4 line by aggregate patch identity.
- **Release boundary** — tag, npm publish, host install, and daemon cutover remain separate authorized acts.

## Known Limitations (0.5.6 backlog)

- **Cross-host stuck-sweep false positives** — 39 active findings at census (20 proven FP, 19 unverified); contained fleet-wide; detector fix lands in 0.5.6 wave 1.
- **`@external` direct-send routing** — 0.5.6 wave-2 routing fix.
- **Delivery preferences → rules engine** — 0.5.6 slice 01.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the `[0.5.5]` entry.
- `docs/releases/v0.5.4.md` — the prior honesty release.
- GitHub Release: https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.5

body.name: v0.5.4 — the honesty release
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.4

## Summary - "The honesty release"

**v0.5.4 makes command output describe the effect that actually happened.** Transport resolution distinguishes missing, found, and indeterminate sessions. Delivery verification distinguishes staged input from an agent-consumed turn. Queue, refocus, lifecycle, import, and preview surfaces preserve real state and refusal semantics instead of collapsing them into plausible success.

**v0.5.4 contains v0.5.3 in full.** The VM cut was reconciled onto the published line by an ordered 32-of-32 stable patch-id match.

No new migrations. Migration head stays at 071 (matching v0.5.3). Node engine requirements are unchanged. Existing CLI commands remain; this release adds `rig seat set-model`, `rig seat stop`, and `rig seat clean`.

## What Shipped

### One classified session-resolution path

Send, capture, nudge, and walk consume one probe result: found, absent, or indeterminate. A tmux or transport blip no longer becomes a false `Session not found`, and recovery output says what was checked.

### Delivery verification by effect

`rig send --verify` checks whether input remained staged or was consumed as a turn. Single-target, fan-out, and JSON output use the same classification, so "typed" and "delivered" are no longer synonyms.

### Honest unknown-sender delivery

Messages without attributable sender identity are delivered with an unknown-sender label instead of refused. Where possible, the sender receives a notice to follow up with attribution.

### Supported single-seat lifecycle controls

- `rig seat set-model` changes the canonical model binding with an audited reason.
- `rig seat stop` stops one live seat without disturbing siblings.
- `rig seat clean` removes dead-session residue so the logical seat can launch again.

Safety is whole-class: every session a lifecycle action could mutate is probed, and a live or indeterminate result refuses the action. The model change was exercised through a real managed successor.

### State-preserving queue and refocus behavior

Queue notes preserve the row's state. Owned listing without identity refuses instead of silently widening or changing scope. Refocus keeps due state until delivery becomes visible. Preview and handoff output say when content is bounded or optional.

### Running-name guard across create and import

A running rig name cannot be recreated through another instantiator or import route. Every path preserves the same `409 rig_name_running` code and teaching message through the CLI boundary.

### Hermetic startup and plugin authority

Scratch/test startup boundaries are hermetic. The bundled `openrig-core` plugin advances under explicit version authority, preventing an older runtime from silently rolling installed guidance backward. Stale lab refocus registrations are retired.

## Behavior and Compatibility

- **Migrations** - none; schema head remains 071.
- **API compatibility** - existing commands remain available; three seat lifecycle verbs are additive.
- **Lineage** - the 0.5.4 product delta is reconciled onto the published 0.5.3 line by patch identity.
- **Release boundary** - tag, npm publish, host install, and daemon cutover remain separate authorized acts; this document does not imply that they occurred.

## Known Limitations (0.5.5 backlog)

- **Writer-layer disk cap** - cleanup is an interim control; the permanent write-layer cap is unfinished.
- **Repair/approve frontmatter rewrite** - the known rewrite defect remains open.
- **Observation pipeline performance** - the larger pane/process polling redesign remains measurement-gated and is not claimed by this release.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` - the `[0.5.4]` entry.
- `docs/releases/v0.5.3.md` - the prior context release.
- GitHub Release: https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.4 (created only after the authorized publish ceremony).

body.name: v0.5.3 — the context release
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.3

## Summary — "The context release"

**v0.5.3 puts context on rails.** Pull exact sections of shipped skills and library entries by address instead of reading whole files. Discover context by asking, not by guessing paths. Refocus resolves refs automatically. Handovers write a durable, superseded-chain seat recap that lands in every restore packet. Composition is by reference, so there is no second copy to drift.

**v0.5.3 contains v0.5.2 in full.** One lineage, no divergence.

No new migrations. Migration head stays at 071 (matches v0.5.2). Nothing to apply on a v0.5.2→v0.5.3 upgrade. No CLI-command or flag removals or renames from v0.5.2.

## What Shipped

### Address grammar for context: `rig context get` (headline)

Pull the exact bytes of one section:

```
rig context get <pack-ref>/<file>#<H2-slug>[/<H3-slug>]
```

The `/<file>` component is required even in a one-file pack. Refs are canonical full paths (e.g. `skills/<namespace>/<name>`). A bogus slug fails loud and lists the addressable sections. `rig context list` enumerates every shipped entry's ref and name; `rig context show` inspects one. Cross-source access (`seat:` / `mission:` atoms) is an **authoring** affordance — declared in pack manifests and granted via `rig context profile --rig/--seat/--mission` during composition — not an ad-hoc argument to `get`.

### `openrig-skills` router — ask → ref → load

The router teaches the three-step: ask your question, get a ref, load by ref. Use it when you don't know which skill or context applies, or nothing is projected after a cold boot.

### Durable seat recap — `rig context recap-write`

Handover time, compaction boundary, or any moment your successor would otherwise re-derive your state from scrollback: `rig context recap-write` maintains a seat-scoped `RECAP.md` beside `LEARNED` with a collision-safe superseded chain. Restore packets now carry an authored-recap pointer.

### Refocus resolves refs automatically

The refocus hook resolves library refs automatically (ref beats file), fails loud but non-blocking, and delivers pointers. This is the shipped channel for pointing running seats at new content.

### Bounded expertise packs on demand

`rig context get` serves expertise packs by path-like ref, e.g. `skills/process/context-engineering`. The old `context-pack:` colon form was removed and the CLI says so.

**Caveat that pack:** it is titled "Traditional Context Engineering — 2024-2025 Snapshot" for a reason — provisional, historical, non-normative by founder ruling. Current OpenRig skills, explicit user rulings, and measured practice outrank it on any conflict.

## STOP doing (was correct under 0.5.2, is wrong now)

1. **STOP copying library content into seat or mission files to compose context.** Compose by ref: addressing means there is no second copy to drift. Nothing catches the copy automatically; it is still a defect by rule.
2. **STOP treating a `MODEL DIVERGENCE` proclamation as alias noise.** The canonicalize-then-compare fix ended the pinned=fable / effective=claude-fable-5 false-positive class, and the monitor now isolates per-seat throws. A proclamation on this runtime is a real escalation — act on it.
3. **STOP reading "founder-gated" in tool errors as an authorization wall.** The overstated wording is retired from the scripts; those guards demand explicit paths (e.g. `OPENRIG_SKILL_CANON_ROOT`), not permission. The real founder boundary is exactly: pushes and PRs. Local commits and ordinary apply work never need founder word.
4. **STOP hand-placing evidence or trusting a placeholder PRD as the proof contract.** `rig proof add` pairs evidence to the contract, and a pristine scaffold PRD can never silently become that contract: the authored SPEC serves with a named advisory (`contractSource` in the echo tells you which source bound).

## Landed but not yet drivable

Eval CASES ship (14 selection/loading cases), but no runnable grading pass exists today. `--provider rig` is the live proof-contract door and is NOT YET DRIVEN — it says so itself and redirects to fake (the wiring is the convergence-test driver work in flight). `--provider fake` replays only transcripts supplied via `--transcripts <map.json>` and errors every case without one. When the live door is driven, the next release promotes this to a capability.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — none in this release. Migration head stays at 071 (matches v0.5.2). Nothing to apply on a v0.5.2→v0.5.3 upgrade.
- **API surface preserved** — no CLI-command or flag removals or renames from v0.5.2.
- **v0.5.3 contains v0.5.2** — one lineage, no divergence.

## Known Limitations (5.4 backlog)

- **Reply-hint self-qualify** — carried from 5.2; reply-hints on some cross-host messages address themselves via machine-ID rather than registered host name. Substitute the registered host name from `rig host list`. Fix in 5.4.
- **Eval grading pass** — CASES ship; no runnable grading pass yet. Driven `--provider rig` lands in 5.4.
- **`rig send --verify` does not detect staged-unsent** for multi-line sends toward Claude seats — carried from 5.2 backlog.
- **Claude transcripts thin under fullscreen upsell** — carried from 5.2 backlog.
- Plus internal debt items ledgered for maintenance.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the `[0.5.3]` entry.
- `docs/releases/v0.5.2.md` — the prior release (test system in earnest + crash-cart conductor).
- GitHub Release: https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.3

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.2 — test system exercises for real + crash-cart fleet-restore conductor
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.2

## Summary — Test system exercises for real; crash-cart conductor; reliability fixes

**v0.5.2 puts the v0.5.1 test system to work.** The reliability fixes in this release were found and validated by scenarios that drive the real product through the same commands a person uses. The headline lands: a crash-cart fleet-restore conductor that takes you from a dead daemon to a truthful cockpit and back to a live fleet with one keystroke.

**v0.5.2 contains v0.5.1 in full.** One lineage, no divergence.

No new migrations in this release. v0.5.1 already shipped migrations 068-071 (with 068 and 071 as a matched create / drop-if-exists pair, net no-op for any v0.5.0→v0.5.1 upgrade). v0.5.2 stays at migration 071. No CLI-command or flag removals or renames from v0.5.1.

## What Shipped

### Crash-cart fleet-restore conductor (headline)

Type bare `rig` at a dead daemon and reach a truthful cockpit — no cryptic error, no silent failure. One Enter restores the fleet kernel-first, adopts any surviving tmux panes (never clobbers them), and presents an exact per-seat remediation walkable in one keystroke. Cancel is honest. Destructive restore is only offered when adoption cannot succeed. Ten build rounds, four independent gates, non-author QA door test.

### Daemon event-loop no longer hangs under load

A class of daemon event-loop freeze under load is fixed and measured. If your daemon was going unresponsive under fleet-wide activity, that's this class.

### Unattended Claude seat handover

When a Claude seat needs to hand over (compaction, session boundary, explicit handover request), the outgoing seat now writes a recap and submits its packet automatically — the incoming seat picks up with the recap in hand rather than a cold start. Door-proven end-to-end.

### `rig policy` handles adversarial input honestly

Malformed or hostile policy input now produces honest structured errors rather than silent failure or unexpected behaviour. Three review rounds.

### Cross-host messages carry their machine of origin

Messages sent across hosts now include the machine they came from, so multi-host coordination reads correctly at the receiving end. Enforced end-to-end via door tests.

### Codex model-config drift detector

A new detector for a class of Codex model-config drift that would previously go unnoticed. Caught real cases on landing.

### Test-integrity work

- Test runner refuses to run against a dirty tree — a green run now means green source, not accidentally-uncommitted state.
- Hermetic test roots.
- Flaky fixtures isolated.

### Governance in code

Plan locks are explicit (chosen when you ask for one), not inherited from ambient state. Wake is opt-in.

### Container tar-file hang eliminated at the seam

A class of container tar-file hang is dead by construction — not worked around, but the seam that made it possible is closed.

## Known Limitations (5.3 backlog)

Ledgered honestly for the next release cycle. Named so you know what's not yet fixed:

- **Reply-hint self-qualify** — reply-hints on some cross-host messages address themselves via machine-ID rather than registered host name; using the reply-hint directly may fail with "no registered host X". Substitute the registered host name from `rig host list`. Fix in 5.3.
- **`rig queue handoff --summary`** warns yet the field is unsettable on its own output. Fix in 5.3.
- **`rig send --verify` does not detect staged-unsent** for multi-line sends toward Claude seats. Multi-line sends can stage silently.
- **Claude transcripts thin under fullscreen upsell** — upstream fullscreen upsell writes `"tui":"fullscreen"`; one accepted prompt can re-flip a fleet. Fix + pin + prevention in 5.3.
- **Test runners can silently skip on unbuilt trees** — a final-gate rule (build CLI + assert zero skips) is adopted for the release ceremony; the product-side fix lands in 5.3.
- **`seat-handover` model-fidelity real-Codex end-to-end** fails identically on main (environment-vs-product distinction unrooted). Isolation fix in 5.3.

Plus a handful of internal debt items ledgered for maintenance.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — none in this release. v0.5.1 shipped 068-071 (068 CREATE + 071 DROP-IF-EXISTS pair, net no-op for v0.5.0→v0.5.1 upgraders); v0.5.2 stays at 071.
- **API surface preserved** — no CLI-command or flag removals or renames from v0.5.1.
- **v0.5.2 contains v0.5.1** — one lineage, no divergence.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the `[0.5.2]` entry.
- `docs/releases/v0.5.1.md` — the prior release (a test system for the product + reliability fixes).
- GitHub Release: https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.2

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.1 — a test system for the product, plus reliability fixes
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.1

## Summary — A test system for the product, plus reliability fixes shipped through it

**v0.5.1 gives the product a test system.** Scenarios drive the real product through the same commands a person uses, so it can prove its own behaviour without a human checking by hand. The reliability fixes of this window ship through the test system — proving its value on its first cycle.

**v0.5.1 contains v0.5.0 in full.** One lineage, no divergence.

Migrations are additive only. Existing v0.5.0 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon. No CLI-command or flag removals or renames from v0.5.0.

## What Shipped

### Test system

- **Stub runtime for tests** — a fake agent runtime that scenarios can drive. Lets scenarios exercise the daemon end-to-end without needing a real Claude or Codex process.
- **Scenario format + runner** — a text-based scenario format and an executor that runs scenarios against the real product. Includes a real fix that surfaced from writing the runner: text-matching against a pane or transcript could never match its two intended surfaces; now it does.
- **Seed scenarios** — three seed scenarios that run green end-to-end against the real product. See Known Limits below for the seed-scenario one that could not be built.

### Container test bed — scaffolding

**Scaffolding for container mode** ships: argument builders, image-identity stamping, runbooks, and a unit suite. **The runner does not yet execute in containers** — this is scaffolding you will see in the tree but that no test currently drives. Container-mode execution is scoped forward.

### Reliability fixes (shipped through the test system)

- **Honest render for daemon transport failures** — the operator sees the actual failure rather than a silent no-op or generic error.
- **Queue-persistence** — two fixes ensuring queue records reflect what actually happened after they were written.
- **Cross-machine send regression** — found and fixed during verification. This is the test system doing its job: proving product behaviour across machines and catching a regression before release.

### Small features

- **Per-agent model from spec** — each agent's model comes from its spec rather than a fleet-wide default, so different agents can run on different providers or models.
- **Token usage tracked over time** — the daemon records token use so operators can see trends and predict when a seat is approaching a usage limit.
- **Machine-of-origin on messages** — messages carry the machine they came from, so multi-host coordination is legible.

### Other

- **UI timing hardening** — UI tests no longer fail on load-timing flakes.
- **Queue records tell the truth after they are written** — a class of wrote-it-and-it-did-not-stick issues closed.
- **Unreached-message visibility** — show messages that never reached an agent. On landing, this surfaced nine real handoffs that had been silently lost since 8 August.

## Known Limits

- **Container mode is scaffolded but not driven.** You will see the seam, argument builders, image stamping, runbooks, and a unit suite in the tree, but no test currently executes in a container. Scoped forward.
- **Seed scenarios: three of the intended set run green.** The tenth cannot be built without two capabilities that do not yet exist in the product (a scenario cannot mutate the running system's shape; the terminal interface exposes navigation state rather than fleet inventory). Both capabilities are scoped forward.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — additive only. Existing v0.5.0 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **API surface preserved** — no CLI-command or flag removals or renames from v0.5.0.
- **v0.5.1 contains v0.5.0** — one lineage, no divergence.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the `[0.5.1]` entry.
- `docs/releases/v0.5.0.md` — the prior release (mission control TUI + context library + permission policies).
- GitHub Release: https://github.com/mvschwarz/openrig/releases/tag/v0.5.1

body.name: OpenRig v0.5.0 — Mission control TUI + context library + permission guarantee + provider usage
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.5.0

> **UI posture (unchanged from v0.4.7):** the web UI is in **maintenance mode** — still ships, still runs, no new feature work. **CLI/TUI is the primary surface.** v0.5.0 lands the TUI (`rig` / `rig tui`) as the new mission-control home.

## Summary — Mission control in the terminal + context library + permission policies + provider usage + honest CLI

**Mission control in the terminal.** Typing `rig` (or `rig tui`) opens the new TUI: file-tree navigator, dense agent detail (working directory, runtime, context %), a topology graph with the whole fleet on one screen, honest status/activity language, motion design, working scrolling, and honest width-clip indicators throughout.

**v0.5.0 includes everything from v0.4.8.** There is no divergence between the two releases — the v0.4.8 permission-posture work and shipped skills are all present in v0.5.0.

Migrations are additive only. Existing v0.4.8 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.

## What Shipped

### Permission-policy built-ins + agent-driven translation

Building on the v0.4.8 permission-policy foundation, v0.5.0 ships **the built-in policy templates plus the agent-driven skill that translates them into the target harness's live config**.

- **Four built-in policy templates** — `locked`, `standard`, `open`, `yolo`. Read-only from the package; copy to customize. Plus `none` as a deliberate no-policy choice.
- **`rig setup --policy <name>`** — records the chosen policy into a rig spec. Takes a built-in name (`locked | standard | open | yolo | none`) or a path to a custom policy file (custom policies live as `.policy.md` files you author).
- **`applying-a-permission-policy` — bundled skill for the translation.** At rig setup / preflight, the skill reads the policy spec, checks the seat's current harness version, shows the concrete diff before writing, and lands the config into Claude `~/.claude/settings.json` and/or Codex `config.toml`. Never blind writes. The translation is agent-driven on purpose — harness permission formats change frequently across versions, so a deterministic writer would break the moment the harness surface shifts.
- **Two surfaces** — the **launch-flag** surface (Claude `--permission-mode`, Codex sandbox/bypass, Pi `--approve` / `--no-approve`) is stable and OpenRig-set for you: the floor (Claude `acceptEdits`, Codex workspace-write) and the full-bypass YOLO mode. The **config-file** surface (Claude `~/.claude/settings.json`, Codex `config.toml`) is where the allow/ask/deny rules live and where the skill applies your chosen policy.
- **What's deterministic vs best-effort** — the launch-flag floor and YOLO are deterministic. Fine-grained config-file rules are best-effort because harness rule grammars vary; the skill surfaces the caveats to you (prefix collisions, target-first leaks, Claude's lack of a native network gate) via the diff-before-write flow. If a translation is uncertain, you can always fall back to hand-editing the harness's own settings file, or to YOLO / floor as blunt instruments.

### Permission-writer guarantee, now test-pinned

v0.5.0 upholds the v0.4.8 promise — **OpenRig never writes permission entries into your Claude `settings.json`** — and pins it with a permanent guard test plus an empty-writer sweep. The one sanctioned exception is the project-local `acceptEdits` floor that v0.4.8 itself defines. Warning-ordering during permission-policy discovery is cleaner (pre-existing main-floor warnings first, then policy-attachment warnings); presentation-only, semantic fence unchanged.

### Context library

`rig context` stores and composes context; `rig walk` delivers it paced; `--context` / `--body-context` attach a stored context (by reference) to `rig send` / `rig broadcast` / `rig queue create`. Grammar is strict: **nouns store and compose** (`rig context` never delivers on its own); **verbs deliver** (`rig send`, `rig broadcast`, `rig walk`, or `rig queue create` via `--context` / `--body-context`). The old context-window usage viewer from v0.4.x is removed; the `rig context` name now belongs to the library.

### Behavior change (v0.4.8 → v0.5.0)

`rig.yaml` startup `context_pack` entries are no longer delivered at rig instantiation. **They are rejected with a teaching error pointing you at `rig context compose` + a delivery command.** Users who adopted `context_pack` in a `rig.yaml` on v0.4.8 (shipped days ago; small window) should compose the pack via `rig context compose` and then deliver it with a delivery command — `rig send --context`, `rig broadcast --context`, `rig walk`, or `--context` / `--body-context` on `rig queue create`. The bundle router still stores the pack; it just doesn't auto-deliver it at startup.

### Provider usage observability

The daemon tracks account-level usage per host — the "am I about to hit a usage limit" question — exposed via `GET /api/provider/usage` and `rig provider status`. Explicit-unknown when the provider doesn't report it; conflict-shows-both-facts when signals disagree. Codex account-switch flows are preserved.

### Plan amendment done right

`rig scope slice approve --re-approve --reason "..."` re-stamps a locked plan with an append-only audit trail — replacing an earlier workaround where an already-approved status forced a `Status`-note edit.

### Honest CLI output

- `rig ps` says when it is showing one rig of many, rather than silently limiting.
- `rig send --json` returns structured errors as `{fact, consequence, action}`.
- Activity-hook fix ends the fleet-wide "producer link stale" advisories that were firing on every send. Operator-facing quality improvement.

### Build discipline

Contributor gates and lanes have a single source of truth at `docs/reference/developing.md`.

### UI status (unchanged from v0.4.7)

The web UI stays in maintenance mode as introduced in v0.4.7 — still ships, still runs, no new feature work. CLI/TUI is the primary surface, and v0.5.0's TUI (`rig` / `rig tui`) is where mission-control investment lands going forward. The UI is not deprecated and not removed; existing deployments continue to work.

### Bundled skills

Two new bundled skills join the shipped set alongside the v0.4.8 skills:

- `applying-a-permission-policy` — agent-driven translation for permission policies (see the Permission-policy section above).
- `delegating-work` — distribution guidance for every seat.

The `openrig-user` skill is updated with the v0.5.0 context-library grammar (`rig context compose`, `rig walk`, `--context` / `--body-context`).

## Known Issues

- **Codex `HOME` fix not landed in v0.5.0** — a permission-posture fix that ensures the daemon and Codex seats agree on the `HOME` environment (so the posture writes reach the seat) was accepted for v0.5.0 but was inadvertently omitted from the shipped build. It ships as an early bug-fix in v0.5.1. In the meantime, the v0.4.8 deployment note applies: **the daemon's `HOME` must equal the seat's tmux `HOME`** for the permission-posture writes to reach Codex seats — verify this on any remote-host upgrade.

## Upgrade Notes

- Migrations are additive-only; run `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- Any `rig.yaml` still declaring a startup `context_pack` will see the teaching-error rejection above; migrate to `rig context compose` + a delivery command.

body.name: OpenRig v0.4.8 — Permission-posture fast-follow
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.8

## Summary — Permission-posture fast-follow

Launch posture is configurable, the deny set writes at a level that project-local approvals can't override, and dangerous operations are gated by explicit prefix rules that actually hold under the current harness.

Migrations are additive only. Existing v0.4.7 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.

## What Shipped

### Configurable launch posture

The hardcoded `--permission-mode acceptEdits` launch flag is replaced by a configurable posture defaulting to `dontAsk`. This closes the class of freezes where an autonomous seat could get stuck on a modal permission prompt with nobody to click through it. `dontAsk` is the default because it matches what an autonomous seat can actually respond to; `acceptEdits` remains selectable when a seat needs the prior behavior; a deliberate `bypassPermissions` value is preserved untouched across writes.

### Deny set that project-local approvals can't override

The posture writes to user-level `~/.claude/settings.json` instead of the project-local approval file. **Deny wins over project-local approvals** as a result. Writes are additive (never destructive to sibling keys) and forward-migrate a legacy `acceptEdits` value into the new schema. A deliberate `bypassPermissions` value is preserved.

### Bounded-dangerous deny set

Four dangerous operations are gated by default: `git push`, `gh pr create`, `npm publish`, and `rig down`. `rig down` in particular is gated via the prefix rule `Bash(rig down:*)` — the current Claude harness (2.1.220) only supports prefix matches on Bash rules, and flag-only patterns provably don't gate target-first forms like `rig down <rig> --force`, so the prefix rule is the only shape that actually holds. Plain `rig down` is gated in v0.4.8; selective allowance (e.g. `rig down <rig>` for a specific target) is deferred to v0.5.0 server-side enforcement.

### `rig up` un-gated

The prior release's ask-gate on `rig up` is removed — `rig up` is a reversible operation and doesn't warrant an interactive gate.

### Permission-policy foundation (built-ins land in v0.5.0)

- **Harness-neutral policy schema.** The permission-policy spec is a harness-neutral surface with `default_posture`, `floor`, and `allow` / `ask` / `deny` expressed as **semantic actions** (`push_to_remote`, `force_push`, `delete_files`, `read_secrets`, `create_pr`, `publish_package`, and so on) rather than raw shell-command patterns.
- **`rig setup --policy <name>`** — a new flag on `rig setup` records a permission-policy choice into an existing rig spec. Takes a built-in name or a path to a custom policy file. The **built-in policy files themselves land in v0.5.0**; v0.4.8 ships the framework that consumes them.
- **Two surfaces.** The **launch-flag** surface (Claude `--permission-mode`, Codex sandbox / bypass flags, Pi `--approve` / `--no-approve`) is stable and set by OpenRig for you — this is where the floor and full-bypass YOLO live. The **config-file** surface (Claude `~/.claude/settings.json`, Codex `config.toml`) is where allow/ask/deny rules live; because harness rule grammars change frequently across versions, this surface is applied interactively by an agent-driven skill (that skill ships in v0.5.0 as `applying-a-permission-policy`).

## Deployment Note (operators read this)

For the posture writes to reach seats, **the daemon's `HOME` must equal the seat's tmux `HOME`**. This is a Claude 2.1.220 settings-path invariant that matters for the remote-host leg of any upgrade:

- On a local-only host, this is typically satisfied automatically.
- On a remote-host upgrade, verify HOME parity between the daemon process and the tmux seat process before treating the upgrade as complete.

(v0.5.0 documents this as a Known Issue for Codex `HOME` divergence; the product fix ships in v0.5.1.)

## Superseded

An initial v0.4.8 attempt (with `dontAsk` baked as a **platform default** rather than an OpenRig-side default) was withdrawn on final review; the shipped v0.4.8 is a re-scoped permission-agnostic base plus a policy-spec system. Nothing from the withdrawn attempt shipped.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — additive only. Existing v0.4.7 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **Default launch posture** — changed from hardcoded `acceptEdits` to configurable, default `dontAsk`. If a seat needs the prior behavior, select `acceptEdits` explicitly.
- **Deny-set write location** — user-level `~/.claude/settings.json`; the deny set wins over project-local approvals. Writes are additive.
- **`rig up`** — no longer ask-gated; reversible operations don't warrant interactive gates.

body.name: OpenRig v0.4.7 — Recovery honesty + starter bootstrap + skills wave + Slack + UI maintenance-mode
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.7

> **⚠️ Milestone:** v0.4.7 is where the **web UI moves to maintenance mode**. The CLI is the primary product surface from this release forward; the web UI still ships and still works, but is no longer receiving new feature work. If you drive OpenRig from a browser today, plan a transition to the CLI (and, from v0.5.0 onward, the terminal TUI: `rig` / `rig tui`). See the UI section below for the specifics that ship in 0.4.7.

## Summary — Recovery honesty + starter bootstrap + skills wave + Slack connector + UI maintenance-mode

**Recovery honesty is the through-line.** On a resumed restore, the startup sequence now loads a seat's applicable skill preloads before the role-defining first message — so a resuming seat knows its skills before it starts working. Compaction recovery is honest: transcript ingest exposes degraded states explicitly, and a post-compact restore-and-audit is gated on the seat being idle so "restore-sent" actually means "delivered". Daemon liveness reporting is honest — a dead seat drops effective running to 0 and reports `attention_required`; `rig send` and `rig capture` return an explicit "session missing" error when the seat is gone. CLI probes report uncertainty honestly — an unconfirmable status returns `UNKNOWN` with no false start advice, and a confirmed-stopped seat fails with actionable guidance.

Migrations are additive only. Existing v0.4.6 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.

## What Shipped

### Starter bootstrap

Product-team starter bootstrap is cleaner, and starter seats get a skill preload on both fresh-start and restore. Default culture loads at startup, and rig specs are audited at load time. **Rigs instantiated before v0.4.7 need re-instantiation** (or spec-level patching) to pick up the starter fixes — the loader and audit changes apply immediately, but starter-spec content lands at instantiation.

### Skills wave

The bundled skill layer gains public routing and a default projection, plus public-skill strip and mirror controls, plus a plugin fix that keeps the documented skill count honest. The bundled skill inventory grows substantially, from a handful to broad coverage across core, PM, pod, and process families.

### Slack connector + human queue

First-class Slack connector shape (CLI `rig slack` commands + supporting library). Hosted create crosses an inconclusive local probe to the real configured-daemon result.

### CLI contract honesty

`--json` errors, flag validation, and scoped overdue behavior are tightened for machine-readable use.

### UI — moved to maintenance mode

**The web UI is frozen at this release in maintenance mode.** The wording is CLI-primary — never "deprecated"; the UI still ships and still runs, but it is no longer receiving new feature work, and CLI/TUI is the primary surface going forward. What lands in v0.4.7 to make this explicit to users:

- A dismissible in-app banner in the web UI announcing the maintenance-mode status.
- A `rig ui open` stderr notice at launch time, so operators driving the CLI see the status before they open the browser.
- Documentation positioning updated across README and user-facing docs.

Existing v0.4.6 deployments keep working; nothing is removed. The substantive product investment shifts to the CLI and, from v0.5.0, the terminal TUI.

### Queue, topology, review polish

- Queue compact-list rows mark elided fields so "omitted" is distinguishable from "empty".
- Nested Approve posts a missions-root-relative scope path.
- Mission review card composition is polished.
- Unverified delivered items read "artifact-recorded" rather than "nothing delivered".
- The drawer file viewer resolves inline in-body images via the file-asset API.
- Proof-of-work Markdown links open in the in-app drawer.
- Docs guard encodes the root-placement rule for `docs/DESIGN.md`.

### Host sizing guidance

Recommended: add swap on the host, and plan for roughly ~2 GB RSS per seat as an observed baseline.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — additive only. Existing v0.4.6 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **Rig-spec starter behavior** — the loader and audit changes apply immediately; starter-spec content lands at rig instantiation. Rigs instantiated before v0.4.7 need re-instantiation (or spec-level patching) to pick up the starter fixes.
- **Seat-liveness API** — consumers should key seat liveness off the honest lifecycle state (updated every few seconds) rather than the older session-status field, whose staleness cleanup is tracked for a subsequent release.
- **Web UI posture** — frozen in maintenance mode; no CLI surface breakage. Nothing is removed from the UI at this release.

body.name: OpenRig v0.4.6 — workflows + multi-host + factory
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.6

## Summary — Workflows + multi-host coordination + factory foundations

OpenRig v0.4.6 lands the deterministic workflow engine and the
multi-host coordination model that runs on top of it. Workflows are
now a first-class product surface: a rock-solid engine, a full-
featured spec language, a workflow CLI, a workflow web UI, and an
exception + human-gate maturity model that keeps a healthy run
zero-interruption. On top of that engine, the self-driving factory
starter ships as an MVP shipped starter (`rig up factory-rsi`) —
one rig, seven seats, a self-driving `plan → implement → qa_check
→ review → release` inner loop with dogfood decoupled and running
out-of-band against the shipped product, feeding recorded findings
into the next plan.

Multi-host coordination lands the full happy path. Hosts register
and select through dashboard-visible cards; a remote host's
workspace surfaces are readable from the local operator; queue
items and hot-potato handoffs cross hosts explicitly through the
registered transport (never a silent selection re-home); the direct
coordination verbs (`rig send`, `rig capture`, `rig transcript`,
`rig broadcast`) cross hosts CLI-direct via the shipped http
transport branch with byte-verbatim ssh behavior preserved; a
fleet-altitude attention band rolls up needs-attention across the
whole registered fleet.

Foundations round out the release: a new agent runtime adapter (Pi)
joining Claude/Codex as a first-class runtime, terminal provider
first-class treatment across the terminal-facing surfaces, and
daemon read-path hardening for the multi-host + workflow load with
no functional behavior change.

Two new bundled skills ship canonical + plugin with byte-parity
guard: `openrig-herdr` (rig terminal open/views/status model) and
`openrig-cmux` (provider-agnostic delta).

Migrations are additive only: `049_workflow_instance_version`,
`050_workflow_spec_json`, `051_workflow_resume`,
`052_workflow_instance_bound_rig`, `053_sessions_node_id_index`,
`054_queue_transitions_archive`. Existing v0.4.4 databases upgrade
by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon. (v0.4.5 was
skipped; there is no cut between v0.4.4 and v0.4.6.)

## What Shipped

### Workflows

- **The rock-solid deterministic engine** — strict spec validation
  (unknown keys reject; unreachable steps and unguarded cycles
  fail); `loop_guards.max_hops` enforced at projection; waiting-
  exit replay absorption; per-instance keepalive watchdogs auto-
  armed in the routing transaction; startup sweep re-arms and
  surfaces stuck instances; `rig workflow continue` relabeled to
  its read-only inspector semantics.
- **The full-featured spec language** — steps with role /
  target.rig / preferred_targets / next_hop.on / invariants /
  loop_guards / exception_routing / closure / gates / skill_refs /
  spawn_budget; strict-keyset validation; shipped-spec compat
  pinned by fixture round-trip.
- **The workflow CLI** — new verbs `rig workflow run` (instantiate
  + follow to terminal; exit 3 = workflow-failed distinct from
  transport 1/2), `rig workflow watch` (mid-flight attach),
  `rig workflow status` (needs-attention rollup), `rig workflow
  route` (frontier re-target in one transaction). Formatted
  `trace` / `list` / `show` human output; `--json` byte-identical
  to before. New guard rejects out-of-band terminal closure of a
  live workflow-frontier packet.
- **The workflow web UI** — new
  Workflows/Instance/InstancesBand/TopologyGraph/InstanceTrailTimeline
  pages; SSE stream unscoped by rig; pure `buildLauncherViews` +
  `suggestLayout` + edge-handle assignment exports. UI acceptance
  is carried by per-cut real screenshots + the two-host
  integration proof; twin fixture backfill is routed as a
  non-blocking 0.4.7 hygiene fast-follow.
- **The exception + human-gate model** — `rig workflow resume`
  verb (redrive a failed instance from its failed step, rebound,
  fresh capability-aware re-resolution, one fresh `max_hops`
  window); exceptions become durable attention items in the same
  transaction as the failure; maturity dial `orchestrator-first |
  human_only` per class / per workflow / per host; the attention
  band is workflow-aware; the happy-path guarantee is unchanged.

### Multi-host coordination

- **Add / select hosts + dashboard** — `HostConfigCard` +
  `HostIndicator` surfaces on the dashboard; `rig host select`
  persists a sticky selection consumed by the observe/interactive
  verbs; new `useHosts` / `useFleet` hooks.
- **View remote workspace** — workspace observability tabs gain
  `--host <id>` scope; registry + bearer fans out per-host reads.
  Read-only.
- **Cross-host queue routing** — `rig queue create / handoff /
  handoff-and-complete` gain `--host <id>` + host-qualified
  destination form `member@rig@<host>`. Explicit-only routing.
  At-least-once + idempotent via deterministic successor id;
  handoff creates successor FIRST + closes local SECOND; retries
  absorb on primary key. Failure honesty per host outcome.
- **Cross-host agent coordination** — `rig send` + `rig capture`
  gain an http transport branch reaching the remote daemon's
  existing `/api/transport/send|capture` routes CLI-direct;
  `rig transcript` + `rig broadcast` gain their first cross-host
  affordance the same way. The `agent@rig@host` target form is
  CLI-edge sugar for session-target verbs. Byte-verbatim ssh
  behavior preserved for ssh-registered hosts; explicit `--host`
  > target sugar > selection; `send --verify` over http prints
  the REMOTE route's verdict verbatim.
- **Fleet-attention altitude** — fleet-wide attention rollup via
  `FleetBand` + `FleetPage`; per-host status + drill-down.

### Factory

- **The workflow-to-rig binding layer** — bind a workflow to a rig
  at instantiation via `--rig`; roles resolve to seats by
  capability; capable-seat resolution honors managed-only,
  harness-pin-aware runtime match, least pending backlog,
  deterministic tiebreak; resolve-once, record-in-the-packet;
  roles bind to the stable seat coordinate `{pod}-{member}@{rig}`
  (agent handover behind the seat never strands the workflow).
- **The self-driving factory starter (`factory-rsi`)** — new
  `rig up factory-rsi` starter; new `factory-rsi` builtin
  workflow with a `plan → implement → qa_check → review →
  release` inner loop sanctioned by `loop_guards.max_hops`;
  dogfood decoupled + running out-of-band against the shipped
  product with its findings feeding the next plan (the RSI edge,
  ungated in the MVP — refined in a later release); publish stays
  a human act via `release_signoff` gate.
- **The member-exists advisory + cross-rig wrapping** —
  mis-routed workflow destinations caught loudly at instantiate;
  cross-rig wrapping workflows travel via the cross-host queue
  routing path.

### Runtime + terminal + read-path

- **Pi agent runtime adapter** — a new first-class runtime
  joining Claude/Codex; participates in all workflow / role /
  queue / send / capture surfaces exactly like the shipped
  runtimes.
- **Terminal provider first-class treatment** — terminal provider
  first-class treatment across the terminal launcher,
  send/capture/broadcast, and the new `openrig-cmux` skill's
  `--provider cmux` seam with best-effort fallback.
- **Daemon read-path hardening** — SSE stream backpressure
  guards, projection caches, additive indices for read-side query
  performance. No functional behavior change; the same reads
  return the same results, faster.

### New bundled skills

- **`openrig-herdr`** — the full rig terminal open/views/status
  model (verbs, view grammar, honest-partial reading, read-only
  policy, terminal-views.yaml schema). AGPL clean-room rail — no
  herdr source text vendored.
- **`openrig-cmux`** — the provider-agnostic vs cmux-specific
  delta with shipped-integration open-or-focus rule.

Both ship canonical + bundled openrig-core plugin, byte-parity
guarded.

## Migrations

Additive only:

- `049_workflow_instance_version` — optimistic concurrency on
  `workflow_instances`.
- `050_workflow_spec_json` — full parsed spec cached on
  `workflow_specs`; legacy rows self-heal on next read-through.
- `051_workflow_resume` — `resume_count` + `hops_baseline` on
  `workflow_instances`.
- `052_workflow_instance_bound_rig` — nullable `bound_rig` TEXT
  on `workflow_instances`.
- `053_sessions_node_id_index` — additive index.
- `054_queue_transitions_archive` — archive table for read-side
  query performance.

Existing v0.4.4 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on
the new daemon.

## Known Follow-ons

- **Save-verb** did not land in 0.4.6; rides 0.4.7.
- **Twin fixture backfill** for the new workflow + multi-host UI
  routes routed as a non-blocking 0.4.7 hygiene fast-follow; UI
  acceptance for the cut carried by per-cut real screenshots + the
  two-host integration proof.
- **Continuous out-of-band dogfood runtime** — the factory-rsi
  RSI edge ships ungated in the MVP; the continuous mechanism is
  refined in a later release.
- **Carry-forwards from 0.4.4**: `openrig-user` bundled plugin
  stale-copy sweep, `whoami --all-hosts` silent host filter,
  managed-stop SIGTERM-escalation brittleness, post-cutover
  reconcile-settle-visibility signal on `/healthz`.
- **iOS Safari** (Living Notes composer verification) —
  carry-forward from 0.4.4.
- **Wider mission-template prose sweep** — post-cut sequencing.

Full technical detail lives in
[CHANGELOG.md](../../CHANGELOG.md#046---2026-07-09).

# OpenRig v0.4.4

## Summary — Multi-host + Living Notes

OpenRig v0.4.4 lands the multi-host foundation: a shared rig topology
can now span multiple hosts, with a staged spin-up flow, real cross-
host file movement, and a consolidated For-You activity feed that
merges signal across every host in the topology. The VPS product-
factory story hardens for real multi-host operation.

Alongside the multi-host foundation, this release ships the **Living
Notes signal layer** — a durable, agent-authored notes surface that
threads INTENT → PLAN → DELIVERED down the mission tree, with a
one-structure review contract that reads left-to-right as a single
vertical stack (INTENT above, PLAN in the middle, DELIVERED at the
bottom; delete-not-demote when a plan changes). Composer surfaces make
authoring cheap; the review surface makes reading intent-versus-build
one-glance.

Operator UX picks up **`rig ps` consolidated default** (the token-
efficient-defaults family gains progressive disclosure that keeps the
default view glanceable without hiding the fleet), an **agent altitude
coordination panel** that surfaces multi-agent state at the right
altitude for the operator, and the **operationalize-SDLC control
plane** which pulls the release / delivery / lifecycle levers into a
single control surface. As-built docs closeout catches everything up.

Migrations, if any, are additive. Existing v0.4.3 databases upgrade by
running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.

## What Shipped

### Multi-host foundation

- **Shareable whole-topology staged spin-up** — a rig topology can be
  brought up in stages across multiple hosts; the spec + the daemon
  coordinate to reach a green whole-fleet state without requiring a
  single-host bring-up. Prior to this release, a whole-topology spin-
  up assumed a single host.
- **VPS product-factory multi-host hardening** — the shipped
  `openrig-user`/`openrig-architect` operator flows work correctly
  across VPS/self-hosted product-factory scenarios; multi-host
  handshake + registration hardens.
- **Multi-host consolidated For-You feed** — the For-You feed
  aggregates activity across all registered hosts in the topology, not
  just the local daemon. The stream classifier + real-data fidelity
  from 0.4.3 apply per-host and merge upstream. A real-host feed-
  subscription capture ships as belt-and-suspenders proof (see
  Known Follow-ons).
- **`rig file` cross-host movement** — files move across the
  topology's registered hosts via the `rig file` surface. Real
  registered-host two-host end-to-end round-trip proves the flow on
  top of the VM stand-ins already merged.

### Living Notes

- **Signal layer** — a durable, agent-authored notes surface at
  mission and slice altitude; INTENT / PLAN / DELIVERED entries thread
  down the mission tree with agent authorship + timestamps.
- **Composer surfaces** — cheap authoring surfaces make Living Notes
  the first-class place agents record decisions, plans, and delivered
  work.
- **One-structure review contract (§3.1) — corrective rebuild** — the
  Living Notes review surface reads left-to-right as a **single
  vertical stack** (INTENT above, PLAN + mockup in the middle,
  DELIVERED with paired proof at the bottom); a plan change **deletes**
  the old plan and writes a new one — never demotes / stacks multiple
  competing plans. The corrective rebuild replaced an earlier
  three-column layout after human review.

### Operator UX

- **`rig ps` consolidated default + progressive disclosure** — the
  default `rig ps` now consolidates the fleet's readable rows into a
  single glanceable default; progressive disclosure via `--full` /
  `-A` / per-scope filters keeps the rich per-node record retrievable.
  Follows the token-efficient-defaults family established at 0.4.0.
- **Agent altitude coordination panel** — a coordination surface
  scoped to the right altitude (workspace / mission / slice) so the
  operator sees the actual coordination state without drowning in
  per-seat detail. Composes with the workspace observability tabs
  shipped at 0.4.1.

### Doctrine

- **Operationalize the SDLC control plane** — release / delivery /
  lifecycle levers pull into a single surface. The lanes that shipped
  0.4.1 → 0.4.3 (release-cut squash + bounded-diff, sidecar-operator
  host cutover, curation pass) are now first-class control-plane
  actions rather than lifecycle-tribal-wisdom.
- **As-built docs closeout** — the as-built documentation family
  (`docs/as-built/architecture.md`, `docs/as-built/cli-reference.md`,
  codemaps) is caught up to what shipped through 0.4.4.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — additive only. Existing v0.4.3 databases upgrade
  by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **Multi-host registration** — the multi-host handshake is
  backward-compatible with single-host deployments; single-host
  operation is unchanged.
- **`rig ps` default view** — the consolidated default is a
  compact readable view; `--full` returns the v0.4.3 default shape.
- **For-You feed** — multi-host feed aggregation is opt-in via
  registered-host membership; a single-host topology sees no
  behavior change.

## Known Follow-ons

- **R2 — iOS-Safari S20 (Living Notes composer)** — deferred to
  0.4.5 for iOS Safari verification.
- **R4 — S18 symlink footgun** — routed to the 0.4.5+ backlog.
- **`openrig-user` stale plugin copy + `whoami --all-hosts` silent
  host filter** — 0.4.5 candidates.
- **Wider mission-template prose sweep** — post-cut sequencing.
- **Belt-and-suspenders real-host proofs** — R13-1 (published-npm
  Linux install smoke + daemon-start / `/healthz` / WebSocket
  handshake), R1 (real registered-host two-host e2e for S13 + S18 on
  top of the merged VM stand-ins), and R3 (S15 real-host feed-
  subscription capture) are sequenced as post-publish lifecycle
  validation lanes. The shipped code was already proven via VM/SSH
  stand-ins per PM rulings; the real-host lanes are defense-in-depth
  belt-and-suspenders proofs, not release gates.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the standard changelog entry for `0.4.4`.
- `docs/releases/v0.4.3.md` — the prior release ("rigs that
  survive").
- `docs/releases/v0.4.2.md` — the daemon-status hotfix.
- `docs/releases/v0.4.1.md` — the workspace observability overhaul.

body.name: v0.4.3 — rigs that survive
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.3

## Summary — "rigs that survive"

OpenRig v0.4.3 makes rigs actually survive. Crash the daemon or the whole
machine — turn the power off, not a graceful stop — and on reboot the
seats come back to their **original** sessions, with their pre-crash
markers recalled, zero fresh-prime. The proof is a real hard power-off
capstone (`Tart stop --timeout 0` → reboot → `rig start` → both Claude
and Codex seats resumed to their originating conversations). This is the
load-bearing "rigs that survive" claim.

Alongside the survival backbone, the release ships the **deny-by-default
`rig send` reversal**: `needs_input` (an actual interactive picker) is
now the only hard send-refuse; unknown / stale / missing / busy all
advise-and-send. The 0.4.1 3-layer guard was too strict in practice —
0.4.2 hotfixed the daemon-status probe, and 0.4.3 corrects the send-guard
posture so peer coordination no longer needs a `--dangerously-interact`
bridge for routine sends. The genuine prompt block still stands.

Wave-2 UI lands rig-status + launch-control on the workspace, a
switch-client view-retarget, and a real theming system (Vellum Dark
opt-in; light stays byte-identical). Seat-handover full-cycle + seat-
forking closeout complete the recovery story. Doctrine ships too:
mission-slice-sop skill.

Existing v0.4.2 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the
new daemon. Migrations 045, 046, and 047 are additive.

## Survival — the load-bearing set

- **Crash-restore resume-token ledger (FR-3 → FR-7)** — the seat's
  resume marker is captured on adoption (FR-3), refreshed on snapshot
  (FR-4), pinned to a restore target (FR-5), freshness-gated with a
  1-hour advisory threshold + `--fresh` re-verify (FR-6 + FR-6.1
  periodic re-stamp), and — critically — the restore path never
  silently fresh-primes a seat that had a resume marker (FR-7). Prior
  to FR-7, a restore that couldn't reach the token would degrade to a
  fresh-prime, losing the original session identity; that silent
  degrade is now eliminated.
- **Fixture-home isolation guard** — a fresh-prime that would have
  clobbered a live rig's home dir is refused loudly, not silently
  swallowed.
- **Liveness PID-verify** — the daemon distinguishes a live seat from a
  dead-PID ghost by verifying the process actually exists before
  labeling the seat running.
- **Daemon event-loop health + terminal broker resilience** — the
  daemon publishes an event-loop-latency health signal; the
  `TerminalSessionBroker` recovers cleanly across daemon restarts.
- **Startup-proof** — a seat proves it actually read its orientation
  material rather than skipping past it; a challenge-verified read
  path.
- **Seat-handover full-cycle** — an outgoing seat can hand its captured
  context to a fresh successor; the resume marker carries automatically
  via FR-3; the loud-unwind path fires on both lanes when handoff
  fails.
- **Seat-forking closeout** — the fork lifecycle terminates cleanly on
  the shared checkpoint; predecessors and successors are named + wired.

## The deny-by-default reversal (`rig send`)

The 0.4.1 3-layer guard was too aggressive at the fleet level: unknown /
stale / missing / busy activity signals all default-blocked, which
required constant `--dangerously-interact --reason "..."` overrides for
routine peer coordination. 0.4.3 corrects this:

- **`needs_input` (a real interactive picker rendered on the target
  pane) is the only hard send-refuse.** The guard here is unchanged
  behavior at the actual footgun-point.
- **Unknown / stale / missing / busy** now **advise-and-send** rather
  than block. Peer sends land; the operator sees the advisory in the
  send output.
- **`--dangerously-interact --reason "..."`** override still exists for
  intentionally driving a prompted seat, unchanged.

Also improved: **Codex activity-signal hardening** — an idle Codex seat
now takes normal sends; the genuine prompt block still holds; hook-trust
autoclear lands as a fast-follow so a restored Codex seat clears its
attention-gate on restore.

## `rig send` unified targeting

`rig send` grows explicit multi-recipient targeting — a recipient list +
`--pod` + `--rig` — reusing the existing broadcast fan-out + per-
recipient guard. Backward-compatible: single-recipient send is
unchanged.

## Wave-2 UI + theming

- **Rig-status + launch-control UI** — the workspace surface for
  starting / stopping / recovering a rig lands. Combines the topology
  view with a launch modal for mixed-plan rigs.
- **Switch-client view-retarget** — clicking through a switch-client
  action lands the operator on the correct target view without a stale
  breadcrumb.
- **Dashboard theming — Vellum Dark opt-in** — a real theming
  primitive: `light` is the existing `:root` theme (byte-identical),
  `dark` is the first shipped alternate, and the substrate scales to
  N themes via the token-block + registry entry. Uses Tailwind
  `darkMode: 'selector'`. Light is unchanged.

## Recovery + operator-UX

- **Idle-gate watchdog** — an idle seat holding a claimable gate qitem
  gets woken with a bounded skip-recording so the queue doesn't back up
  behind a dormant seat.
- **Session-admin mutation auth-guard** — the admin mutation surface is
  no longer reachable without the correct auth posture.
- **`rig queue show` bounded body preview** — long queue-item bodies
  are truncated in the show view; the full body remains inspectable via
  the queue-item drawer.
- **Manual configurable compaction trigger + same-seat guard** —
  Claude Code seats can be prompted to compact from outside the seat;
  the trigger refuses a same-seat mutation.
- **Secret-boundary B1 hardening (`rig auth`)** — the `rig auth`
  secret boundary now opens the fd first + operates on the fd never
  re-resolving the path, closing the check-then-use gap for
  interruption / concurrent-legitimate-rig-process scenarios (the
  TOCTOU class is closed as a consequence). The `rig auth` file is a
  real credential; leak-hunt is real security, not theater.

## Doctrine + fast-follow

- **`mission-slice-sop` skill** ships — the per-file rules for
  `PROGRESS.md` / `PROOF.md` / `MISSION_NOTES.md` / `MISSION_BRIEF.md` /
  `README.md`, the SCAFFOLD/POPULATE/PROJECT/VERIFY lifecycle,
  hot-potato queue handoffs, and the `rig scope audit` backstop.
- **Hook-trust autoclear (fast-follow)** — a restored Codex seat that
  hits its attention_required VM-local hook-trust gate now auto-clears
  the attention on the restore path, mirroring slice-10, for
  fully-unattended Codex restore.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — additive only. `045_resume_verification`,
  `046_seat_identity_verdicts`, `047_events_node_type_index` land in
  this release. Existing v0.4.2 databases upgrade by running
  `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **`rig send` default posture change** — unknown / stale / missing /
  busy activity signals no longer default-block; only `needs_input`
  does. If you were relying on the 0.4.1 default-block posture, add an
  explicit guard on your call sites; the intent-signaling for peer
  coordination now lives in the fleet-standard advise-and-send path.
- **`rig send` grammar** — multi-recipient list + `--pod` + `--rig`
  are additive; single-recipient calls are unchanged.
- **Cosmetic Project surface** — Dashboard theming is opt-in via the
  UI toggle; light theme is byte-identical.

## Known Follow-ons

- **Slice-04 real-provider handover VM-marker** — code proven at
  runtime (unit + integration + loud-unwind both lanes); the real-
  provider end-to-end VM-round-trip is a **fast-follow proof capture**
  (VM-env limitation on prior provider auth). Not a claim gap; the
  load-bearing survival proof is the crash-restore capstone.
- **`rig ps` consolidated-default + progressive disclosure** — captured
  for 0.4.4 (token-efficient-defaults family evolution).
- **Deploy-identity: git SHA via `/healthz` + `rig --version`** — the
  version-truth-vs-commit-truth observability gap (captured for 0.4.4
  Discovery).
- **Managed-hooks-via-`requirements.toml`** — the robust structural
  hook-trust re-arch (later fast-follow).
- **Skill-layer cut depth (slice-25)** — awaits a decision on the
  load-bearing skill set; deferred.
- **Dashboard glyph swap (slice-24)** — awaits icon pick; deferred.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the standard changelog entry for `0.4.3`.
- `docs/releases/v0.4.2.md` — the prior release (daemon-status hotfix).
- `docs/releases/v0.4.1.md` — the workspace observability overhaul.

body.name: v0.4.2
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.2

## Summary

OpenRig v0.4.2 is a targeted hotfix for the CLI `daemon-status` probe's
false-negative window right after a `rig daemon start` / restart. On the
prior 0.4.1 build, the probe issued a single `/healthz` fetch per
`getDaemonStatus` branch; if the daemon process was up but the HTTP
listener had not yet begun accepting, the single probe lost the race and
`rig daemon status` reported a false "Daemon not running" /
"healthz failed" even though `/healthz` was returning `200`.

The fix wraps the three `getDaemonStatus` `/healthz` branches in a
status-probe-local bounded settle: max 5 attempts, 200ms backoff,
hard-bounded by construction. A genuine-down still fails all attempts
and is reported stopped / unhealthy after the budget — never masked,
never an unbounded wait. `fetchDaemonProbe` and start / stop / checkPid
timing are unchanged.

## What Changed

- **`rig daemon status` no longer false-negatives during the daemon's
  post-start listener-bind window.** The probe re-checks up to 5 times
  with a short backoff before it reports stopped, so a healthy daemon
  that is still binding its listener resolves as running / healthy
  instead of reporting a false down state.
- **Genuine-down reporting is unchanged.** If the daemon really is not
  running, all attempts fail and the probe reports stopped or unhealthy
  after the bounded budget — no hang, no mask.

## Files Touched

- `packages/cli/src/daemon-lifecycle.ts` — three probe branches
  (pid-alive `/healthz`, no-state `/healthz`, and the injected-probe
  wrapper) now go through `probeHealthzWithSettle`.
- `packages/cli/test/daemon-lifecycle.test.ts` — focused probe-layer
  tests: transient-then-healthy settles to running / healthy;
  pid-alive-but-never-answers stays `healthy: false`; genuine-down is
  reported stopped after the hard-bounded budget.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **No CLI surface changes.** All commands, flags, and arguments are
  identical to `0.4.1`.
- **No daemon / DB / migration changes.** Migration state is unchanged
  from `0.4.1`; no new schema migrations ship in this release.
- **No dependency changes.** `package-lock.json` is refreshed for the
  version bumps only.

Existing v0.4.1 databases are unaffected. Upgrading is simply
`npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.4.2` (or a package refresh) and a normal
`rig daemon` restart if the daemon is running.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the standard changelog entry for `0.4.2`.
- `docs/releases/v0.4.1.md` — the prior release.

body.name: v0.4.1
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.1

## Summary

OpenRig v0.4.1 is an observability + operator-UI overhaul: the workspace
becomes a developer's mission cockpit. Across the Project UI, altitude
projection (workspace → mission → slice) and a coherent tab set replace
the partially-built Project pages from v0.4.0. The Mission landing tab
shows steering + the human-facing mission brief. The Story tab
reconstructs what actually happened on a mission as a scrollable
git-graph derived from queue lineage. The Workflow tab visualizes the
configured workflow spec. The Artifacts navigator + Proof tab + Progress
heat-map give workspace altitude its own native surfaces. The Dashboard
route gets a clean cosmetic refresh as the launcher home.

Underneath: a UI digital twin renders all six real Project surfaces
1:1 daemon-free from typed fixtures so visual intent can be approved
before any UI slice is built, then proven against a real screenshot at
the end. A topology edge-flow animation surfaces real queue/handoff
movement on the topology graph (signal-driven, never decorative). The
For-You feed picks up a phone-friendly restyle with real-data fidelity.

New CLI: `rig auth` lands as a product-native, CLI-local Codex
auth-profile manager with a hardened secret boundary that refuses
symlink + hardlink escapes out of CODEX_HOME. `rig send` ships a 3-layer
interactive-prompt guard (default-blocked at a target pane's prompt;
`--raw` keystrokes still guarded; `--dangerously-interact --reason`
audited override) so a peer message can no longer accidentally select
an option in another agent's terminal.

Reliability fixes: a fresh `npm install -g @openrig/cli` followed by
`rig daemon start` now resolves cleanly (a missing `@hono/node-ws`
runtime dep was masked by monorepo hoisting on the dev host but failed
on a fresh install; the CLI now mirrors the daemon's full runtime
dep set, gated by a packaging-completeness test). Table-view + hybrid
terminal-action errors surface as visible alerts instead of silent
failures, and the table terminal opens. Queue items take a
human-readable `summary` field (additive migration 044; phased
WARN-on-author).

Existing v0.4.0 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the
new daemon. Migrations are additive (044 adds a nullable
`queue_items.summary` column; pre-0.4.1 items degrade cleanly to a
body-fallback label).

## Included In This Release

### New top-level CLI surface

- **`rig auth`** — product-native, CLI-local Codex auth-profile
  management. List / show / switch / capture / forget Codex profiles
  under a CLI-owned `~/.openrig/codex-auth/`, never reaching outside
  CODEX_HOME. The adversarial path is closed: a symlinked active auth
  is refused, hardlinks and symlinked parents cannot escape CODEX_HOME,
  and the secret boundary is integration-tested. Replaces the prior
  ad-hoc out-of-product Codex auth swap with a single first-class
  surface.

### `rig send` — interactive-prompt guard

A peer message can no longer accidentally pick an option or approve a
permission in another agent's terminal. Three layers:

- **L0 (default)** — `rig send` is **blocked** when the target pane is
  at an interactive prompt or permission block. Detection is
  hook-primary (Codex `PermissionRequest`) with a hardened capture-pane
  fallback (12-line trailing-content scan + 15-second send-readiness
  freshness).
- **L1 — `--raw`** — exact keystrokes; the L0 guard still applies.
- **L2 — `--dangerously-interact --reason "..."`** — explicit override,
  implies `--raw`, requires `--reason`, writes an audit row.

This closes the long-standing "stand-down message submitted an
authorize-publish default" footgun.

### Workspace observability tabs (the headline)

- **Steering tab (mission landing)** — Panel 1 projects `STEERING.md`
  (what agents are currently being told to do); Panel 2 projects the
  mission's human-facing `MISSION_BRIEF.md` derived from the new locked
  7-section schema. The landing tab when you click into a mission;
  Overview stays available.
- **Mission brief doc-type + projection** — a real canonical
  human-facing doc-type alongside `README.md` / `PROGRESS.md` /
  `MISSION_NOTES.md`. `rig scope init-workspace` /
  `rig scope mission create` emit a root `MISSION_BRIEF.md` from the
  7-section template (Brief / What & why / Building / Progress / Proven
  / Needs you / Pointers); backfill the same template into existing
  missions on demand. The Mission Steering tab renders it
  markdown → UI.
- **Story tab — queue-item DAG git-graph** — reconstructs a forest of
  DAGs from `chain_of_record` + handoff lineage as a scrollable,
  upward-growing git-graph. Single-parent edges only (no invented merge
  state); one-line rows over a curved gutter; full-width expanded row;
  a Tier-3 drawer reuses the queue-item viewer for the full agent-speak
  body + chain. Both mission and slice altitudes; client-side from the
  existing `/api/queue` read API (no new surface). The Queue tab folds
  into Story.
- **Workflow tab — spec visualizer** — finishes the half-built Project
  Topology tab into a real read-only visualizer of the configured
  workflow spec: dotted-grid canvas, dark-header step cards, per-step
  state dot, dagre LR layout, amber reject → rework loop-back. Label
  rename Topology → Workflow (test-id stays `project-tab-topology`,
  id-stable). Both mission and slice altitudes. Workspace-only; the
  standalone Topology page (NOC) is unchanged.
- **Proof tab** — per-slice proof galleries + empty-state for
  scaffolded-but-unpopulated slices. Reads from the slice's
  `proof/` directory + a `PROOF.md` summary if present.
- **Progress heat-map** — Project Progress tab consolidates to the
  heat-map (per-slice rollup cards retired); the heat-map carries
  status at a glance without the duplicate-card noise.
- **Artifacts navigator** — slice-altitude `ArtifactsNavigator`
  replaces the prior `SliceArtifactsTab` card wall; files and docs
  resolve through the same `/api/files/*` surface; the Proof tab owns
  proof artifacts; the Decisions surface routes through Story
  (decision-of-record items are already Story nodes).
- **Workspace portfolio** — workspace parent altitude renders a
  cross-mission portfolio panel: mission list with steering glance on
  expand, lazy `MISSION_BRIEF.md` fetch, rollup metric counts
  *proven* (from `hasProofPacket`) rather than `done`.

### UI digital twin + visual intent → proof convention

- **UI digital twin (harness)** — a derive-from-source twin renders all
  six real Project UI surfaces 1:1 daemon-free from typed fixtures
  (cache-seed + a thin fetch override + a seeded SSE stream; **not**
  MSW). One self-contained `intent.html` per surface; tsc
  compile-time drift-guard (a real interface change breaks the twin
