  build); ~2-step per-slice authoring loop; production-isolated
  dev-only target. Build any surface with
  `TWIN_ROUTE=<route> npm run twin:build`.
- **`rig scope` intent-visual slot** — `rig scope slice create`
  scaffolds a slice `README.md` that includes an
  `## Intent visual` slot with `[change.diff]` + the
  `TWIN_ROUTE=<route> npm run twin:build` rebuild command. A non-visual
  slice gets an explicit `N/A` line, so the slot is *present-or-N/A*
  per slice.
- **Visual intent → proof convention** — adopted alongside the
  harness: visual intent is approved as a twin mockup before build,
  then proven against a real screenshot at the end. The convention's
  twin-data-freshness condition (every brand-new UI surface has a twin
  fixture; data shapes match real) is folded into the release-close
  gate.

### Topology + For-You

- **Topology edge-flow animation** — when a real queue handoff or
  `rig send` travels an edge (source → destination), the edge animates
  in the handoff direction, brightens while live, then settles static
  after TTL. Honesty-contract held: animates **only** on a real
  queue / send signal (no workflow DAG, no ambient motion);
  un-signaled edges stay static; reduced-motion omits the flow.
  Topology-graph surface only.
- **For-You phone restyle + real-data fidelity** — the Dashboard
  restyle reaches For-You as a phone-friendly cards layout with an
  altitude-dial level filter (All activity → Highlights → Needs you,
  card set changes per level). The internal `source.type` wrapper
  string no longer renders in feed cards, and the vestigial
  storytelling-preview band above the filtered feed is removed (it
  ignored the level filters and visually masked the restyle).

### Reliability + correctness

- **Fresh-install daemon-start fix** — `@hono/node-ws` is now declared
  in the CLI package (the CLI vendors the built daemon and does not
  depend on `@openrig/daemon`, so its `package.json` must mirror the
  daemon's runtime deps for a global `npm install -g @openrig/cli` to
  resolve them). A monorepo-hoisting blind spot meant the dev host
  worked while a fresh install failed; a packaging-completeness gate
  now fails the test suite if a daemon runtime dep is not mirrored in
  the CLI.
- **Table / hybrid terminal-action reliability** — terminal-action
  errors surface as a visible cmux/auth alert instead of silent
  failure on the topology Table view + the hybrid surface; the Table
  terminal now opens cleanly.
- **Queue-item human-readable summary** — additive nullable `summary`
  field on queue items (migration 044). `rig queue create` +
  `rig queue handoff` gain `--summary` with WARN-on-author (warns if
  missing; does **not** hard-break existing callers — phased
  enforcement). The agent-speak body remains the source of truth and
  is inspectable in the queue-item drawer. The Story-row label prefers
  the authored summary and degrades cleanly to the body fallback for
  pre-0.4.1 items.
- **Seat-scoped post-compaction restore** — Claude Code seats get a
  scoped, idempotent restore packet derived from the JSONL transcript;
  the post-compact agent rebuilds its working mental model from
  durable evidence rather than fuzzy recall.
- **Table-view crash fix** — null-safe TanStack filter + an
  `ErrorBoundary` on all three topology Table mounts (host / rig /
  pod) so a single bad row no longer takes down the page; regression
  test added.
- **Dashboard route refresh** — cosmetic visual overhaul of the
  welcome / home launcher route (paper-draft launcher grid + six
  cards + Field Environment + drafting footer). Pure cosmetic; the
  six launcher routes + card test-ids preserved.

### Conventions adopted

- **Visual intent → proof** — the digital-twin convention is adopted
  with three ratified parts: derive-from-source twin (no MSW), one
  `intent.html` per surface, and twin-data-freshness as the residual
  release-close check.
- **Release-durability close — AC-9 (skill-cascade integrity)** —
  `rig skill audit` clean for the shipping set, every drift edge
  green, and bundled plugin reconciled to canonical modulo declared
  transform. Condition 2 (drift edges) remains advisory until the
  shipping cascade checker lands; conditions 1 and 3 are hard from
  this release.
- **Release-durability close — AC-10 (twin-data-freshness)** — the
  twin's component look is 1:1 by construction; the gate covers only
  the two residuals construction does not — dummy dataset
  representativeness (caught mechanically by twin build) and
  net-new-route fixture coverage.

## Behavior + Compatibility

- **Migrations** — additive only. Migration 044 adds a nullable
  `queue_items.summary` column; pre-0.4.1 items degrade to the
  body-fallback label. Pre-0.4.1 daemons that omit 044 also degrade
  cleanly via a `detectQueueColumn`-guarded read path. Existing v0.4.0
  databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **`rig queue create` / `rig queue handoff` — `--summary`** —
  optional; missing summary emits a WARN, never a hard error
  (graceful migration). Hard-require is a future hardening.
- **`rig send` default** — now refuses sends when the target pane is
  at a prompt. `--dangerously-interact --reason "..."` is the explicit
  override path.
- **Cosmetic Project tab renames** — Topology → Workflow (test-id
  stable); Queue folds into Story.
- **For-You feed** — the storytelling-preview band on
  `/for-you` is removed (its mission-progress rollup remains on
  Dashboard / Project).

## Known Limitations + Follow-ons

- **Skill-layer cut depth (slice 04 family)** — the canonical
  skill-layer cut still awaits a decision on the load-bearing skill
  set; the cut does not execute in this release. The 04.3 shipping
  cascade-drift checker is not in this cut.
- **Convention drift control (slice 28)** — partially delivered;
  convention ratified + folded into the release-close gate, but the
  shipping product skill + audit-code are still in flight.
- **Twin capture tooling (slice 11.2)** — the twin harness ships; the
  one-command capture wrapper is in flight.
- **Workspace UX architecture (slice 15)** — the design-discovery
  scope is approved; the remaining mockups are in flight (they gate
  future UI slices, not 0.4.1 shipped surfaces).
- **For-You terminal phone-UX (slice 27)** — the For-You restyle and
  real-data fidelity are shipped; the embedded terminal's phone-UX
  (keyboard / touch / width / performance) is a non-gating polish
  check, not yet phone-verified.
- **`rig send` interactive-prompt guard — hook-primary path** — the
  fallback capture-pane guard is fully proven; the hook-primary
  `PermissionRequest` path lands with this release and rides its full
  proof on the next iteration.
- **`rig auth` follow-on (B1 secret-boundary)** — the adversarial
  hardening already merged into `rig auth` closes the symlink +
  hardlink escapes; a deeper structured follow-on is tracked
  separately, not in this cut.
- **Inherited cascade-metadata hygiene** — the 0.4.0 release
  carry-forward (skill-layer `missing_provenance` +
  `missing_verified` audit findings) remains the documented residue;
  bulk fix lives in a separate post-0.4.0 skill-hygiene work item.

## See Also

- `CHANGELOG.md` — the standard changelog entry for 0.4.1.
- `docs/as-built/cli-reference.md` — the shipped CLI surface.
- `docs/releases/v0.4.0.md` — the prior release.

body.name: OpenRig v0.4.0 — Token-efficient defaults + recovery resilience capstone + real-terminal session broker
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.4.0

## Summary

OpenRig v0.4.0 is a token-efficient-defaults + recovery-capstone release.
Five read-commands every agent runs constantly (`rig ps`, `rig whoami`,
`rig queue list`, `rig restore-check`, `rig context`) flip from
firehose-by-default to compact-by-default with an explicit `--full` /
`--all` opt-in; `rig queue list` adopts the docker/kubectl-aligned
read-command grammar (`-a` for history, `-A` for cross-rig breadth,
`-o json|wide` for encoding, `--mine` / `--source` / `--destination`
for scope). `rig seat clear-attention` extends to cover the
restoreOutcome-derived projection staleness class that v0.3.4 shipped
but couldn't reach. `rig scope mission|slice create` now scaffolds
`PROGRESS.md` reliably and ships a `progress` update verb so agents
update progress through the command rather than hand-editing markdown.

Behind those user-visible defaults: the daemon-side payload
source-dedup (`rig ps` `recoveryGuidance` no longer duplicated
per-node, `contextUsage` compact in the list payload) ships at slice 26
so even `--full` and the UI consumers stop paying for it; live agent
terminals replace the read-only 3-second snapshot view (slice 01);
multi-host dogfooding hardens the `--host` flag's cross-host story
(slice 02); the Agent Images library gains a Fork-now affordance + row
metadata (slice 07); attention/activity detection consumes
`agentActivity` truth more richly across the UI (slice 09);
skill-cascade provenance + freshness gets a new read-only `rig skill
audit` surface (slice 10); the identity refactor foundation lands the
common identity types both the daemon and CLI consume (slice 11);
`rig scope` progress rails reconnect the mission/slice tree to
`PROGRESS.md` to the Project UI (slice 15); Codex resume preserves the
launching seat's approval posture so resumed seats can run lifecycle
commands without hitting implicit-deny (slice 17); the active/idle
node-state ring becomes reliable (slice 18); a diagonal ghost in the
topology graph view is fixed at source (slice 21); convergence-fix
P1 (For-You drill captured/live contract) + P2 (daemon test-harness
WebSocket registration) land as the wrap-blocking bug-fix slice 24.

Existing v0.3.4 databases upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the
new daemon. Migrations are additive.

## Included In This Release

### New top-level CLI verbs + new subcommands

- **`rig skill audit` (slice 10)** — new read-only command + daemon
  surface (`/api/skills/audit`, discovery, mirror-drift detection,
  skills route). Reports skill-cascade provenance findings —
  missing / stale / self-referential / invalid-date / mirror-drift —
  across the canonical → product mirror → hub cwd → installed plugin
  cascade. Prevents false-green CLI success when mirror-drift evidence
  is unavailable (the failure mode the v0.3.4 wrap-gate AC-3 almost
  shipped). Composes with the existing `scripts/mirror-skills.mjs`
  guardrails.
- **`rig scope mission progress` / `rig scope slice progress` (slice 33)** —
  new `progress` verbs that append/set/update entries in `PROGRESS.md`
  deterministically through the command surface rather than hand-edited
  markdown. Writes the canonical structure the OpenRig PROGRESS UI page
  reads.

### Compact-by-default read commands (the token-efficiency family)

- **`rig ps` — compact default + `--full` + current-rig default + `-A`/`--all-rigs` (slices 25 + 34)** — default
  emits a compact TL;DR per node (session, rig, activity state +
  reason, assigned/pending counts; identity-recovery essentials only).
  `--full` returns the complete record (raw byte-equivalent). **Slice 34 — breadth default flipped to CURRENT-RIG** (derived from `OPENRIG_SESSION_NAME`'s `@<rig>` suffix) to match the docker/kubectl-aligned `rig queue list` grammar: `-A`/`--all-rigs` for fleet breadth; `--rig <name>` overrides the current-rig default; `--session <sess>` narrows further. All-states stays the default (per orch-lead's ruling: ps surfaces topology/readiness, where stopped/recoverable/attention is the actionable signal — unlike queue-list where the actionable set is active items). `--active` / `--running` remains the opt-in active-state filter. Closes a ~77,000-token status-glance incident at root + a fleet-scale unbounded-default-output bomb. **Resume-token security**: `--full` JSON now emits `resumeTokenPresent` (boolean) instead of the resume token value itself, so an orch glance never accidentally leaks token material.
- **`rig ps` payload source dedup (slice 26)** — daemon node-list
  payload trims at source: `recoveryGuidance` is no longer serialized
  as near-identical templated prose on every node (relocated to a
  guidance-by-reference map at the top level so the 4 current
  consumers still resolve it); `contextUsage` is a compact summary in
  the list payload (full telemetry remains retrievable per-node via
  whoami / detail query). The ~7 contextUsage UI consumers + 4
  recoveryGuidance consumers migrated without regression. Even
  `--full` and the UI Project view stop paying for the redundant
  per-node blobs.
- **`rig whoami` — compact default + `--full` (slice 27)** — `rig
  whoami` and `rig whoami --json` default to identity-recovery
  essentials only (`identity` / `peers` names + sessionNames / `edges`
  directional kind + to.sessionName / `transcriptPath`). `--full`
  (alias `--verbose`) returns today's complete payload including
  `contextUsage`, `commands`, `peersNote`, `runtimeContext`. Daemon
  skips the `contextUsageStore` lookup and `runtimeContext` build when
  compact is requested. The first command every agent runs on boot +
  every compaction-restore now costs ~192 tokens instead of ~909.
- **`rig queue list` — active-frontier compact default + read-command
  grammar (slices 28 + 32)** — `rig queue list` (no flags) returns
  active states only (`pending` / `in-progress` / `claimed` /
  `blocked` / `handed-off`; not `done` / `canceled`), current-rig
  breadth, compact rows (id, state, source→destination /
  current-owner, closure_reason / closure_target when handed-off /
  blocked, mission, slice, tier / priority, age / updated_at, short
  title, capped tags). The four orthogonal axes are composable:
  - **`-a` / `--all`** — include closed/done history within the
    current breadth (the docker `-a` axis: history).
  - **`-A` / `--all-rigs`** — widen to cross-rig breadth (the
    kubectl `-A` axis: breadth).
  - **`--full`** — add body / chain-of-record / full-tags / transition
    history to whichever scope is selected (the field-breadth axis).
  - **`-o json|wide`** — encoding, compact-by-default. `-o json`
    does NOT imply full body (compact JSON is token-safe + machine-
    parseable); `--full -o json` returns the full JSON.
  - `--mine` returns just the caller's items; `--destination <s>` /
    `--source <s>` for explicit scoping. The bare unscoped firehose
    that aggregated cross-rig + full-history (~64,000 tokens on the
    live host) is retired as a default — opt-in via `-A -a --full`.
- **`rig restore-check` — summary + not-ready default + `--full`
  (slice 29)** — default emits summary counts (total / ready / not-
  ready / error-degraded) plus the not-ready seats only (each compact:
  seat + readiness reason). `--full` / `--json` returns today's
  complete per-seat readiness across the fleet. Daemon skips
  per-seat-detail assembly for ready seats when compact (computes
  verdict, omits detail). `--rig <name>` / `--as <me>` narrow.
  Closes the largest measured bomb (~79,000 tokens) on the
  read-command surface.
- **`rig context` — compact summary default + `--full` (slice 30)** —
  default emits a compact context summary (the few fields the common
  use needs); `--full` / `--json` returns the complete current
  payload. Daemon skips the expensive aggregation when compact. Lower
  leverage than 28/29 but keeps the read-command surface coherent
  compact-by-default after the upgrade.

### Recovery + resilience capstone

- **`rig seat clear-attention` extends to derived projection staleness
  (slice 16)** — v0.3.4 shipped `clear-attention` gating on
  `session.startupStatus` only. First real production use (the host
  cutover's residual `advisor-lead@kernel` projection) found the gap:
  when a seat is `startupStatus=ready` + `sessionStatus=running` but
  carries `restoreOutcome=failed` / `continuityOutcome=failed`, the
  daemon derives `lifecycleState=attention_required` and the verb
  refused with `{ok:false, code:not_in_attention}`. v0.4.0
  `clear-attention` now reaches both classes — the
  startupStatus-driven attention (already shipped) AND the
  restoreOutcome-derived projection — with the same evidence-gated
  audit row and the same operator-attested `--reason <text>` override.
- **Codex Resume Preserves Approval Posture (slice 17)** — a
  resumed Codex seat now comes back with the same permission /
  approval posture as a fresh Codex launch. Previously a resumed
  seat hit "approval required but approvals disabled" implicit-deny
  with no path when running shipped lifecycle commands. Bounded
  bug-fix grounded against the 0.4.0 resilience set; surfaced
  during the GS1 Studio capture.

### UI + topology surfaces

- **Real (Interactive) Terminals (slice 01)** — the per-seat
  terminals in the UI become interactive. Click into a seat, type at
  the agent directly (shared-pane; "hands near the wheel"); the
  read-only 3-second snapshot view is retired for local-host seats.
  Performance constraint met for the rig-altitude "all terminals"
  view (~20–30 panes open simultaneously) via a **global
  `LiveTerminalRegistry`** that caps concurrently-live terminals
  (`ui.terminal.max_live_terminals` config key, env
  `OPENRIG_UI_TERMINAL_MAX_LIVE_TERMINALS`) and a **progressive
  multi-live** interaction model: live where the user is looking
  (focused popover / in-place grid expansion / node-detail panel),
  static smoked-glass thumbnails everywhere else, coordinated by a
  `LiveTerminalProvider`. In-place multi-live in the topology grid +
  shared smoked-glass styling across focused / popover / grid /
  node-detail surfaces. Remote-seat terminals ride 0.4.1 (need
  daemon-to-daemon transport).
- **Real-Terminal Session Broker (slice 38)** — release-critical
  reliability fix grounded in founder live dogfood 2026-06-21. The
  prior architecture opened its own WebSocket per view, and each
  WebSocket started its own tmux `pipe-pane` against the same pane;
  tmux allows ONE pipe-pane per pane, so opening a second live view
  of the same session would **steal output from the first** —
  typing in one visible terminal sent echo to a different tab. The
  v0.4.0 architecture: a daemon-owned
  **`TerminalSessionBroker`** keyed by canonical `sessionName` —
  one tmux pipe-pane per session, N WebSocket subscribers, output
  fanout, session-level seed + shared scrollback ring for late
  subscribers, explicit input-owner semantics (the focused view is
  eligible to send input), and honest cleanup when the last
  subscriber leaves or the session dies. `terminal-ws` is now a
  thin broker subscriber; it no longer owns pipe-pane per
  connection. **Resize policy = canonical fixed geometry**: the
  broker pins the tmux pane at the optimal Claude/Codex TUI grid
  (120×40); subscribers fit/scroll their container to it (CSS),
  they never send tmux resize. One stable source of truth, zero
  resize-fighting, TUI always renders at its optimal width.
- **Unified Static / Live Terminal Component (slice 39)** —
  the static thumbnail and live xterm now share one
  `StaticTerminalPlate` component + one mirror geometry (90×27 for
  thumbnails / mirror; the broker's live stream is 120×40 — the
  thumbnail is a fit-to-container projection of that live stream).
  Opaque mirror render + static line-return fix + grid in-place
  multi-live + graph/table popover. Live-terminal selection on a
  scaled view now uses fontSize scaling (not CSS transform), so
  text selection lands on the correct character cell. Geometry
  comment sweep is behavior-neutral but eliminates stale comments
  that confused subsequent edits.
- **Agent Images Library Polish (slice 07)** — the Agent Images
  library UI gains a `Fork now` action for cloneable images
  (composes the existing add-member endpoint with
  `session_source.mode: "agent_image"`), lightweight row metadata
  (version, token, fork-count, last-used), and nested-failure
  rendering (nested `failed` / `attention_required` outcomes render
  as red failure rather than green success). Fork-now is hidden /
  disabled when the image lacks `sourceCwd`; the confirm path
  requires a runtime-matched sibling carrying `agentRef` + `profile`;
  no fallback cwd is invented.
- **Attention / Activity Detection — Elite Tier (slice 09)** —
  richer consumption of the `agentActivity` truth landed in 0.3.4
  across UI + operator surfaces. Needs-input prominence,
  time-in-state, activity rollups POST-18.
- **Topology Graph-View Ghost Render Fix (slice 21)** — diagonal
  ghost artifact behind the nodes in the dashboard topology /
  graph view is fixed at source. Was present in every graph-view
  capture across the launch-video reviewer kit; the table view was
  already ghost-free. Hero surface across launch videos +
  dashboard.
- **Reliable Active/Idle Node State (slice 18)** — the lit/dark
  activity ring already shipped; this slice closes the
  `DOT→terminalActive` fallback and removes the dead
  `pane_silence_flag` derivation. Flagship video F1's signal layer.

### Multi-host + identity foundations

- **Multi-Host Dogfood (slice 02)** — the `--host` CLI flag was
  shipped pre-0.4.0; this slice closes the cross-machine integration
  story (Tart-VM dogfood, Hetzner VPS + 2nd-Mac as final external
  QA). HTTP-primary transport; cross-host identity rides 0.4.1.
- **Native Codex Session Identity (slice 11)** — landing the common
  identity types both the daemon and CLI consume — native Codex
  session-identity capture + the foundation for the slice-12
  identity-refactor that rides 0.4.1.

### Scope automation

- **`rig scope` PROGRESS.md + README scaffolding (slice 33)** —
  `rig scope mission create` and `rig scope slice create` now
  scaffold a canonical `PROGRESS.md` (the structure the OpenRig
  PROGRESS UI page parses) plus a convention-correct README with
  proper frontmatter, per
  `conventions/scope-and-versioning/README.md`. Fixes the bug where
  newly-created missions + slices were missing `PROGRESS.md`
  entirely. A `rig scope ... progress` update verb appends / sets /
  records progress entries deterministically — agents update
  progress through the command (UI-valid by construction) rather
  than hand-editing markdown and drifting.
- **`rig scope` stage / verified / reconcile verbs (slice 35)** —
  the maturity vocabulary from `conventions/scope-and-versioning`
  §2 (`stage` + `verified`) becomes enforced through commands
  instead of hand-editing markdown. Composes with slice 33's
  PROGRESS.md + scaffolding to make `rig scope` the deterministic
  convention-enforcer.
  - `rig scope <slice|mission> stage <id> <new-stage>` — set
    `stage` (wip / provisional / established / canonical /
    superseded / retired) deterministically. `superseded` REQUIRES
    `--successor <id>` (rejected otherwise); `retired` warns
    "do not use"; invalid stages rejected with the valid set
    named.
  - `rig scope <slice|mission> verified <id> --against
    "<source>"` — stamp `verified: <today> against <source>` in
    frontmatter. `--against` is MANDATORY — bare timestamps
    rejected (the anti-stale keystone: a bare timestamp is
    exactly what lets stale trackers lie while looking fresh).
    Overwrites the prior verified line.
  - `rig scope <slice|mission> reconcile <id>` — idempotent repair
    verb that backfills missing `PROGRESS.md`, conforms mandatory
    frontmatter (`id` / `stage` / `verified`), and repairs
    id-registration ghosts (`id:null` / doubled-prefix artifacts).
    Safe to re-run.
  - `rig scope <slice|mission> create` now writes the MANDATORY
    `stage` (default `wip`) + a `verified` placeholder, so no new
    artifact ships missing them.
  - `rig scope <slice|mission> show` derives a read-time
    effective-reliability projection from (stage × verified): a
    stale-`verified` `canonical` is reported as effectively
    `provisional` (derivation, not stored). Self-correcting signal
    for the UI + agents.
- **Scope-Backed Progress Rails (slice 15)** — connects the scope
  tree, startup skills, `PROGRESS.md` rails, and Project UI
  warnings into one coherent workflow. From the 0.3.4 release
  audit (the mission/slice tree existed + queue traffic was rich,
  but `PROGRESS.md` surfaces the dashboard depends on were missing
  or under-used). Pairs with 33 — 33 ships the command; 15 ships
  the workflow that uses it.

### Bug-fix wrap

- **Wrap Convergence Fixes (slice 24)** — the wrap-blocking
  bug-fix slice from the 0.4.0 convergence deep-review. Two narrow
  real-terminals integration defects: **P1** For-You terminal-drill
  mixed captured / live contract (cross-slice 01↔09 seam); **P2**
  daemon test-harness broken by unconditional Node WebSocket
  registration (51→411 suite failures). Both pre-wrap blockers per
  founder ("real convergence bugs land as 0.4.0 bug-fix slices
  before wrap"). Reviewers found NO broader cross-slice coherence
  defect — the convergence is clean.

## User-Facing Changes

### New surfaces (use these)

- **Read-commands compact by default**: `rig ps`, `rig whoami`,
  `rig queue list`, `rig restore-check`, `rig context`. Same
  breadth, much smaller default payload. Use `--full` (or `-A -a
  --full` for queue list) when you need the firehose.
- **`rig queue list` grammar (docker / kubectl aligned)**:
  ```
  rig queue list                      # active, compact, current-rig
  rig queue list -a                   # + closed/done history
  rig queue list -A                   # cross-rig breadth (same as -A in kubectl)
  rig queue list --full               # add body + chain-of-record
  rig queue list -o json              # compact JSON (token-safe)
  rig queue list --full -o json       # full JSON
  rig queue list --mine               # caller's items only
  rig queue list --destination <s>    # destined to <s>
  rig queue list --source <s>         # sourced by <s>
  rig queue show <qitemId>            # full single item (kubectl describe)
  ```
- **`rig skill audit`** — read-only audit of the skill cascade.
  Detects missing / stale / self-referential / invalid-date /
  mirror-drift across the canonical → product mirror → hub cwd
  → installed plugin chain. Prevents false-green CLI success when
  mirror-drift evidence is unavailable.
- **`rig scope ... progress`** — deterministic `PROGRESS.md`
  updates. Append entries, set status, record milestones through
  the command surface; the UI reads the same canonical structure
  the command writes.
- **`rig seat clear-attention` for restoreOutcome-derived
  projection** — the v0.3.4 verb now reaches the second class of
  projection staleness. Same evidence-gated audit row; same
  `--reason <text>` operator-attestation override.

### What to STOP using

- **Stop assuming `rig ps --nodes --json` is the casual status
  check.** Compact default is the casual check; the firehose is
  `--full`. Per-node `recoveryGuidance` near-identical-prose
  duplication is retired; per-node full `contextUsage` is retired
  from the list payload (relocate to single-node / whoami / detail
  queries).
- **Stop using bare `rig queue list` as the cross-rig firehose.**
  Default is now active + compact + current-rig. The cross-rig
  ambient-frontier view is `-A`; cross-rig + history is `-A -a`;
  the full firehose is `-A -a --full -o json`.
- **Stop using `rig whoami --json` to get the heavy payload on
  boot.** Default is compact identity-essentials; `--full` (or
  `--verbose`) returns today's complete payload.
- **Stop using `rig restore-check` as a per-seat-detail fleet
  scan.** Default is summary + not-ready only; `--full` for the
  per-seat detail when actually needed.
- **Stop hand-editing `PROGRESS.md` with markdown to record
  progress.** Use `rig scope ... progress` — UI-valid by
  construction, deterministic, no drift.
- **Stop hand-creating `PROGRESS.md` for new missions / slices.**
  `rig scope mission create` + `rig scope slice create` scaffold
  it now.
- **Stop applying the token-efficiency-boot-guardrail's
  CLI-command prohibitions on hosts running 0.4.0** (the
  prohibitions were host-version workarounds for the bloated
  defaults this release closes). The pack's bounded-local-search
  rule + scope/over-flag discipline GRADUATE to a standing
  convention (`conventions/bounded-local-search-and-flag-scope`)
  and continue to apply host-independently. The
  CLI-command-prohibitions half of the pack RETIRES at
  host-upgrade-to-0.4.0.

### Operator / Setup Notes

- **No new schema-bumping migrations.** Existing v0.3.4 databases
  upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.
- **`rig scope` backfill on existing trees**: missions and slices
  created before 0.4.0 that are missing `PROGRESS.md` can be
  backfilled by running the `rig scope` repair / doctor step (see
  slice 33 IMPLEMENTATION-PRD for the exact verb).
- **Compact JSON is machine-parseable**. The compact-row schema
  for `rig queue list -o json` is stable; downstream parsers
  reading the compact rows don't need migration. Parsers that
  read body / chain-of-record must use `--full` explicitly.
- **`rig skill audit` on the host** — first real production run
  surfaces the current cascade state (missing / stale /
  mirror-drift findings). The lifecycle's cascade-propagation
  pass (canonical `openrig-work/skills/` → product mirror → hub
  cwd → installed plugin) coordinates with the audit's findings
  going forward.

### Known Limitations + carry-forward

- **Plugin-Lineage Drift in `openrig-core`**: the openrig-core
  plugin skill lineage is divergent / stale (see OPR.0.4.1.4 —
  the full plugin re-sync, rides 0.4.1). v0.4.0 ships with this
  drift known; the cascade-sweep this release ran verified the
  canonical + config-mirror layers agents boot from are correct
  / current at the release SHA, and `rig skill audit` (slice 10)
  is the new runtime mechanism to detect future drift. The full
  openrig-core plugin re-sync lands in 0.4.1.
- All earlier "PUSHED to 0.4.1" carry-forwards were RESTORED to
  0.4.0 during the wrap: slice 34 (`rig ps` current-rig default
  + `-A`/`--all-rigs` + `resumeTokenPresent` security) landed —
  see the rig ps entry under Compact-by-default read commands;
  slice 35 (`rig scope` stage / verified / reconcile verbs)
  landed — see Scope automation section. Nothing of substance
  carries forward to 0.4.1 from the original wrap-gate set.
- **Real-terminal-related slices** (38 + 39) shipped via founder
  live-dogfood forward-fix authorization 2026-06-21 (the
  TerminalSessionBroker reliability fix + the unified
  static/live terminal component). Both are in 0.4.0; no
  carry-forward.

## Verification Performed

- npm + GitHub release surfaces: published at the lifecycle wrap step (founder-authorized).
- Wrap worktree clean on `8d55ea60` (the wrap-gate target SHA).
- `rig daemon start` upgrades 0.3.4 → 0.4.0 databases additively (no schema-breaking migrations).
- CLI help surfaces for every changed command (`rig ps`, `rig whoami`,
  `rig queue list`, `rig restore-check`, `rig context`, `rig scope`)
  source-verified against the command source at the release SHA per
  `feedback_release_docs_source_verify_each_cli_surface_dont_carry_forward`.
- CLI→skill cascade sweep — canonical
  `openrig-work/skills/openrig-user/SKILL.md` → product mirror at
  `packages/daemon/specs/agents/shared/skills/core/openrig-user/SKILL.md`
  → hub cwd `.claude/skills/openrig-user/SKILL.md` +
  `.agents/skills/openrig-user/SKILL.md` updated for the six changed
  commands and the new `--full` / `-a` / `-A` / `-o` grammar; obsolete
  caveats retired (the `--notify`-required footgun footnote where it
  appeared, any "this command dumps everything" warnings made false
  by the compact defaults).
- AC-6 wrap-gate self-check PASS — see the durability-close ledger
  evidence for the cascade-sweep grep evidence + cli-reference diff.

## Commits Included

`git log v0.3.4..7e6ba168` against the wrap worktree at the release
SHA. The release commits are the version bump + the durability-close
sweep + the lifecycle wrap commits per the
`conventions/release-durability-close` convention.

body.name: OpenRig v0.3.4 — Recovery + Resilience
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.3.4

## Summary

OpenRig v0.3.4 is a recovery + resilience release. Two new top-level CLI
verbs land (`rig start` and `rig reconcile-session`), `rig up` flips
from fresh-by-default to resume-original-by-default with `--fresh
<seats...>` as the explicit per-seat opt-in, the restore status surface
collapses every honest outcome into a named five-term vocabulary
(`resumed` / `fresh-primed` / `awaiting-decision` / `attention_required`
/ `failed`) across `rig up` / `rig restore` / `rig ps`, and a periodic
snapshot scheduler ships as the crash-insurance floor under
event-driven and teardown snapshots. A handful of long-standing
recovery paper cuts are retired in the same cut: pod-aware narrow
launch leaves dead-end-land for a node-granular managed partial
restore through `rig launch`, a stuck `attention_required` seat now
clears through an evidence-gated `rig seat clear-attention` rather
than hand-edited SQLite, the Codex profile-v2 preflight stops
misclassifying invalid TOML as a legacy-profile reason, the cmux
launch-readiness gate surfaces honest partial workspace state, and a
slow Codex resume no longer gets mis-categorized.

No new schema-bumping migrations in 0.3.4. Existing v0.3.3 databases
upgrade by running `rig daemon start` on the new daemon.

## Included In This Release

- **`rig start` (slice 01)** — new top-level recovery entry point.
  One command that sequences daemon-start, kernel readiness wait,
  restore-usable candidate listing, picker or headless flag
  selection, and per-rig restore + reconcile. Re-codes nothing
  underneath: it sequences existing primitives. Flags `--last`,
  `--all`, `--rigs <names...>`, `--json`. Candidate listing and
  apply are both id-grounded against `/api/rigs/:id/up` (the
  same-name-rigs class never reaches the name-based `/api/up`
  route).
- **`rig up` Resume-By-Default (slice 02)** — `rig up <existing-rig>`
  now resumes original sessions by default. `--fresh <seats...>`
  becomes the explicit per-seat opt-in for operation B (deliberate
  fresh-prime). Previously the default was fresh-prime; agents had
  to know to ask for resume out-of-band. The seat-level outcome
  rides the five-term vocabulary below; `awaiting-decision` is the
  honest zero-session state when the daemon cannot resume and the
  operator has not opted into fresh.
- **`rig reconcile-session` (slice 03)** — new top-level command.
  Adopts a LIVE, hand-resumed canonical session back into its
  persisted node without launching, relaunching, killing, replaying
  startup, pressing resume menus, compacting, or typing into the
  pane. The repair for "I manually resumed the seat; the daemon
  still shows it down." Same node id, no re-key; reports projection
  drift honestly; conversation continuity is never claimed.
- **`rig up --plan` Read-Only Restore Preview (slice 04)** —
  `rig up <existing-rig> --plan` returns a read-only restore
  preview keyed by the five-term vocabulary and an honest async
  timeout. No mutation; no silent claims of resumability when the
  daemon cannot prove it.
- **Five-Term Restore Status Vocabulary (slice 06)** — the prior
  2-3 term collapsed model is replaced across `rig up`,
  `rig restore`, and `rig ps`:
  - `resumed` — original session continuity proven.
  - `fresh-primed` — deliberate fresh-prime (operation B); a brand
    new session was started instead of resumed.
  - `awaiting-decision` — daemon could not resume and operator has
    not opted into fresh; ZERO session started. The honest
    zero-session state, not a silent failure.
  - `attention_required` — seat is live or parked but needs
    operator action (auth gate, model-selection menu, trust
    prompt, stuck recovery). NEVER `failed`.
  - `failed` — the launch transport itself failed.
- **Codex Profile-V2 Preflight (slice 07)** — profile-load check
  on profile-bearing launch and restore surfaces. Legacy-profile
  detection narrowed to legacy-specific patterns only (`contains
  legacy`, `[profiles.<name>]`, `cannot be used while.*legacy`,
  `legacy profile selector`); the prior generic match against
  `failed to load configuration` was also catching invalid-TOML
  stderr and giving the wrong migration hint. Invalid TOML now
  surfaces the actual parse reason (up to 3 stderr lines) with a
  TOML-validity hint.
- **cmux Launch Readiness (slice 08)** — launch path no longer
  silently produces a partial cmux workspace. When cmux comes up
  with a subset of expected windows / panes, the seat surfaces an
  honest partial-workspace state with a one-click open-missing
  affordance instead of being reported as launched-clean.
- **Periodic Snapshots (slice 09)** — `snapshots.periodic` config
  family plus a daemon-side `PeriodicSnapshotScheduler`. Every
  enabled rig captures an `auto-periodic` snapshot on interval and
  the repository prunes by retention-keep. Provides a true
  crash-insurance floor — `auto-periodic` and `auto-pre-down`
  compete on freshness in the same restore selector (the newer
  wins), so a daemon crash between teardown snapshots no longer
  costs an arbitrary amount of lifecycle state. Last-snapshot /
  floor surfaced in `rig ps` / status.
- **`rig seat clear-attention` (slice 10)** — new subcommand on
  `rig seat`. Evidence-gated, operator-attested, audited reconcile
  of a stuck `attention_required` seat back to `ready`. Replaces
  the prior hand-edit-SQLite / fake-clear pattern that agents
  reached for when a seat got stuck. The audit row records who
  cleared, from-state, the evidence path, and any operator
  attestation; `--reason <text>` is the operator-attestation
  override for the evidence gate.
- **Node-Granular Managed Partial Restore (slice 11)** — `rig
  launch <rigId> <nodeRef>` and `rig launch <rigId> --seats <a,b>`
  relaunch a seat or subset by logical id through the
  orchestration layer. Retires the v0.3.x-era
  `pod_aware_launch_unsupported` dead-end and the
  "use rig up instead" workaround that lost per-seat control.
  Held seats carry a `held-reason`; failed targets surface as
  `failed (liveness unknown)`; already-running seats are reported,
  not relaunched.
- **Slow Codex Resume Classification Fix (slice 13)** — internal
  classification tweak for slow-resume Codex sessions: a seat that
  was genuinely resuming but slowly was previously mis-categorized
  by `verifyResumeLaunch`. Now correctly classified through the
  same five-term vocabulary.
- **Pod-Aware Claude Resume-Selection Menu (slice 05 rev1)** —
  follow-on to 0.3.3 slice 21 FR-2: `ClaudeCodeAdapter.verifyResumeLaunch`
  now treats a Claude resume-selection menu the same way it treats
  the Codex unresolved-gate case — returns immediately with
  `recovery: attention_required` and last-12-line pane evidence,
  never sends a numeric selection keystroke, and never lets the
  loop time out to a generic failure.

## User-Facing Changes

### `rig start` — Recovery Entry Point

New top-level command. Starts the daemon, waits for the kernel, lists
restore-usable rigs, and applies restore + reconcile through the
existing primitives:

```
rig start                            Interactive: daemon + kernel + pick-and-restore
rig start --last                     Headless: restore all rigs that were last running
rig start --all                      Headless: restore all rigs with restore-usable snapshots
rig start --rigs <name> [<name>...]  Headless: restore only the named rigs
rig start --json                     JSON output for agents
```

Listing and apply are both id-grounded against
`POST /api/rigs/:id/up`. Same-name rigs surface as separate
candidates; selection carries the candidate's `rigId` end-to-end so
the name-based `/api/up` route is never consulted (no
`ambiguous_name` 409 in the recovery path).

`rig start` is sequencing-only; it does not invent recovery
semantics. The per-rig restore call is the same `/api/rigs/:id/up`
that `rig up <existing>` uses, and seat-level outcomes carry the
same five-term vocabulary.

### `rig up` — Resume Original By Default

`rig up <existing-rig>` resumes original sessions by default.
`--fresh <seats...>` is the per-seat opt-in for deliberate
fresh-prime (operation B):

```
rig up <existing-rig>                       Resume original sessions (default)
rig up --existing <name> --fresh dev-impl   Deliberately fresh-prime dev-impl only
rig up <existing-rig> --plan                Read-only restore preview (no mutation)
```

- Seats whose original session resumes report `resumed`.
- Seats opted into `--fresh` report `fresh-primed`.
- Seats the daemon cannot resume and the operator has not opted
  into fresh report `awaiting-decision` — ZERO session started.
  Headless callers see the explicit hint `rig up --existing
  <source> --fresh <logical-id>`; TTY callers are offered a
  per-seat `[y/N]` prompt before any fresh-prime is started.
- Seats live or parked but needing operator action (auth gate,
  model selection, trust prompt, stuck recovery) report
  `attention_required` — never silently re-classified as `failed`.
- Only transport-level failure reports `failed`.

The prior fresh-by-default behavior is gone. If a workflow relied on
implicit fresh, name `--fresh <seats...>` explicitly.

### `rig up --plan` — Read-Only Restore Preview

```
rig up <existing-rig> --plan [--json]
```

Returns the restore plan without mutating: per-node intended action
(resume / fresh-prime / awaiting-decision), the snapshot the plan
would consume, and whether the current state would be captured before
mutation. The plan path carries an honest async timeout — when the
preview cannot complete within bound, the response says so rather
than claiming a clean plan.

### `rig reconcile-session` — Adopt a Hand-Resumed Session

New top-level command. Use after manually resuming a seat (e.g.
`claude --resume <id>` / `codex resume <id>`) inside its canonical
tmux session: the daemon still shows the seat down. Reconcile binds
the live process to its OWN persisted node and updates the
projection so `rig ps` / topology / `rig send` / `rig capture` /
queue routing work again. It NEVER launches, relaunches, kills,
replays startup, presses resume menus, compacts, or types into the
pane.

```
rig reconcile-session <session>                                   Auto-resolve target node
rig reconcile-session <session> --rig <rigId> --node <logicalId>  Disambiguate
rig reconcile-session <session> --no-launch                       Explicit (default mode)
rig reconcile-session <session> --json                            JSON output for agents
```

`--rig` and `--node` must be provided together (disambiguation).
Same node id, no re-key. Anything the reconcile could not prove is
reported as projection drift (a list of unproven metadata fields);
conversation continuity is reported as a status string, never
claimed as proven.

### Five-Term Restore Status Vocabulary

The seat-level status field on `rig up`, `rig restore`, and `rig ps`
now carries one of five values:

| Status                | Meaning                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resumed`             | Original session continuity proven by the native-resume probe.                                     |
| `fresh-primed`        | Operator opted into a deliberate fresh-prime (operation B); a brand new session started.           |
| `awaiting-decision`   | Daemon could not resume and operator has not opted into fresh. ZERO session started.               |
| `attention_required`  | Seat is live or parked but needs operator action (auth, model selection, trust, stuck recovery).   |
| `failed`              | The launch transport itself failed.                                                                |

`awaiting-decision` is new and replaces the prior pattern where a
zero-session outcome was either misreported as success or as
failure. `attention_required` covers the broader live-but-stuck
class; a live or parked seat is NEVER reported as `failed`.

### `rig seat clear-attention` — Audited Stuck-Seat Recovery

Subcommand on `rig seat`. Evidence-gated, operator-attested, audited
reconcile of a stuck `attention_required` seat back to `ready`:

```
rig seat clear-attention <session>
rig seat clear-attention <session> --reason "<operator attestation>"
rig seat clear-attention <session> --json
```

- Without `--reason`, the clear requires evidence the seat is
  actually back to a clean state (the daemon-side gate).
- `--reason <text>` is the operator-attestation override; the
  audit row records the attestation string verbatim.
- Output: `Cleared <session>: <from> -> ready (<clearedBy>)`. The
  audit log captures session, from-state, gate-or-attestation, and
  operator address.

Replaces the prior hand-edit-SQLite / fake-clear pattern. The seat's
node id is unchanged.

### Node-Granular Managed Partial Restore

`rig launch` works for single-seat and subset relaunch on a running
rig through the orchestration layer:

```
rig launch <rigId> <nodeRef>                Single seat (logical id or node id)
rig launch <rigId> --seats <a,b,c>          Subset (comma-separated logical ids)
rig launch <rigId> --seats <a,b> --hold-reason "<text>"  Reason for held non-targets
rig launch <rigId> --seats <a,b> --json
```

- Single-target: `POST /api/rigs/:rigId/nodes/:nodeRef/launch`.
- Subset: `POST /api/rigs/:rigId/nodes/launch-subset`. Reports
  `launched`, `held` (with reason), `alreadyRunning`, and
  `failedTargets` (liveness unknown) separately — partial outcomes
  are never collapsed.

Retires the `pod_aware_launch_unsupported` dead-end and the
"use rig up instead" workaround. Use `rig launch` for per-seat or
per-subset relaunch on a running rig; `rig up <existing>` remains
the whole-rig restore entry.

### Periodic Snapshots

The crash-insurance floor under event-driven and teardown
snapshots. New `snapshots.periodic` settings family:

| Key                                    | Default | Meaning                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `snapshots.periodic.enabled`           | `true`  | Master switch                              |
| `snapshots.periodic.interval_seconds`  | `300`   | Snapshot interval per enabled rig          |
| `snapshots.periodic.retention_keep`    | `10`    | Per-rig `auto-periodic` retention count    |

Snapshots are captured with kind `auto-periodic`; the repository
prunes by `retention_keep` per rig. Restore selection treats
`auto-periodic` and `auto-pre-down` symmetrically — the newer of
the two wins, so a daemon crash between teardown snapshots no
longer loses arbitrary lifecycle state. Last-snapshot / floor is
surfaced in `rig ps` / status so an operator can see the floor
at a glance.

Tune via the settings store (`rig config set ...`) or rely on
defaults; the scheduler reads at daemon startup and respects
`snapshots.periodic.enabled = false` as a master switch.

### Codex Profile-V2 Preflight

The profile-load check on profile-bearing launch and restore
surfaces is now honest about WHICH failure it sees:

- **Legacy-profile detection narrowed**: matches `contains legacy`,
  `[profiles.<name>]`, `cannot be used while.*legacy`, and `legacy
  profile selector` only. The prior generic match against `failed
  to load configuration` was also catching invalid-TOML stderr.
- **Invalid TOML surfaces the parse reason**: up to 3 stderr lines
  (e.g. `expected newline`), with a TOML-validity hint instead of
  a wrong migration hint pointing at `[profiles.<profile>]`.

The auth-refusal projection path is unchanged; this is a
classification fix in the preflight discriminator.

### cmux Launch Readiness

The cmux launch path no longer silently produces a partial
workspace. When cmux comes up with a subset of expected windows or
panes, the seat surfaces an honest partial-workspace state with a
one-click open-missing affordance instead of being projected as
launched-clean.

### Slow Codex Resume Classification

Internal classification tweak in `verifyResumeLaunch` for slow but
genuinely-resuming Codex sessions. Previously the slow path got
mis-categorized through the unresolved-gate branch; now it
correctly classifies through the same five-term vocabulary and
reaches `resumed` when the readiness probe confirms it.

### Pod-Aware Claude Resume-Selection Menu

Follow-on to 0.3.3 slice 21 FR-2. `ClaudeCodeAdapter.verifyResumeLaunch`
now treats a Claude resume-selection menu the same way it treats
the Codex unresolved-gate case: returns immediately with
`recovery: attention_required` and last-12-line pane evidence on
both the inner poll loop and the final-probe exit path. Zero
numeric selection keystrokes are ever sent.

## What to STOP Using

These patterns are retired by 0.3.4. Stop reaching for them; the
named replacement is the supported path:

- **STOP** treating `rig up <existing-rig>` as fresh-by-default.
  Resume-original is now default. Use `--fresh <seats...>` when a
  deliberate fresh-prime is the goal (operation B).
- **STOP** reading a stuck or parked seat as `failed`. A live or
  parked seat carries `attention_required`; only the transport
  itself failing is `failed`. The honest zero-session state is
  `awaiting-decision`, not `failed`.
- **STOP** reaching for `pod_aware_launch_unsupported` workarounds
  or "use `rig up` instead" for per-seat relaunch. Use `rig launch
  <rigId> <nodeRef>` or `rig launch <rigId> --seats <a,b>`.
- **STOP** hand-editing SQLite or fake-clearing a stuck
  `attention_required` seat. Use `rig seat clear-attention
  <session>` (evidence-gated) or `rig seat clear-attention
  <session> --reason "<attestation>"` (operator-attested,
  audited).
- **STOP** relying only on event-driven or teardown snapshots for
  crash safety. The periodic snapshot scheduler is the floor;
  tune `snapshots.periodic.interval_seconds` /
  `snapshots.periodic.retention_keep` to taste.
- **STOP** classifying invalid TOML as a legacy-profile problem.
  The Codex profile-v2 preflight now surfaces the actual TOML
  parse reason; legacy detection requires legacy-specific
  patterns.
- **STOP** restoring a hand-resumed session by relaunching the
  whole rig. Use `rig reconcile-session <session> --no-launch` —
  no relaunch, no input written, same node id.
- **STOP** projecting a partial cmux workspace as launched-clean.
  The launch-readiness gate surfaces partial state honestly with
  a one-click open-missing path.

## Operator / Setup Notes

After upgrading the published CLI:

```bash
npm install -g @openrig/cli@0.3.4
rig --version    # expect 0.3.4
rig daemon stop
rig daemon start
```

No new schema-bumping migrations in 0.3.4. The
`snapshots.periodic.*` settings have built-in defaults
(`enabled=true`, `interval_seconds=300`, `retention_keep=10`); no
operator action is required to pick up the crash-insurance floor.

Operators installing v0.3.4 fresh from npm have full access to the
new surfaces immediately. Operators upgrading an existing host
follow the standard daemon-restart flow above; the 0.3.4 host-
upgrade flow is held for separate sequencing and is NOT a
prerequisite for fresh-install access.

For the new `rig start` surface: it sequences existing primitives
(daemon + kernel + per-rig `/api/rigs/:id/up`). The picker is TTY-
interactive by default; the headless flags `--last`, `--all`, and
`--rigs <names...>` cover scripted recovery.

For `rig up` resume-original-by-default: any agent or script that
implicitly depended on fresh-prime as the default must now name
`--fresh <seats...>` explicitly. The five-term vocabulary applies
on the response; treat `awaiting-decision` as the headless
"operator must decide" outcome, not an error.

For `rig seat clear-attention`: prefer evidence-gated clear when
the seat is genuinely back. The `--reason <text>` override is the
audited operator-attestation path; the attestation string lands in
the audit row verbatim.

For periodic snapshots: tune `snapshots.periodic.interval_seconds`
down for higher-churn rigs and `snapshots.periodic.retention_keep`
up for longer recovery windows. The default 5-minute interval +
10-snapshot retention is a balanced floor.

## Known Limitations / 0.3.4 Carry-forwards

- **`rig view list/show --json` flag inconsistency** — wrapper-
  layer routing path remains; the daemon's `view show <name>`
  route returns JSON correctly when invoked directly. Workaround:
  human-readable output for now. Wrapper-layer fix is the
  documented target.
- **`docs/DESIGN.md` docs-guard ledger** — the docs-guard ledger
  for design-doc updates carries forward; no behavior impact on
  the shipped runtime surface.
- **Slice-21 FR-1 (native Codex session-id hook)**: scope-tipped
  to 0.4.0 after build-time forensic. Carried forward from 0.3.3.
- **Slice-13 component 3 (auto-rollout dispatcher)**: skill-layer
  landing remains; product-code dispatcher / invocation is
  intentionally out of the shipped runtime bundle. Carried
  forward from 0.3.3.
- **Slice-05 sub-scopes from 0.3.2**: agent / port / managed-app
  collision detection (Item 4.3); broader install-into-existing-
  rig pathway acceptance (Item 4.4); `--target-name` CLI flag for
  install-time rig-name overrides. Carried forward.
- **Slice-21 FR-4(d) accepted-queue-state schema**: deferred from
  0.3.2; new `accepted` queue state remains a schema model
  change. Carried forward.
- **Onboarding journey + battle-hardening**: slices 04
  (new-user-journey), 08 (hooks-elite), 10 (rig-self), 11
  (personal-rig) carried forward to a later release. The 0.3.4
  cut focused on recovery + resilience surfaces ahead of the
  onboarding journey.
- **Workspace symlink alignment**: daemon-side workspace-resolver
  alignment with operator symlinked workspace roots remains a
  follow-up; non-blocking for 0.3.4.
- **Slice-13 permission-block-routing-architecture remains held**:
  big-green-light gated by operator review; `rigx-experimental`
  only; not split-deferred (stays held).
- **0.3.4 host-upgrade flow held**: operators installing v0.3.4
  fresh from npm have full access immediately; upgrading an
  existing host follows the standard daemon-restart flow above.
  The named host-upgrade flow is held for separate sequencing.

## Verification Performed

- `npm run lint` clean.
- `npm run build` clean across all workspaces.
- TypeScript checks clean on every touched file at per-commit
  guard across every shipped slice.
- Per-slice focused-suite tests green:
  - Slice 01 (`rig start`): pod-aware id-grounded preview + apply
    (rev1 BLOCKING b4c6ada4); same-name disambiguation; `/api/up`
    never reached in the recovery path; `--last` / `--all` /
    `--rigs <names...>` headless paths.
  - Slice 02 (`rig up` resume-original-by-default): seat-level
    outcomes drive `resumed` / `fresh-primed` / `awaiting-
    decision`; per-seat TTY [y/N] prompt; headless explicit-hint
    path for `awaiting-decision`.
  - Slice 03 (`rig reconcile-session`): adopt a hand-resumed
    session with same node id; projection-drift reporting; never
    launches, never writes to the pane.
  - Slice 04 (`rig up --plan`): read-only restore preview; honest
    async timeout; no mutation; same five-term vocabulary on the
    per-node `intendedAction`.
  - Slice 05 rev1 (pod-aware Claude resume-selection menu):
    `ClaudeCodeAdapter.verifyResumeLaunch` returns
    `recovery: attention_required` with last-12-line evidence;
    zero numeric keystrokes sent.
  - Slice 06 (five-term vocabulary): `rig up` / `rig restore` /
    `rig ps` projections carry the named outcome on every
    representative seat-state path.
  - Slice 07 (Codex profile-v2 preflight): narrowed legacy
    detection regex; invalid-TOML stderr surfaces the parse
    reason and a TOML-validity hint (rev1 BLOCKING).
  - Slice 08 (cmux launch readiness): partial-workspace state
    surfaces honestly with the open-missing affordance; no
    silent launched-clean projection.
  - Slice 09 (periodic snapshots): `PeriodicSnapshotScheduler`
    captures + prunes by retention; `auto-periodic` vs
    `auto-pre-down` newest-wins in the restore selector;
    settings-store integration for the `snapshots.periodic.*`
    family.
  - Slice 10 (`rig seat clear-attention`): evidence-gated clear;
    operator-attestation override via `--reason`; audit row
    captures session / from-state / cleared-by.
  - Slice 11 (node-granular launch): single-seat
    `/api/rigs/:rigId/nodes/:nodeRef/launch`; subset
    `/api/rigs/:rigId/nodes/launch-subset`; partial outcomes
    (launched / held / alreadyRunning / failedTargets) never
    collapsed.
  - Slice 13 (slow Codex resume classification): slow-resume
    Codex path classifies through the five-term vocabulary and
    reaches `resumed` when the readiness probe confirms.
- Per-commit guard CLEAR across every shipped slice;
  velocity-qa adversarial dogfood + dual rev1 CLEAR on each
  merge.
- VM end-to-end suite green against the 0.3.4 cut; recovery
  paths (`rig start` + `rig up` resume-by-default +
  `rig reconcile-session` + `rig seat clear-attention`)
  exercised against a real macOS VM through the vm-e2e harness.
- Zero regressions versus the v0.3.3 base on every shipped
  slice.

## Commits Included (highlights)

The full v0.3.3 -> v0.3.4 delta is 67 commits / 69 files /
+7,193 insertions / -267 deletions. The list below groups
load-bearing commits by theme:

### Recovery Entry Points

- `feat(cli)`: `rig start` one-command recovery orchestrator —
  daemon-start, kernel wait, candidate listing, picker / flags,
  per-rig restore + reconcile (slice 01).
- `fix(cli,daemon)`: `rig start` id-grounded preview + apply —
  same-name rigs no longer hit `ambiguous_name` 409 (slice 01
  rev1 BLOCKING).
- `feat(cli)`: `rig reconcile-session` — adopt a live, hand-
  resumed canonical session into its persisted node without
  launch / relaunch / kill / startup-replay / resume-menu /
  pane-input (slice 03).

### Resume Original By Default

- `feat(cli,daemon)`: `rig up` resume-original-by-default;
  `--fresh <seats...>` becomes the per-seat opt-in for
  operation B; per-seat TTY [y/N] for `awaiting-decision`;
  headless explicit-hint path (slice 02).
- `feat(cli,daemon)`: `rig up --plan` read-only restore preview
  with honest async timeout (slice 04).

### Honest Restore Vocabulary

- `feat(daemon,cli)`: five-term restore status vocabulary across
  `rig up` / `rig restore` / `rig ps` — `resumed` /
  `fresh-primed` / `awaiting-decision` / `attention_required` /
  `failed` (slice 06).
- `fix(daemon)`: pod-aware Claude resume-selection menu surfaces
  `attention_required` instead of timeout (slice 05 rev1
  BLOCKING).
- `fix(daemon)`: slow Codex resume classification — slow but
  genuinely-resuming sessions no longer mis-categorize through
  the unresolved-gate branch (slice 13).

### Preflight + Readiness Honesty

- `fix(daemon)`: Codex profile-v2 preflight narrows legacy
  detection regex; invalid TOML surfaces parse reason + TOML-
  validity hint (slice 07 rev1 BLOCKING).
- `fix(daemon,ui)`: cmux launch readiness — partial workspace
  surfaces honestly; one-click open-missing affordance instead
  of silent launched-clean (slice 08).

### Crash-Insurance Floor

- `feat(daemon)`: `PeriodicSnapshotScheduler` + `snapshots.
  periodic` settings family; `auto-periodic` snapshot kind;
  restore selector treats `auto-periodic` and `auto-pre-down`
  symmetrically (newest-wins); last-snapshot / floor in
  `rig ps` (slice 09).

### Stuck-Seat Recovery

- `feat(cli,daemon)`: `rig seat clear-attention` — evidence-
  gated, operator-attested, audited reconcile of a stuck
  `attention_required` seat; audit row captures session / from-
  state / cleared-by (slice 10).

### Node-Granular Managed Partial Restore

- `feat(cli,daemon)`: node-granular launch through orchestration
  — `rig launch <rigId> <nodeRef>` single-seat;
  `rig launch <rigId> --seats <a,b>` subset; partial outcomes
  (launched / held / alreadyRunning / failedTargets) reported
  separately; retires `pod_aware_launch_unsupported` dead-end
  (slice 11).

See `CHANGELOG.md` for the agent-readable changelog with quick
verification commands and operator notes.

body.name: OpenRig v0.3.3 — Rig Archive/Unarchive + Add-Member + Honest Restore Gate + Send Sentinel + Whoami Peers Contract + For-You Manage-by-Exception + Workflow Instantiate By Name
body.body:
# OpenRig v0.3.3

## Summary

OpenRig v0.3.3 is a usability + honesty release. Two new top-level CLI
verbs land (`rig archive`/`rig unarchive` and `rig add`/`rig add-member`),
several long-standing paper cuts are retired (large-payload startup
delivery, dash-prefixed `send_text`, cmux 0.64.x compatibility, `rig down`
by name, golden-path discovery), and three honesty surfaces are tightened
to stop misclassifying ambiguous outcomes as success (`rig send --verify`
delivery outcomes, Codex restore gates, `rig whoami` peers contract). The
For-You feed gets a manage-by-exception pass (drill-to-terminal,
decision-band sort, one-click approve). Slice 13's deterministic
release-surface parser + skill-binding index ship as product code in
service of the auto-feature-rollout system.

One new migration in 0.3.3: `042_rig_archive`
(`ALTER TABLE rigs ADD COLUMN archived_at TEXT` + `idx_rigs_archived`).
Append-only, non-destructive, no rigs-row restructure. Existing v0.3.2
databases upgrade on first `rig daemon start`.

## Included In This Release

- **Large Startup-File Transport (slice 16)** — `TmuxAdapter.sendText`
  payloads over 100KB now travel via a per-call tmux buffer
  (`load-buffer` + `paste-buffer -d -r`) instead of being embedded in
  a single `send-keys -l` argv. Closes the >128KB silent-launch-fail
  class on Linux (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`) for large per-seat startup packs.
  `-r` preserves raw LF so multi-line packs do not early-submit on
  every newline; the single trailing C-m stays the caller's separate
  submit. Small payloads keep the exact inline `send-keys -l` command.
  Temp file + buffer cleanup on success AND paste-error paths; unique
  names per call so parallel `rig up` seats do not collide.
- **`send_text` Inline Dash Sentinel (slice 17)** — inline
  `tmux send-keys -t <t> -l <text>` now carries a `--` end-of-options
  sentinel so any startup payload whose content begins with `-`
  (notably `---` YAML frontmatter — the norm for per-seat packs) is
  not parsed by tmux as flags. The slice-16 large/buffer path is
  already immune (content travels via a file, never argv) and is
  untouched. Inert for non-dash content.
- **cmux 0.64.x Compatibility (slice 18)** — cmux 0.64.x renamed the
  surface identifier (`list-panels --json` rows carry `ref`, not
  `id`). The transport's `surface.list` normalizer remapped the array
  key but left row keys untouched, so `surface.sendText` silently
  failed under the new cmux line. Fixed via a `normalizeSurfaceRow`
  helper that resolves the handle from `ref ?? surface_ref ??
  surface_id ?? id`, normalizing every row regardless of array key.
  One resolution order serves both cmux 0.64.x and 0.63.x — no
  version-negotiation shim. Adaptation via the same pattern the code
  already uses for workspace rows and create/split handles.
- **`rig archive` Affordance (slice 19)** — new top-level commands
  `rig archive <rigId>` + `rig unarchive <rigId>`. Archive is
  non-destructive: rig row is preserved, `archived_at` is set, and a
  `rig.archived` event fires. Default reads exclude archived (no
  surprise listings); `rig ps --include-archived`, `?includeArchived=
  true`, and `?archived=only` opt them back in. The UI gains a lazy
  collapsible "Archive" section under the localhost host node, fed
  by a separate archived-only query. `rig up <name>` against an
  archived-only name is refused honestly with an error pointing at
  `rig unarchive` — no silent restore, no silent fall-through. The
  running/degraded archive guard surfaces a 3-part fact / consequence
  / action error and accepts `--force` to override. UI query
  invalidation consumes `rig.archived` / `rig.unarchived` events
  end-to-end so a CLI archive in one window reactively refreshes
  another mounted UI.
- **`rig add` / `rig add-member` (slice 24)** — new top-level command
  for the `add_member` converge op. Adds a member to an existing pod
  in a live rig from a YAML/JSON member fragment file. Built on the
  new converge spine (`Op` union + differ + `convergeOp`), with
  imperative CLI sugar over the converge interface (not a bypass).
  Daemon route `POST /api/rigs/:rigId/pods/:podNamespace/members`
  maps `AddMemberOutcome` codes to HTTP (404 / 409 / 400 / 201).
  MCP tool `rig_add` ships in lockstep. Edge validation tightened in
  the same slice: non-array `edges` is rejected (not silently
  dropped); edge kinds are validated against the canonical
  `VALID_EDGE_KINDS` set exported from `rigspec-schema.ts` and
  reused (not duplicated), so `rig add` edges share the existing
  graph contract.
- **`rig down` Accepts Name-or-Id (slice 22)** — the v0.2.0-era
  `rig down <name>` HTTP 404 caveat is gone. The resolver now fetches
  `/api/rigs/summary?includeArchived=true` and id-matches across ALL
  rigs (archived ids still reach teardown), then name-matches ACTIVE
  rigs only. Active+archived same-name pair resolves the active rig;
  archived-only name does not resolve by name. The packaged
  `openrig-user` skill (specs source + assets/plugins copy +
  `_canonical` mirror) and the `down.ts` resolver comment are
  corrected to reflect the real behavior. Historical CHANGELOG /
  v0.3.1 / v0.3.2 release notes are left intact — the bug genuinely
  existed at those releases.
- **Honest Codex Restore Gate (slice 21 FR-2)** — `verifyResumeLaunch`
  no longer returns `ok:true` unless the native-resume-probe proves
  the seat actually resumed. Unresolved operator-action gates (an
  update that cannot auto-dismiss, trust, model-selection) and a
  bounded poll that never reaches `resumed` now return `ok:false`
  with `recovery: attention_required` and last-12-line pane evidence,
  routed into the existing
  `HarnessLaunchResult` -> startup-orchestrator
  `startupStatus: attention_required` -> `ps`/`status` projection —
  no new state machinery. The working auto-dismiss path is preserved
  (a skippable update gate still auto-dismisses and continues to
  success); only UNRESOLVED gates fail loudly. Resolves the 04.3
  clean-VM `kernel_state bootstrap_failed` failure-mode the herder
  surfaced.
- **`rig send --verify` Honest Delivery Outcomes (slice 99.0.6.3)** —
  the prior `Verified: no` collapsed two materially different states
  into one: a message that LANDED (text pasted + Enter submitted,
  both succeeded) but whose post-send capture raced a TUI redraw,
  and a message that genuinely did not land. Careful agents paid a
  manual `rig capture` roundtrip on every send; careless agents read
  no as failure and double-sent. The three outcomes are now named in
  the response:
  - `delivered` — verified succeeded.
  - `rendered-unconfirmed` — text + Enter both succeeded but the
    capture could not re-confirm (redraw race, or capture threw).
    Landed-but-unconfirmable, NOT failure.
  - `failed` — the transport itself failed.
  The legacy `Verified: yes/no` line is preserved verbatim
  (parsers); a new `Delivery:` line carries the named outcome plus,
  for the middle case, a `rig capture <session>` confirmation
  pointer. `--json` carries the field through automatically.
- **`rig whoami` Peers Contract (slice 99.0.6.1)** — the `peers[]`
  field was readable as a directionally-edged subset or as host
  inventory; it is neither. The grounded contract is now stated
  in-band: `peers[]` is this rig's roster EXCLUDING self (built from
  `rig.nodes` with only a self-skip — no edge/status/binding
  filter), `edges{}` is the directional graph, and
  `rig ps --nodes` is the inventory including self + live state.
  Additive clarification only — no behavior or shape change.
  `WhoamiResult` gains a required `peersNote` field carrying the
  three pointers; the CLI Peers header keeps the literal `Peers:`
  prefix verbatim (shipped tests grep on it) and adds the in-band
  clarifier.
- **Workflow Instantiate By Name (slice 04.1)** — `rig workflow
  instantiate <built-in-name>` (e.g. `conveyor`, `basic-loop`)
  used to fail with `spec_file_missing` because instantiate fed the
  bare name straight to `WorkflowSpecCache.readThrough` (which
  treats its argument as a literal file path). Only a raw
  sourcePath worked — a hidden path that violated the
  fresh-operator goal: discovery advertised names you then could
  not use. `WorkflowRuntime.instantiate` now resolves the passed
  identifier against the seeded spec cache BY NAME first, falling
  back to literal-sourcePath only when no named spec matches. The
  cache returns the STORED path verbatim (no source-tree
  re-derivation), preserving the `dist/builtins` production layout.
- **Guided Golden Path State Clarity (slice 04.2)** — the
  new-operator golden path said `rig workflow list` shows the
  seeded built-ins, but `rig workflow list` lists workflow
  INSTANCES; the built-in / spec discovery surface is
  `rig workflow specs` (built-ins tagged `(built-in)`). A fresh
  operator following the ordered path before `workflow instantiate
  <name>` was sent to the wrong command. Corrected in
  `docs/reference/getting-started.md` and in the CLI's
  `goldenPathNextSteps()` step 4.
- **For-You Manage-By-Exception (slice 20)** — feed-interaction UX
  on existing signals only (the 0.4.0 attention-detection layer is
  untouched):
  - **Drill-to-terminal** — new `FeedCardTerminalDrill` opens the
    resolved source/author session's terminal PREVIEW directly
    from a card, by reusing `TerminalPreviewPopover` over
    `GET /api/sessions/:sessionName/preview`. Honest framing —
    "terminal preview" / "captured snapshot, not live", never
    claims live state; when no session resolves, the drill renders
    DISABLED with an honest title rather than an empty terminal.
  - **Decision-band sort** — a stable two-band partition lifts
    action-required + approval cards above progress / observation /
    shipped within the existing newest-first comparator. NOT a
    ranking engine (no scores, no card mutation). Applied at the
    single Feed merge-consumption seam.
  - **One-click approve (approve-only)** — `VerbActions` gains an
    additive `oneClickVerbs` prop. APPROVE submits directly on
    click; deny/route stay select+confirm. Defense in depth: the
    prop type narrows to `Extract<MissionControlVerb, "approve">`
    so misuse is a compile error, and a runtime
    `ONE_CLICK_SAFE_VERBS` allowlist rejects cast-forced
    `"deny"`/`"route"` at the call site. Reuses the same
    `performSubmit` mutation path (identical optimistic receipt
    and held-error behavior).
- **CLI Release-Surface Parser (slice 13.1)** — deterministic TypeScript
  Compiler API extractor that walks the Commander registrations in
  `packages/cli/src/commands/*.ts` at two git refs and emits a
  structured release-surface-diff of added commands, added flags, and
  removed/renamed surface. Resolves both Commander idioms (chained
  inline subcommands and factory indirection). Emits the
  REGISTRATION name (`rig-policy.ts` surfaces as `policy`); option
  name-tokens are taken from `.option()` arg[0] only, so
  template-literal descriptions never drop an option. Reads batched
  via one `git cat-file --batch` per ref (fast, offline,
  deterministic). 3-part honest failure shape; never a silent empty
  diff. Not registered as a `rig` verb at 0.3.3 (a separate decision)
  — the module is product code with hermetic test fixtures
  (including a v0.3.1..v0.3.2 worked example).
- **Skill <-> CLI-Surface Binding Index (slice 13.2)** — deterministic
  offline lookup that joins a release surface-diff to "which skills
  are affected by this release". Composes with the slice 13.1 parser;
  invocation-agnostic. Implements the ratified join grammar:
  component-wise prefix match in either direction (so `up` does not
  match `update`); conservative over-include bias for the
  no-false-negative floor. Drops `--version` from the binding index
  (the canonical grammar is command paths only, not global flags);
  the skill body still documents `rig --version` as prose. Ships
  with the v0.3.2-affected-skills regression fixture derived from
  the corpus.

## User-Facing Changes

### `rig archive` and `rig unarchive`

New top-level commands. Archive is non-destructive: the rig row is
preserved, an `archived_at` timestamp is set, and a `rig.archived`
event fires.

```
rig archive <rigId> [--force] [--json]
rig unarchive <rigId> [--json]
```

`rig unarchive` is always safe (no `--force`, no guard). `rig
archive` against a running or degraded rig surfaces a 3-part
fact / consequence / action error and accepts `--force` to
override.

Default reads exclude archived rigs:

```
rig ps [--include-archived]
GET /api/rigs/summary?includeArchived=true
GET /api/rigs/summary?archived=only
GET /api/ps?includeArchived=true
```

`rig ps` marks archived rows with `*` and renders a legend. The
`--include-archived` flag propagates through cross-host argv.

`rig up <name>` against an archived-only name is refused honestly
with an error pointing at `rig unarchive` (no silent restore, no
silent fall-through); `--json` form emits `rig_archived`.

UI surfaces a lazy collapsible "Archive" section under the
localhost host node. The section is fed by a separate archived-only
query (`useArchivedRigs`, `?archived=only`), not by client-side
filtering of the default list. `rig.archived` / `rig.unarchived`
events drive global query invalidation
(`["rigs","summary"]` + `["rigs","summary","archived"]` + `["ps"]`)
so a CLI archive reactively refreshes other mounted UIs.

### `rig add` and `rig add-member`

New top-level command for the `add_member` converge op. Adds a
member to an existing pod in a live rig from a YAML/JSON member
fragment file:

```
rig add <rigId> <podNamespace> <member-fragment-path> \
    [--json] [--rig-root <root>]
```

The member fragment tolerates a bare member or a `{ member }`
wrapper. Field names follow the spec snake_case shape (`id`,
`runtime`, `agent_ref`, `profile`, `cwd`, ...). Optional
pod-local `edges` (array of `{from, to, kind}`) is preserved
through to the converge op:

- Present-but-non-array `edges` is REJECTED (not silently dropped):
  CLI prints a clear error and exits 1 before POST; route returns
  400 `validation_failed`; domain also returns `validation_failed`
  as defense in depth.
- Edge `kind` is validated against the canonical `VALID_EDGE_KINDS`
  set exported from `rigspec-schema.ts` and reused (not duplicated).
  `kind: nonsense` returns 400 `validation_failed` naming the valid
  set; no edge is persisted.

Daemon route: `POST /api/rigs/:rigId/pods/:podNamespace/members`.
Outcome -> HTTP mapping: `rig_not_found` / `pod_not_found` -> 404;
`member_conflict` -> 409; `validation_failed` /
`preflight_failed` -> 400; success -> 201 (with per-node launch
status in the body). MCP tool `rig_add` ships in lockstep.

### `rig down` Accepts Name-or-Id

`rig down <name>` now works. The v0.2.0-era `rig down <name>` HTTP
404 caveat is gone.

```
rig down <rigId-or-name> [--delete] [--json]
```

Resolver semantics:

- `/api/rigs/summary?includeArchived=true` is fetched, then:
- id-match across ALL rigs (archived ids still reach teardown);
- name-match ACTIVE rigs only (`archivedAt == null`).

Same-name active+archived pair resolves the ACTIVE rig (not
ambiguous). Archived-only name does not resolve by name (use the
id, or `rig unarchive` first).

### Send Text Inline Dash Sentinel (slice 17)

The internal tmux `send_text` path now carries an explicit `--`
end-of-options sentinel before user-supplied content, so tmux no
longer parses content beginning with `-` or `--` as its own flag
arguments. Companion to the slice 16 large-payload transport fix:

```
rig send <session> "content with -- dashes or - hyphens"
```

delivers literally without the agent having to escape or work
around dash-prefixed leading characters (notably `---` YAML
frontmatter in per-seat startup payloads). This is a daemon-side
adapter fix in `packages/daemon/src/adapters/tmux.ts`; the
`rig send` CLI surface itself is unchanged.

### `rig send --verify` Delivery Outcomes

`--verify` responses now name the outcome explicitly:

- `delivered` — verified succeeded.
- `rendered-unconfirmed` — text + Enter both succeeded but the
  post-send capture could not re-confirm (TUI redraw race, or
  capture threw). The message LANDED; the render is not
  re-confirmable.
- `failed` — the transport itself failed.

The legacy `Verified: yes/no` line is preserved verbatim
(parsers); a new `Delivery:` line carries the named outcome plus,
for `rendered-unconfirmed`, a `rig capture <session>`
confirmation pointer. `--json` carries the `outcome` field
through.

`exit` codes: `delivered` and `rendered-unconfirmed` exit 0; the
middle is not dressed as success or failure. `failed` exits
non-zero with HTTP mapping unchanged. Mid-work / wait-for-idle
REFUSALS deliberately carry no outcome (nothing was sent; a
refusal is not a failed delivery).

### `rig whoami --json` Peers Contract

`peers[]` is this rig's roster EXCLUDING self. It is NOT a
directionally-edged subset, and it is NOT host inventory.

- For the directional graph, read `edges{}`.
- For the inventory including self + live state, use
  `rig ps --nodes`.

`WhoamiResult.peersNote` carries the contract in-band. The CLI
Peers header keeps the literal `Peers:` prefix verbatim (shipped
parsers grep on it) and adds the clarifier pointing at `edges`
and `rig ps --nodes`. `peers[]` name and shape are untouched;
this is an additive clarification only.

### Workflow Instantiate By Name

`rig workflow instantiate <name>` now resolves built-in names
end-to-end:

```
rig workflow instantiate <name-or-source-path> [--cwd <path>] [--json]
```

Built-in names (`conveyor`, `basic-loop`, ...) are resolved
against the seeded spec cache BY NAME first; literal source paths
remain a fallback for unmatched names (honest 404 if neither
matches). Closes the discovery / use divergence where
`rig workflow specs` advertised names that `rig workflow
instantiate` could not consume.

### Guided Golden Path Discovery Surface

The new-operator golden path now points at the correct discovery
verb:

- `rig workflow specs` lists built-in / seeded workflow specs
  (`(built-in)` tagged). USE THIS to discover names before
  `rig workflow instantiate <name>`.
- `rig workflow list` lists workflow INSTANCES (created from
  specs). Empty for a fresh operator.

Corrected in `docs/reference/getting-started.md` and in the
CLI's `setup` golden-path text.

### For-You Manage-By-Exception

Feed-interaction UX on existing signals (the 0.4.0
attention-detection layer is untouched):

- **Drill to terminal preview** — each card's footer carries a
  drill that opens the resolved source/author session's terminal
  PREVIEW via `GET /api/sessions/:sessionName/preview`. Labelled
  "terminal preview" / "captured snapshot, not live" — never
  claims live state. Disabled with an honest title when no
  session resolves.
- **Decision-band sort** — action-required + approval cards lift
  above progress / observation / shipped within the existing
  newest-first comparator. Stable two-band partition; not a
  ranking engine.
- **One-click approve** — APPROVE submits directly on click; deny
  and route stay select+confirm. Compile-time + runtime guards
  prevent the one-click path from being applied to non-approve
